title: AEF-Interrupt: dispersion-triggered mid-chunk preemption replacing SmolVLA's empty-queue replan gate
lenses: METHOD-TRANSFER lens: a multi-scopic primitive (P1-P7) that works in legged locomotion but is untried in VLA manipulation, ported as a FUNDAMENTAL change to a named SmolVLA component (inference-loop / tokenizer / action-expert flow head / training objective), verified on LIBERO with the user's existing SmolVLA+LeRobot harness and its ready-made flow-head dispersion signal.
primitive: P5 (AEF interrupt: a fast learned/threshold pathway that preempts the ongoing motor plan when an affordance change demands it), with P1 micro-clock framing (the dispersion monitor is the ~per-step reactive loop below the chunk loop).
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the inference-loop component: SmolVLAPolicy._check_get_actions_condition (and the queue-drain logic in select_action) — the open-loop chunk-commitment rule. Not a bolt-on: the policy's core act/replan decision rule is swapped, not augmented with a parallel module.
summary: Port P5 (the affordance-effectivity-fit interrupt that lets reactivity preempt deliberation) onto SmolVLA's chunk-execution gate. SmolVLA today refills its action chunk ONLY when the queue empties (_check_get_actions_condition returns len(queue)==0), so it runs a 50-step chunk fully open-loop. Replace that empty-only gate with a fast per-step monitor: each control step, cheaply re-sample K=4 candidate suffixes from the action expert (reusing the already-cached prefix KV, so no backbone re-run) and compute the harness's raw_dispersion over the REMAINING suffix; when dispersion crosses a conformally-calibrated threshold (the calib machinery already exists in uncertainty.py / ConformalActionUncertainty), ABORT the rest of the chunk and force an immediate full re-inference. This changes the inference-loop's replan trigger from time/queue-driven to content/uncertainty-driven.
hypothesis: Under mid-rollout disturbance, a dispersion-gated interrupt that preempts the open-loop chunk recovers more episodes (and recovers faster) than fixed open-loop chunking, because SmolVLA otherwise blindly executes a stale 50-step plan through the disturbance window.
mve_libero: Add a RobustVLA-style mid-episode perturbation to the LeRobot LIBERO env wrapper (teleport/nudge the target object, or inject an external force, at a fixed step t). Subclass SmolVLAPolicy to override _check_get_actions_condition: keep an EWMA of suffix dispersion (K=4 cheap suffix resamples on the cached prefix); fire replan when dispersion > tau. Compare vs unmodified SmolVLA on libero_spatial + libero_object (N=20 episodes each), reusing evaluate.py/lerobot-eval. Calibrate tau on 1 held-out task using existing conformal code. No training needed (inference-only).
expected_signal: Post-perturbation success delta (interrupt minus baseline) and recovery latency (steps from perturbation until task completes). Positive: interrupt recovers >=+10pp on perturbed episodes with <=5pp drop on clean episodes; baseline shows near-zero recovery because it executes the stale chunk. A null/negative result (LIBERO too quasi-static, interrupt thrashes) is itself a publishable finding about reactivity benchmarks.
contribution_type: method + new evaluation probe (mid-rollout perturbation on LIBERO)

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-TRUE, with a caveat. The proposal swaps the actual replan-decision rule of the inference loop: SmolVLAPolicy._check_get_actions_condition (modeling_smolvla.py:352-353) which currently returns `len(self._queues[ACTION]) == 0`, plus the queue-drain in select_action (lines 325-350). Changing WHEN the policy commits-vs-replans is a genuine change to the inference/execution method, not a parallel bolt-on module — the policy's core act/replan rule is replaced. That clears the "fundamental method" bar in spirit. The honest caveat: the *mechanism* doing the deciding (an uncertainty monitor on resampled chunks) is a small added monitor; it leaves the architecture, training objective, tokenizer, and flow head untouched. So it is a fundamental change to the *execution policy* but a relatively shallow one (inference-time control logic), and reviewers who define "fundamental" as architecture/training will read it as a sophisticated inference heuristic. I would not oversell it as architectural.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable but the perturbation MUST be built — vanilla LIBERO is too quasi-static to show a reactivity benefit. Suite: libero_spatial + libero_object, N=20 episodes each (matches existing evaluate.py / evaluate_checkpoint defaults). Baseline = unmodified SmolVLA (50-step open-loop, _check_get_actions_condition==queue-empty). Treatment = subclass overriding the gate to fire on dispersion>tau. Metric: post-perturbation success delta and recovery latency (steps from perturbation to completion). Perturbation: teleport/nudge the target object at fixed step t in the LIBERO env wrapper (this is exactly what ReViP arXiv:2601.16667 already does on LIBERO — "spatial perturbations to target object positions"). Positive = interrupt recovers >=+10pp on perturbed episodes with <=5pp clean-episode drop. CRITICAL GAPS that break the 2h pilot if not fixed: (1) the existing dispersion is computed by policy.reset()+K resamples on the SAME observation (uncertainty.py:137-143) — it measures the flow head's intrinsic sampling noise on a FIXED image, which is roughly constant step-to-step and does NOT spike when the world changes unless you feed a fresh image, which is a full backbone re-run. So the "cheap suffix resample on cached prefix" cannot detect the disturbance; the monitor must re-embed the current observation (defeating the "no backbone re-run" selling point) or use a different signal. (2) Must add a clean-vs-perturbed split and report per-step extra latency budget. (3) lerobot-eval is a subprocess (evaluate.py) returning only aggregated pc_success; you need a custom rollout loop to log recovery latency and to inject the override — evaluate.py as-is is insufficient.
anno.smolvla_fit: Component changed: SmolVLAPolicy._check_get_actions_condition + select_action queue logic (modeling_smolvla.py:325-353). Feasibility of the cheap-resample claim: the flow head (VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions, lines 826-881) DOES cache the prefix KV once (past_key_values, fill_kv_cache=True at line 836) and re-runs only the suffix per denoising step, so resampling chunks from a FIXED observation is genuinely cheap (no backbone re-run) — the harness already exploits this. BUT detecting a disturbance requires the prefix to reflect the NEW observation, and the prefix KV is built from the chunk-time image; refreshing it is a backbone pass. So the user's existing dispersion signal (raw_dispersion in uncertainty.py, ConformalActionUncertainty calibration) plugs in syntactically, but semantically it measures intrinsic flow-noise, not affordance-mismatch. The much bigger fit problem: this exact codebase ALREADY ships RTC (Real-Time Chunking, Physical Intelligence) — rtc_config, RTCProcessor, execution_horizon=10, prefix-attention inpainting (modeling_smolvla.py:257-271, 860-872; rollout/inference/rtc.py). RTC already does mid-execution chunk regeneration before the queue empties via inpainting. The candidate must position against the in-repo RTC baseline, not just vanilla 50-step open-loop, or a reviewer will ask "why not just turn on RTC / set execution_horizon shorter?"
prior_work: Bidirectional Decoding (Liu et al., Stanford, arXiv:2408.17355) — the canonical work bridging action chunking with closed-loop reactivity by sampling multiple candidates and selecting via backward-coherence/forward-contrast; directly subsumes 'resample K chunks and decide whether to commit'. THE reference to beat.

Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLAs (arXiv:2604.04161, 2026) — uses ACTION ENTROPY to dynamically adjust chunk length / replan frequency on VLAs (high uncertainty -> shorter chunk, more replanning). This is almost exactly the candidate's dispersion-triggered gate, already on VLAs, already recent. Largest novelty threat.

Real-Time Chunking / RTC (Physical Intelligence, Black et al. 2025) — ALREADY IMPLEMENTED in the user's own LeRobot dep (policies/rtc/, execution_horizon, prefix-attention inpainting). Mid-execution replan before queue-empty is solved here without an uncertainty trigger.

Leave No Observation Behind / A2C2 (arXiv:2509.23224) — lightweight per-control-step correction head for chunk reactivity under delay; competing solution to the same 'stale open-loop chunk' problem, with LIBERO delay/horizon experiments.
ReViP (arXiv:2601.16667) — already introduces LIBERO spatial perturbations to target-object positions and a replanning evaluation, i.e. the candidate's proposed 'new evaluation probe' largely exists.

Failure Prediction at Runtime for Generative Robot Policies (arXiv:2510.09459) and ReconVLA (arXiv:2604.16677, uncertainty-guided failure-aware VLA) — runtime uncertainty monitors on generative policies.
anno.so_what: The motivating fact is real and clean (SmolVLA default n_action_steps=chunk_size=50, so it truly executes a 50-step open-loop chunk; confirmed in configuration_smolvla.py:29-30). A working dispersion-gated interrupt would matter for delay/disturbance robustness, and even a NULL result ("LIBERO is too quasi-static for reactivity gating; the interrupt thrashes or never fires meaningfully") is a publishable benchmark-critique finding. The problem is the so-what is heavily pre-empted: the action-chunk reactivity gap, uncertainty/entropy-triggered replanning, and LIBERO perturbation probes are all already published (2408.17355, 2604.04161, 2509.23224, 2601.16667). The contribution narrows to 'use the SmolVLA flow-head DISPERSION specifically, conformally calibrated, as the trigger' — an incremental delta over entropy-triggered adaptive chunking, not a new capability.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The dispersion signal cannot do what the hypothesis needs. raw_dispersion (uncertainty.py:31-47, used at lines 137-143) is the std across K flow-head samples on a FIXED observation — it measures the flow head's intrinsic stochasticity, which is approximately stationary over a rollout and does NOT spike when the target object is teleported, because the cached prefix KV (and the candidate's whole 'cheap, no-backbone-rerun' premise) still encodes the OLD image. To make dispersion respond to the disturbance you must re-embed the current frame = a full backbone pass every step, which destroys the efficiency rationale and just becomes 'replan every step' (i.e., n_action_steps=1, the trivial closed-loop baseline). So the central claim — a cheap suffix-resample that detects affordance change and preempts — is internally inconsistent. Secondary objection: RTC is already in the repo and already solves mid-chunk replanning; the candidate must beat RTC, not vanilla open-loop, to be interesting.
anno.effort_note: Days, NOT hours; see above. Pilot eval fits the GPU budget but the harness build (perturbation wrapper + latency-logging rollout + a trigger that responds to observation change) is the real cost.

title: Three-Clock SmolVLA: micro/meso/macro inference with intention-gated backbone re-encode
lenses: METHOD-TRANSFER lens: a multi-scopic primitive (P1-P7) that works in legged locomotion but is untried in VLA manipulation, ported as a FUNDAMENTAL change to a named SmolVLA component (inference-loop / tokenizer / action-expert flow head / training objective), verified on LIBERO with the user's existing SmolVLA+LeRobot harness and its ready-made flow-head dispersion signal.
primitive: P1 (three clocks, each with its own rate) + P2 (bottom-up adaptability vs top-down optimality reconciled at the meso clock).
fundamental_method_change: Restructures the inference-loop: splits the single _get_action_chunk / sample_actions path into a cheap meso re-decode (reuse cached past_key_values) vs an expensive macro re-encode (recompute prefix KV), with separate clock rates. The monolithic 'one backbone pass per chunk' contract is replaced.
summary: Port P1 (three independently-clocked loops) and P2 (bottom-up/top-down reconciled at the meso level) onto SmolVLA's inference loop. SmolVLA already structurally separates a slow prefix-KV-cache pass (the SmolVLM2 backbone, computed once in sample_actions) from the fast denoise loop (action expert). Formalize THREE clocks: MICRO = per-step queue drain + cheap dispersion monitor; MESO = action-expert re-decode reusing the FROZEN cached prefix KV (cheap, no backbone) fired when running dispersion rises; MACRO = full embed_prefix + backbone KV recompute fired ONLY on sustained dispersion or language-intent change. The meso loop is the meet-in-the-middle: rising bottom-up dispersion shortens the meso period (re-decode more) while a stable top-down language prefix is reused, and only persistent disagreement escalates to macro. This makes 'when to re-run the heavy backbone' a function of self-disagreement instead of queue exhaustion.
hypothesis: Decoupling cheap action-expert re-decodes (meso, prefix-cache reuse) from expensive backbone re-encodes (macro, on intention/dispersion change) gives equal-or-better LIBERO success at materially fewer backbone forward passes than fixed-horizon chunking, because most steps need only a fresh action sample, not fresh perception.
mve_libero: Subclass SmolVLAPolicy: persist past_key_values from the last sample_actions; add a meso path that re-runs only the denoise loop on the cached prefix when dispersion is moderate, and a macro path that recomputes embed_prefix+KV only when dispersion stays high for M steps. Instrument a backbone-call counter. Evaluate on libero_spatial/object (N=20) for success and backbone-calls-per-episode vs stock SmolVLA. Inference-only; no retraining.
expected_signal: Two-axis result: success (pp vs baseline) and mean backbone forward passes per episode. Positive: success within +-2pp of baseline at >=30% fewer backbone calls (mirrors the locomotion paper's ~70% compute-reduction claim, scaled to manipulation). Counts as a clear contribution even if success is flat, because the compute reduction is the so-what.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Genuinely changes a core VLA INFERENCE method, not a bolt-on. It restructures SmolVLA's action-generation contract: the monolithic "embed_prefix + backbone KV-fill + full denoise, once per chunk-exhaustion" path (verified in sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py: sample_actions L812-881 does fill_kv_cache=True then loops denoise_step at fill_kv_cache=False) is split into (a) a CHEAP meso re-decode that reuses persisted past_key_values and re-runs only denoise_step, and (b) an EXPENSIVE macro re-encode that recomputes embed_prefix + backbone KV. The trigger for the heavy path becomes self-disagreement (dispersion) rather than queue exhaustion (_check_get_actions_condition, L352-353). That replaces the open-loop chunk-execution + fixed perception cadence, a fundamental control of the inference loop. CAVEAT: it does NOT touch architecture weights, tokenization, or the training objective; inference-time only. Honest framing: it is a fundamental change to the inference SCHEDULE, the lightest of the three "fundamental" categories.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suites: libero_spatial + libero_object, N=20 each (~280-step caps per .deps/.../envs/libero.py L99-100). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLAPolicy (lerobot/smolvla_base, RTC disabled). Treatment = subclass overriding select_action to persist past_key_values and run the three-clock schedule. Two-axis metric: (1) pc_success via eval_info.json (existing evaluate.py parser), (2) backbone-forward counter incremented only on macro re-encode. Positive = success within +-2pp of baseline at >=30% fewer backbone calls. CRITICAL FLAW to fix first: vanilla SmolVLA already uses n_action_steps=50=chunk_size (configuration_smolvla.py L29-30), so it ALREADY runs the backbone only ~6x per 280-step episode -- there is almost NO backbone-call headroom vs the true default. The experiment is meaningful only if the baseline is reset to SMALL n_action_steps (e.g. 5-10, the regime where backbone cost bites) and the three-clock variant must MATCH that reactivity at fewer passes; state this or the efficiency result is vacuous. Reactivity/perturbation arm (needed for the P5 spirit): inject a mid-episode disturbance (randomize an object pose at a fixed step, or add a held-out distractor) and show macro re-encodes spike at the perturbation while meso re-decodes dominate steady state. Without a perturbation the "dispersion shortens the meso period" claim is untested.
anno.smolvla_fit: Lands on SmolVLAFlowMatching.sample_actions / denoise_step (modeling_smolvla.py L812-916) and SmolVLAPolicy.select_action / _get_action_chunk / _check_get_actions_condition (L324-353). Concretely: (1) persist past_key_values from the L836 vlm_with_expert.forward(fill_kv_cache=True) onto the policy; (2) add a meso path running only the denoise loop (L848-876) against the cached prefix; (3) add a macro path that recomputes embed_prefix+KV. use_cache defaults True (configuration_smolvla.py L66), so KV reuse is wired. The existing dispersion signal HELPS as the gating cue (raw_dispersion in conformal_active/uncertainty.py L31-47 is std-across-K-chunks), BUT a mismatch: today dispersion is computed by full resampling via repeated predict_action_chunk + policy.reset() (policy_runner.py L137-143) = K FULL backbone passes, the opposite of cheap. The point requires re-deriving dispersion from K cheap meso re-decodes on the cached prefix (multiple noise seeds through denoise_step only). That re-plumb is the real implementation cost and is not free.
prior_work: StreamVLA (arXiv:2602.01100): dual-system slow-think/fast-act on a SHARED backbone; during steady execution high-level intents are LOCKED to condition a flow-matching action head, bypassing the expensive backbone for 72% of timesteps via completion-state gating; 98.5% on LIBERO, 48% latency reduction. Essentially the candidate's exact thesis (gate the heavy backbone, reuse cached context, drive a flow head fast) already validated on LIBERO -- strongest threat.

FAVLA (arXiv:2602.23648): fast-slow VLA where the slow VLM backbone produces a REUSABLE KV cache for a small fast action expert running at a DIFFERENT FREQUENCY, flow-matching actions. Directly anticipates the meso/macro KV-reuse-at-different-clock-rates split.

Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time (arXiv:2604.04161): action entropy/uncertainty adaptively shrinks chunk size and replans when within-chunk variance is high, training-free, reports LIBERO gains. Anticipates 'rising dispersion -> re-decode more often.'
SCALE: Self-uncertainty Conditioned Adaptive Looking and Execution for VLA (arXiv:2602.04208): title paraphrases the candidate -- self-uncertainty gates when to 'look' (re-perceive) vs 'execute.'

VLA-Cache (arXiv:2502.02175): training-free adaptive KV-cache reuse across frames (reuse static-token KV, recompute active ones) to cut backbone compute on LIBERO/OpenVLA -- overlaps the reuse-vs-recompute axis.

In-repo RTC / Real-Time Chunking (Physical Intelligence; .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/rtc/configuration_rtc.py, execution_horizon=10): already ships latency-aware chunk replanning via inpainting in THIS codebase -- the baseline reviewers will demand a comparison against.
anno.so_what: If positive, the deliverable is a two-axis Pareto point: equal LIBERO success at materially fewer backbone forward passes, mirroring the locomotion paper's compute-reduction claim. Honest weight: the 'compute saved' so-what is the same headline StreamVLA (72% bypass), FAVLA, and VLA-Cache already claimed, so a flat-success/-30%-backbone result on SmolVLA reads as replication, not a new contribution. It MATTERS only if it adds something they lack: (a) the specific dispersion-of-the-flow-head gate (vs entropy / completion-classifier) shown to be a better trigger, (b) the explicit THREE-tier (micro/meso/macro) decomposition with a measured meso tier that two-tier fast/slow papers lack, or (c) a clean negative result showing dispersion is a poor recompute trigger on SmolVLA. Without one of those, the so-what is weak.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The efficiency axis may have no headroom and the success axis may be a wash, making the result vacuous. Vanilla SmolVLA already runs the backbone only ~once per 50 steps, so against the true default there is nothing to save -- the candidate must redefine the baseline to small chunks to manufacture savings, at which point a reviewer asks 'why not just use RTC, which already ships here and solves exactly this?'. Worse, the meso re-decode reuses a STALE prefix KV from an OLD observation; over many meso steps the robot has moved, so cached perception is wrong -- this is exactly why open-loop chunking exists and why RTC does inpainting rather than blind cache reuse. Reusing a frozen prefix while the world changes risks success DROPS, not parity. The gate is also circular: dispersion is meant to be computed from meso re-decodes, but if the prefix is stale the dispersion measures disagreement under wrong perception, so it may fail to fire exactly when re-perception is most needed. Strongest single objection: StreamVLA already did fast/slow backbone-gating on LIBERO with a flow head (98.5% + 72% bypass) -- the candidate must beat or clearly differentiate from it, not rediscover it.
anno.effort_note: Weeks, more than the proposal implies. The eval harness shells out to lerobot-eval as a subprocess (evaluate.py L66-84) and the rollout loop is in .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/rollout/inference/sync.py calling policy.select_action -- so the three-clock logic must live in a SmolVLAPolicy subclass that lerobot-eval can load, with past_key_values persisted across select_action calls (today local to sample_actions). The cheap-meso-dispersion re-plumb (K denoise-only passes on the cached prefix) is net-new code, not reuse of policy_runner.py's full-resample path. Realistic 2-hour pilot: ONE suite (libero_spatial), N=10, fixed thresholds, success + backbone-counter only, NO perturbation arm. Full claim (two suites, perturbation/reactivity arm, RTC baseline, threshold sweep) is multi-day GPU+dev. Recommended cut: first run a 1-hour 'headroom probe' logging backbone-calls/episode for vanilla SmolVLA at n_action_steps in {5,10,25,50} to confirm a regime worth optimizing BEFORE building the machinery.

title: Dispersion-adaptive flow budget: per-step num_steps and expert-depth allocation in the action expert
lenses: METHOD-TRANSFER lens: a multi-scopic primitive (P1-P7) that works in legged locomotion but is untried in VLA manipulation, ported as a FUNDAMENTAL change to a named SmolVLA component (inference-loop / tokenizer / action-expert flow head / training objective), verified on LIBERO with the user's existing SmolVLA+LeRobot harness and its ready-made flow-head dispersion signal.
primitive: P3 (dynamic-density compute allocation with strength feedback: more denoising where uncertain, less where confident).
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the action-expert / flow-head inference component: the fixed num_steps integration loop inside VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions becomes a dispersion-gated adaptive-step loop (and optional adaptive expert depth). The denoising compute schedule itself is changed, not wrapped.
summary: Port P3 (attention = adaptive compute density; spend representational/compute density where the scene is information-rich, sparse elsewhere) onto SmolVLA's flow-matching integration budget. Today sample_actions runs a FIXED num_steps=10 Euler integration steps for every observation regardless of difficulty. Make the integration budget a function of the flow head's own self-disagreement: take 1-2 coarse denoise steps, measure dispersion across a couple of cheap parallel noise draws on the same cached prefix, then spend MANY more integration steps (and optionally route the suffix through more action-expert layers) only when dispersion is high, and early-exit when it is low. This turns the fixed integration loop into a difficulty-adaptive compute controller driven by the ready-made dispersion signal.
hypothesis: Most LIBERO frames are easy and converge in <10 flow steps; spending the saved compute only on high-dispersion frames preserves success while cutting mean flow-integration steps, demonstrating attention-as-adaptive-compute in the action-generation pathway rather than the visual front-end.
mve_libero: Patch sample_actions to (a) run an adaptive number of denoise steps gated by an inter-sample dispersion estimate (K=2-3 noise draws sharing the prefix KV), with min/max step caps. Log per-frame steps taken. Evaluate libero_spatial/object (N=20) for success vs stock (num_steps=10) and mean steps/frame. Inference-only; <=2 GPU-hours per pilot since eval cost is dominated by the env rollouts, not the extra cheap denoise draws.
expected_signal: Success vs mean-flow-steps trade curve. Positive: success within +-2pp of the 10-step baseline at >=35% fewer mean integration steps, with a visible correlation between allocated steps and (held-out) frame difficulty. Negative result (uniform difficulty -> no savings) still informs whether LIBERO has exploitable compute heterogeneity.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-but-yes. The change is INSIDE VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:844-876): the fixed Euler loop `num_steps = self.config.num_steps; for step in range(num_steps): ... x_t += dt*v_t` becomes a dispersion-gated adaptive-step loop with min/max caps and early-exit. This replaces the policy's inference-time generative compute schedule itself, not a wrapper around it — the denoise loop is the action expert's core inference component, so it qualifies as changing a fundamental VLA inference method (per the mandate's option (c)/(a)). HONEST CAVEAT: the OPTIONAL "route the suffix through more action-expert layers" part IS effectively a bolt-on / would need retraining (the pretrained expert has a fixed depth; you cannot validly skip/add layers at inference without consistency training), so that sub-claim should be dropped or flagged. The defensible, fundamental change is the adaptive integration-step count only. If reduced to merely "lower num_steps when a heuristic fires" with no architectural touch, it slides toward a config-knob tweak rather than a method change — the fundamental-ness rests on the loop being rewritten with an inter-sample convergence criterion, which is a real algorithmic modification of the sampler.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_spatial + libero_object, N=20 episodes/task (matches the user's existing N=20 sweep harness). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA with stock num_steps=10 (the lerobot/smolvla_base default, confirmed in config). Metric: (a) task success rate, (b) mean flow-integration steps/frame (the efficiency axis), (c) correlation between allocated steps and a held-out frame-difficulty proxy. Implementation: patch sample_actions to run K=2-3 cheap noise draws sharing the already-computed past_key_values (line 836 caches the prefix ONCE, so extra draws are near-free — verified), take 1-2 coarse steps, measure inter-draw std (the dispersion signal), then continue integrating only while std > threshold up to max_steps, early-exit below it. Log per-frame steps. POSITIVE = success within +-2pp of the 10-step baseline at >=35% fewer mean integration steps, with visible step-vs-difficulty correlation. This is INFERENCE-ONLY (no retrain), so a pilot fits the 2-GPU-hour budget since cost is dominated by env rollouts, not the cheap extra draws. CRITICAL GAP for the reactivity framing: the candidate's P3 'attention-as-compute' claim is verified by the success/steps trade curve and does NOT require a perturbation. But if the proposal is ever upsold as 'reactivity' (P5), that WOULD need a named perturbation (e.g. mid-episode object displacement / camera jitter injected into the LIBERO obs) and is currently absent — flag it as out-of-scope for this MVE.
anno.smolvla_fit: Exact component: VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions in .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py (lines 812-881). The Euler loop and num_steps live there; the KV cache (past_key_values) is built once at line 836 before the loop, which is precisely what makes K parallel noise draws on a shared prefix cheap — the mechanism is well-matched to the architecture. The user's dispersion signal (raw_dispersion in conformal_active/uncertainty.py, mean per-(step,dim) std across K chunks) helps CONCEPTUALLY and as reusable code, but note an important mismatch: today raw_dispersion is computed across K FULLY-DENOISED chunks (each a complete 10-step sample) for OFFLINE per-episode active-learning data selection (n_action_samples=8, frame_stride=8). The idea needs dispersion computed across K PARTIALLY-denoised draws at an intermediate timestep, inside the loop, online. That is a new code path, not a drop-in reuse — but the existing function shows the team already knows how to sample K chunks and reduce to a scalar, so the lift is small.
prior_work: D3P: Dynamic Denoising Diffusion Policy via Reinforcement Learning (arXiv 2508.06804) — NEAREST PRIOR ART. Adaptively allocates denoising steps per action at test time via a lightweight state-aware adaptor, explicitly motivated by 'crucial vs routine actions', 2.2x speedup at comparable performance. Differs from candidate only in the GATE: D3P learns the stride via PPO (needs RL training); candidate uses a training-free inter-sample self-disagreement criterion. This is the main novelty threat — the high-level claim 'adaptive denoising steps for robot policies' is already published.

CEED-VLA / Inter-Layer Truncated Flow Matching with warm-start denoising (arXiv 2506.13725) and AC2-VLA (arXiv 2601.19634, 'unified router allocating computation across spatial/depth/temporal') — adaptive VLA action-head/flow compute; AC2-VLA's router subsumes the candidate's 'adaptive expert depth' sub-idea, reinforcing that the optional layer-routing part is not novel.

DeeR-VLA — early-exit in the VLA LLM by comparing adjacent-exit output CONSISTENCY to terminate inference; the consistency-as-stopping-criterion idea overlaps the candidate's dispersion-as-stopping idea, though DeeR applies it to the backbone, not the flow head.

Adaptive Guidance (arXiv 2312.12487) and shortcut/consistency flow models (ManiFlow 2509.01819, One-Step Shortcut 2410.12557) — training-free omission of later denoising steps based on convergence; establishes 'later flow steps are often redundant' as known, weakening the surprise of the efficiency result.

Act, Think or Abstain (arXiv 2603.05147) — builds adaptive inference ON TOP OF SmolVLA via a VLM-embedding router; demonstrates the exact substrate is already being used for adaptive inference, so the SmolVLA+adaptive-compute framing alone is not novel.
anno.so_what: Clear and modest. Positive result: demonstrates that the flow head's OWN self-disagreement is a training-free, signal-free-of-extra-training controller for inference compute, matching success at >=35% fewer steps — a deployable speedup with zero retraining, which is the practical edge over D3P's RL adaptor. Negative result is ALSO informative and cheaply obtained: if LIBERO frames are uniformly easy/hard (no exploitable heterogeneity), you learn the difficulty distribution of a standard benchmark, which informs whether adaptive-compute methods can win there at all. The contribution matters either way, but it is an EFFICIENCY/MECHANISM result, not a capability result — it will not improve success rate, only the compute-success frontier, so the 'so what' ceiling is bounded by 'faster, not better'.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection (two-pronged): (1) NOVELTY. D3P already published 'adaptive denoising steps per action for robot policies, crucial-vs-routine, 2.2x speedup'. The candidate's ONLY differentiator is the gate being training-free self-disagreement instead of a learned RL stride. A reviewer will ask: is 'training-free dispersion gate' enough of a delta, and does it actually beat a trivial fixed-step baseline (e.g. just set num_steps=6)? If a static num_steps=6 already matches success at 40% fewer steps — which is plausible given flow policies are known to tolerate few steps — then the WHOLE adaptive machinery is unjustified, because the win came from 'LIBERO needs fewer than 10 steps', not from per-frame adaptivity. The MVE MUST include the static-low-step baseline (num_steps in {4,6,8}) or the result is uninterpretable. (2) SIGNAL VALIDITY: inter-sample std at an EARLY/coarse timestep may be dominated by the injected noise scale rather than genuine task difficulty, so the gate could fire on noise magnitude, not on affordance-mismatch — collapsing the elegant P3 story into a noise-variance thermostat. There is no evidence yet that early-timestep dispersion correlates with per-frame difficulty on LIBERO.
anno.effort_note: Days, low risk, as claimed — IF scoped to adaptive STEP COUNT only (drop adaptive-expert-depth, which needs retraining). The sample_actions patch is ~30-50 lines; KV cache already shared so K extra coarse draws are cheap; user already has the dispersion primitive and an N=20 LIBERO sweep harness. Real cost is the ablation set for interpretability (static num_steps in {4,6,8,10} baselines + step-vs-difficulty correlation), not the core implementation; add ~1 day. Inference-only, fits 2-GPU-hr pilots.

title: AEF-density tokenizer: affordance/dispersion-weighted visual token routing replacing uniform SigLIP patches
lenses: METHOD-TRANSFER lens: a multi-scopic primitive (P1-P7) that works in legged locomotion but is untried in VLA manipulation, ported as a FUNDAMENTAL change to a named SmolVLA component (inference-loop / tokenizer / action-expert flow head / training objective), verified on LIBERO with the user's existing SmolVLA+LeRobot harness and its ready-made flow-head dispersion signal.
primitive: P3 (representational density where the scene is information-rich) fused with P4/P6 (affordance-centric, embodiment-relative perception) and P7 (compact/topological token set over dense uniform patches).
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the tokenizer component: VLAFlowMatching.embed_prefix's uniform image-token construction (embed_image -> concatenate all patches) becomes affordance-density token selection/merging before the backbone. The model's perceptual input representation is changed.
summary: Port P3+P4 (adaptive-density attention + affordance-centric, body-relative perception) onto SmolVLA's visual tokenizer. embed_prefix currently feeds ALL uniform SigLIP patch tokens from embed_image into the backbone at uniform density. Replace this with a token-routing front-end: score each patch token by an affordance-effectivity-fit proxy (cheap signal = per-patch action-relevance derived from where action-expert cross-attention concentrates, optionally distilled into a tiny learned head), keep/super-resolve high-AEF patches near graspable/contact regions and merge/drop background patches, conditioned on the gripper/proprioceptive state (embodiment-relative). This is the visual-tokenization branch of the fundamental-change mandate, generalizing geometric ROI-foveation to a learned, body-relative affordance prior.
hypothesis: Concentrating token density on affordance-relevant, gripper-relative regions and sparsifying background preserves LIBERO success at fewer visual tokens (lower backbone cost), and is more robust to object displacement than uniform layout-memorizing patches, attacking the documented LIBERO-PRO memorization failure mode.
mve_libero: Implement training-free patch scoring first: derive per-patch keep scores from action-expert->vision cross-attention (cross_attn mode is on) with a temporal EMA, drop the lowest-scoring fraction in embed_prefix, re-pad to prefix_length. Evaluate libero_spatial/object (N=20) at several keep-ratios for the success-vs-token-count curve. Optional 1-round LoRA (4000 steps, fits budget) if training-free pruning hurts. Robustness check: re-eval under object-reposition perturbation.
expected_signal: Success vs visual-token-count curve, plus success delta under object-displacement perturbation. Positive: >=50% token reduction at <=3pp success loss on clean, AND smaller displacement-induced drop than uniform tokenization. The displacement-robustness delta is the distinctive so-what (affordance vs memorized layout).

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Genuinely changes a core VLA method: the perceptual input REPRESENTATION. embed_prefix (modeling_smolvla.py:637-729) currently concatenates ALL ~64 connector-resampled image tokens per camera at uniform density before the SmolVLM backbone; selecting/merging/super-resolving tokens by an affordance score alters the token set the transformer consumes. That is representation-level, not a bolt-on. CAVEAT: as written, the proposed training-free MVE (EMA over decode attention, drop lowest fraction, re-pad) is closer to a bolt-on pruning front-end than a true architectural change. To be a fundamental change rather than an inference accelerator, it must do something the pruning literature does NOT already do (learned body-relative super-resolution / token-merging, or a trained selection head changing the representation) — otherwise it collapses into existing VLA token-pruning work and should be flagged as an add-on.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA (lerobot/smolvla_base) all tokens. Suites: libero_spatial + libero_object (N=20), per-suite success rate; secondary = visual-token count / backbone latency. Primary curve: success vs kept-token fraction at e.g. 75/50/25%. Clean-positive: >=50% token reduction at <=3pp success loss. The DISTINCTIVE claim (affordance vs memorized layout) needs a NAMED perturbation, not a vague reactivity claim: use LIBERO-PRO / LIBERO-Plus object-displacement and background-texture perturbations (arXiv 2510.03827 / 2510.13626). Robustness-positive: affordance-routed tokens show a SMALLER displacement-induced success drop than uniform tokens at matched token budget. Note both vanilla SmolVLA and the pruned variant may collapse toward ~0% under LIBERO-PRO displacement (documented effect), which would make the robustness delta hard to measure and is the real risk to the headline so-what. The token-vs-success curve fits the 2h/single-GPU budget; LoRA at 4000 steps is plausible but eval-only training-free is the safe pilot.
anno.smolvla_fit: Component: VLAFlowMatching.embed_prefix in modeling_smolvla.py (image-token construction) plus the per-image embed_image path in smolvlm_with_expert.py:191. IMPORTANT MISMATCHES with the proposal: (1) tokens are produced by a pixel-shuffle CONNECTOR (smolvlm_with_expert.py:203) to a FIXED ~64 tokens/image, so this prunes resampled tokens, not raw SigLIP patches; "super-resolve patches" is not free in this resampler design. (2) Default attention_mode='cross_attn' but self_attn_every_n_layers=2, so it is a HYBRID; the prefix is processed by self-attention and the action expert cross-attends to it. (3) The cheap signal is NOT free: eager_attention_forward (smolvlm_with_expert.py:516-561) computes softmax probs internally and returns ONLY att_output — per-patch action->vision weights are discarded. Extracting them requires patching the attention forward to return/aggregate probs over expert query rows. (4) The user's existing dispersion signal does NOT help here: it is an action-OUTPUT-space scalar (std across K sampled action chunks, policy_runner.py:133-143), with no spatial/per-patch localization; mapping it to token importance needs a separate attribution mechanism. The proposal's framing that dispersion is a ready-made per-patch affordance score is incorrect for this harness.
prior_work: VLA-Pruner (arXiv 2511.16449): dual-level criterion = VL-prefill attention (semantic) + action-decode attention (action relevance), with a TEMPORAL SMOOTHER on decode attention because action->vision attention is unavailable at prefill. This is essentially identical to the candidate's 'score patches by action-expert cross-attention with temporal EMA' MVE.

LightVLA (arXiv 2509.12594): differentiable token pruning with learned dynamic queries + Gumbel-softmax selection; 78 avg tokens, 97.4% LIBERO, +2.9% success while cutting FLOPs/latency. Covers the 'optional LoRA learned selection head' branch.

ThinkProprio / 'Think Proprioceptively' (arXiv 2602.06575): injects proprioception into the VLM embedding space specifically to shape WHICH visual tokens are attended, suppressing redundant tokens, >50% latency cut on LIBERO/CALVIN. Directly pre-empts the candidate's 'embodiment/gripper-state-conditioned' distinctive angle.

ROI-Driven Foveated Attention for VLA (arXiv 2603.20668): the geometric-foveation-to-learned generalization the candidate explicitly names as its framing. 'See What Matters: Differentiable Grid Sample Pruning' (arXiv 2605.11817) and SpecPrune-VLA / VLA-IAP / DTP are further training-free or differentiable VLA token-pruning entries.

LIBERO-PRO (arXiv 2510.03827) and LIBERO-Plus (arXiv 2510.13626): the memorization/displacement-robustness benchmarks the candidate would use; they own the 'positional bias vs semantic understanding' framing the candidate claims as its so-what.
anno.so_what: The efficiency so-what (success-vs-token-count curve) is ALREADY established and beaten by VLA-Pruner/LightVLA/ThinkProprio on LIBERO, so a positive efficiency result is not publishable on its own. The only potentially novel and worthwhile so-what is the DISPLACEMENT-ROBUSTNESS DELTA: does affordance/body-relative token routing degrade less under object reposition (LIBERO-PRO) than uniform tokens at matched budget — i.e., does adaptive density attack the memorization failure mode rather than just speed? If yes, that is a real contribution (efficiency methods also improve OOD robustness). If no (or both collapse to 0%), it is a negative result that is still mildly informative but weak. The contribution hinges entirely on the robustness delta being measurable and attributable, which is the shakiest part.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: the proposed MVE is a near-reimplementation of VLA-Pruner (decode/action attention + temporal EMA + drop low-score tokens), and the two claimed differentiators are each independently pre-empted — embodiment-conditioning by ThinkProprio, the displacement-robustness framing by LIBERO-PRO. So the idea is at high risk of being 'an efficiency add-on we already have, re-run on a smaller backbone.' Compounding this: (a) SmolVLA already aggressively compresses to ~64 tokens/image via the connector and uses only early VLM layers, so the headroom for 'free' token reduction is far smaller than on OpenVLA-class models where these papers got their wins — a 50% cut may show little latency benefit and quick accuracy loss; (b) the 'cheap, training-free, for-free' signal is not free (attention weights are discarded; must patch attention); (c) the distinctive robustness delta may be unmeasurable because vanilla SmolVLA already collapses toward 0% under LIBERO-PRO displacement. To survive review the work would need to abandon the pruning framing and demonstrate something pruning papers do not: learned body-relative density that provably improves displacement robustness at matched budget — and even then it must out-position VLA-Pruner + ThinkProprio explicitly.
anno.effort_note: The training-free pilot (drop lowest-attention resampled tokens at fixed ratios, eval libero_spatial/object N=20) fits a 2h single-GPU slot per config, but ONLY after ~2-4 days of plumbing to expose discarded attention weights and respect the hybrid attention/connector design. Full study with LIBERO-PRO robustness + optional LoRA is 1-2+ weeks. High effort, high overlap risk.

title: Typed-abort routing: dispersion geometry selects the replan response (resample tail vs macro re-encode vs safe-stop)
lenses: METHOD-TRANSFER lens: a multi-scopic primitive (P1-P7) that works in legged locomotion but is untried in VLA manipulation, ported as a FUNDAMENTAL change to a named SmolVLA component (inference-loop / tokenizer / action-expert flow head / training objective), verified on LIBERO with the user's existing SmolVLA+LeRobot harness and its ready-made flow-head dispersion signal.
primitive: P5 (reactive interrupt) deepened with the response-selection it implies, reconciled at P2's meso level (bottom-up dispersion type meets top-down intention to pick the response).
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the inference-loop response policy: the single fixed 'refill chunk' branch in select_action becomes a typed router over {keep, meso tail-resample best-of-K, macro re-encode, safe-stop}, keyed on dispersion geometry. The replan behavior contract is changed, not extended.
summary: Port P5 in its richer form — the interrupt must not just fire, it must choose the right corrective pathway — combined with P2's meso reconciliation. Instead of a single abort action, classify the GEOMETRY of the flow-head dispersion at the trigger moment: multi-modal/clustered disagreement across the K sampled chunks (an affordance fork: several coherent plans) routes to a cheap meso tail-resample + best-of-K selection on the cached prefix; diffuse/incoherent disagreement (OOD confusion) routes to a full macro backbone re-encode with re-grounded language; degenerate disagreement where no coherent plan exists routes to safe-stop. This makes the act/replan/escalate decision a typed function of the policy's own self-disagreement structure, landing on the inference loop's response policy rather than just its trigger.
hypothesis: Routing the abort by dispersion geometry beats a single uniform abort policy: cheap tail-resample suffices for multimodal affordance forks (saving backbone calls) while reserving expensive macro re-encode for genuinely OOD frames, giving better success-per-compute than always-replan-from-backbone under perturbation.
mve_libero: Build on the AEF-Interrupt MVE. At trigger, cluster the K sampled chunks (cheap: variance ratio / silhouette on the suffix) to label dispersion type, then dispatch the three responses (meso resample reuses cached prefix; macro recomputes embed_prefix). Evaluate on perturbed libero_spatial/object (N=20) vs (a) no-interrupt baseline and (b) always-macro-replan ablation, reporting success and backbone-calls. Inference-only.
expected_signal: Two-axis: post-perturbation success and backbone-calls-per-episode vs always-macro-replan. Positive: typed routing matches always-replan success at fewer backbone calls, OR exceeds it because cheap meso resamples avoid discarding a still-valid prefix. Clear contribution either way; isolates whether dispersion CARRIES actionable structure beyond a scalar magnitude.
contribution_type: method (typed reactive-replan policy) + ablation against scalar-threshold and always-replan

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-TRUE, with a caveat. The change targets the inference-loop RESPONSE policy inside select_action: today (modeling_smolvla.py:325-353) the only branch is "queue empty -> recompute one chunk -> refill"; the proposal replaces that with a typed router over {keep, meso tail-resample best-of-K, macro re-encode, safe-stop} keyed on the GEOMETRY of flow-head dispersion. That changes the decision contract of the inference loop, not just adds a sensor. However, two of the four branches are weak as "fundamental" changes: (a) "macro re-encode" is what SmolVLA ALREADY does at every chunk boundary (each select_action refill calls _get_action_chunk which re-runs the VLM backbone), so it is not new; (b) "safe-stop" is a trivial gate. The genuinely fundamental piece is the MESO tail-resample-with-prefix-reuse branch, but that path does NOT exist in the code — there is no cached embed_prefix / KV-cache reuse in select_action, so the "cheap meso" branch must be BUILT (real architectural work on the action expert's interface to the cached VLM prefix). If the meso branch degenerates to "resample the whole chunk" (no prefix reuse), the whole thing collapses to a scalar-threshold trigger that picks between full-recompute and stop — i.e. a bolt-on, not fundamental. So: fundamental ONLY IF the prefix-reuse meso path is actually implemented; flag this dependency loudly.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable but NOT in the current harness as-is. The user's evaluate.py shells out to lerobot-eval as a subprocess; the per-frame dispersion signal lives only in the OFFLINE pool-based path (episode_signals, teacher-forced over a dataset). You must fork an IN-PROCESS rollout from lerobot_eval.py:rollout() (the intercept point exists: select_action at line 186, env.step at 198) so you can (i) sample K chunks per chunk-boundary, (ii) cluster them, (iii) route. Suite: libero_spatial and libero_object, N=20 episodes/task. Perturbation (mandatory for a reactivity claim): use the LIBERO-plus perturbation dims already referenced in envs/configs.py:726 (camera viewpoint / texture / sensor noise) OR inject mid-episode observation noise/object-shift; without a perturbation the typed router has nothing to react to and the result is uninterpretable. Metric = two-axis: post-perturbation pc_success AND VLM-backbone-calls-per-episode. Baselines: (b0) vanilla SmolVLA = single fixed chunk refill, no intercept; (b1) scalar-threshold abort (always macro re-encode when dispersion > tau) — this is the CRITICAL ablation that isolates whether GEOMETRY adds anything over MAGNITUDE; (b2) always-macro-replan (recompute every step). Positive result: typed routing matches b2 success at materially fewer backbone calls, OR beats b1 at equal backbone budget (proving geometry carries actionable structure beyond a scalar). Negative-but-publishable: geometry gives no lift over the scalar threshold (b1 ~= router) — a clean "dispersion magnitude is sufficient, structure is not actionable" finding. Honest 2h-pilot risk: building the in-process rollout + K-sampling at every step is multi-day, not a 2h pilot; the 2h budget only covers ONE config once the harness exists.
anno.smolvla_fit: SmolVLA's flow-matching action expert (sample_actions/denoise in modeling_smolvla.py) is the right substrate and is genuinely multimodal-capable; select_action's single refill branch is the named component to change; but the user's dispersion code is offline-only and scalar-only, so it helps the concept (std-across-K is the correct primitive) yet must be substantially rebuilt for closed-loop, full-tensor, geometry-clustering use.
prior_work: SCALE: Self-uncertainty Conditioned Adaptive Looking and Execution for VLA (arXiv 2602.04208) — single-pass adaptive inference that modulates BOTH action decoding AND visual attention on the model's own predictive uncertainty; this is the closest and most threatening prior: it already couples uncertainty to a typed compute/execution response. The proposal must differentiate on dispersion-GEOMETRY-typed routing vs SCALE's scalar-conditioned modulation.

SV-VLA: Open-Loop Planning, Closed-Loop Verification / Speculative Verification (arXiv 2604.02965) — executes only the VALID PREFIX of a chunk and replans when state diverges; this is essentially the candidate's prefix-reuse + meso-resample idea minus the geometry typing.
Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLA (arXiv 2604.04161) — shrinks/grows chunk size by action entropy; same uncertainty->execution-policy axis, scalar-driven.

INSIGHT: Inference-time Sequence Introspection for Help Triggers in VLA (arXiv 2510.01389) — uses introspected uncertainty to trigger a typed response (ask-for-help); directly overlaps the 'typed reaction to self-disagreement' framing.

Diff-DAgger (arXiv 2410.14868) — explicitly names the candidate's CORE premise as a known hazard: expressive/ensemble policies disagree either because of genuine multimodality (each mode certain) OR OOD, and these are conflated by variance; the candidate's only real wedge is turning that exact confound into a routing signal rather than just flagging it.
ProbeFlow: Training-Free Adaptive Flow Matching for VLA (arXiv 2603.17850) — training-free adaptive inference on the flow head, same family.
AsyncVLA (arXiv 2511.14148) — asynchronous flow matching with self-correction over the action chunk, an alternative fundamental change to the same execution loop.
anno.so_what: If positive, the contribution is sharp and worth stating either way: it tests whether the SHAPE of a flow policy's self-disagreement (multimodal/clustered vs diffuse vs degenerate) carries actionable information beyond its MAGNITUDE — i.e., whether you can cheaply distinguish 'affordance fork, just pick a mode' from 'genuinely OOD, re-ground' at inference time. That is a real open question (Diff-DAgger frames the confound but does not exploit it) with a clean compute payoff: reserve expensive backbone re-encodes for true OOD, resolve forks cheaply. A negative result (geometry == scalar) is also publishable as a 'dispersion magnitude suffices, structure is not actionable on SmolVLA/LIBERO' finding. The danger is the so-what evaporating if the meso branch isn't genuinely cheaper than the macro branch, because then the two-axis (success vs backbone-calls) story has no axis-2 separation.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The strongest objection is that the central distinction is unmeasurable at the relevant K. Reliable clustering of K sampled chunks into 'multimodal vs diffuse vs degenerate' geometry requires K large enough for a silhouette/variance-ratio test to be stable — but each sample is a full flow-matching backbone+expert pass, so at the 2h/single-GPU budget K is forced small (4-8). At small K, silhouette scores on a (T,A)-dim suffix are dominated by noise; the geometry label will be near-random, and the typed router will be statistically indistinguishable from the scalar-threshold ablation (b1). That collapses the entire novelty claim: if geometry is unmeasurable, you have re-derived adaptive-action-chunking-by-uncertainty (already published, arXiv 2604.04161). Second-strongest: the 'macro re-encode' branch is not a new behavior (SmolVLA already re-encodes the VLM every chunk boundary), and the 'meso prefix-reuse' branch — the only genuinely new mechanism — requires KV-cache surgery on SmolVLA's backbone that is itself a multi-week engineering project with its own correctness risks, dwarfing the 'router' framing. Third: a reactivity claim needs a perturbation that actually induces multimodal (not just elevated) dispersion; if the perturbation only pushes the policy OOD, you never exercise the multimodal branch and cannot validate the routing taxonomy.
anno.effort_note: Weeks; the MVE understates effort (needs an in-process rollout fork, full-tensor K-sampling, and KV-cache prefix reuse for the meso branch). Recommended scope cut: drop prefix reuse, ship a 3-way {keep/full-recompute-best-of-K/safe-stop} router and test geometry-vs-scalar, accepting that the multi-rate P1/P2 framing is then lost and only P5 survives.

title: Dispersion-Geometry Execution Horizon: dissolve the chunk-length/reactivity tradeoff by making n_action_steps per-step adaptive from the flow head's OWN intra-chunk disagreement profile
lenses: CONTRADICTION lens: resolve a real conflict in the literature — design a fundamental change to SmolVLA that dissolves a genuine tradeoff rather than trading one horn for the other.
primitive: P3 (attention = adaptive compute) fused with P5 (AEF-interrupt as graded commit-horizon shortening) — spend execution-commitment density where the action manifold is information-rich (high disagreement) and coast where it is flat.
fundamental_method_change: INFERENCE-LOOP: replaces the fixed self.config.n_action_steps queue-refill policy in SmolVLAPolicy.select_action / _check_get_actions_condition. Instead of refilling only when the ACTION queue is empty (popleft of all 50), the queue is truncated to t* derived from the per-timestep dispersion profile of the just-sampled chunk, so the heavy backbone fires earlier in high-dispersion phases and later in low-dispersion phases. The dispersion-profile -> t* mapping is calibrated per suite via the existing conformal_active quantile machinery.
summary: The contradiction: long open-loop chunks (n_action_steps=50) give smooth, throughput-efficient, temporally-coherent execution but blind the policy to new observations mid-chunk (reactivity loss); short chunks restore reactivity but cost backbone re-encodes and jerk. AAC/AutoHorizon pick a SCALAR chunk length from a global entropy/attention proxy decided up front; they still commit a fixed prefix. The dissolving move: replace SmolVLA's fixed n_action_steps commitment with a per-chunk *commit horizon* read directly off the PER-TIMESTEP dispersion PROFILE within the freshly sampled chunk. SmolVLA already samples K chunks for dispersion; std across the K samples is a (T, A) array. The novel object is the cumulative per-step dispersion curve: commit the policy open-loop only up to the timestep t* where cumulative dispersion crosses a calibrated band, then force a backbone re-encode. Free-space transport (low dispersion deep into the chunk) -> long commit, throughput preserved; contact/insertion phases (dispersion rises early) -> short commit, reactivity restored. One model, one knob computed from a signal the harness ALREADY produces; no extra forward passes beyond the K already sampled.
hypothesis: Per-step dispersion-profile commit horizons yield strictly higher clean-LIBERO success-per-backbone-call than any fixed n_action_steps (5/10/25/50) on the Pareto frontier, AND recover more success than fixed chunks under a mid-episode object perturbation, because the commit horizon auto-shortens exactly in the contact phases where blind open-loop execution fails.
mve_libero: Take a single SmolVLA checkpoint already fine-tuned on libero_spatial (PS.4 gate passed at 80%). At eval, monkeypatch _get_action_chunk to sample K=4 chunks, compute the (T,A) std profile, set t* = first timestep where cumulative-mean-std exceeds tau (tau from the conformal quantile of calibration rollouts), truncate the action queue to t*. Run lerobot-eval on libero_spatial (20 eps) at 4 settings: fixed n_action_steps in {50,25,10} and adaptive. Log success AND number of backbone re-encodes per episode. Reuse conformal_active.uncertainty for tau. No training. ~1.5 GPU-h.
expected_signal: Adaptive matches or beats the best fixed-chunk success while using fewer backbone calls than n_action_steps=10 (the reactive-but-expensive fixed setting); plot success vs backbone-calls/episode and show adaptive lies above the fixed-chunk Pareto frontier. A clean negative (adaptive never beats the frontier) is itself publishable: dispersion profile does not localize the reactive moments.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: It genuinely changes a core VLA INFERENCE method, not a bolt-on module. The change is to SmolVLA's open-loop commitment policy itself: the default is chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50 (verified in configuration_smolvla.py), and select_action refills the ACTION queue only when empty via _check_get_actions_condition() returning len(queue)==0, then commits actions.transpose(0,1)[:n_action_steps] (verified at modeling_smolvla.py lines 325-353). The proposal replaces the FIXED n_action_steps prefix commitment with a per-chunk variable commit horizon t* derived from the (K,T,A) per-timestep dispersion profile, forcing the heavy backbone to re-encode at a data-dependent point. That alters the temporal/computational structure of inference (one fixed clock -> dispersion-gated re-encode clock), which is a legitimate fundamental-method change in the same category the user mandated. Caveat: it does NOT touch architecture, weights, tokenization, or training objective — it is a pure inference-time policy change, the lightest of the "fundamental" categories, and it is implemented as a monkeypatch over an unchanged checkpoint. Honest framing: it is fundamental-but-inference-only, and it is squarely in the same class as several 2025-26 papers (AAC, AutoHorizon, MoH), so 'fundamental' here does NOT imply 'novel.'
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_spatial (the checkpoint already gated at 80% per PS.4); extend to libero_object/goal/long only if the pilot is positive. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA with fixed n_action_steps in {50,25,10,5} (the policy as-shipped). Treatment = adaptive commit horizon t* = first timestep where cumulative-mean dispersion crosses a conformal band. Primary metric is NOT raw success but the success-vs-backbone-calls/episode Pareto: positive = adaptive lies strictly above the fixed-chunk frontier (matches/beats best fixed success at fewer backbone calls than the cheapest reactive fixed setting). CRITICAL CAVEAT on feasibility: the current evaluate.py shells out to `lerobot-eval` as a subprocess and CANNOT inject per-step logic. The MVE's monkeypatch of _check_get_actions_condition/select_action requires running the eval IN-PROCESS (import lerobot.scripts.lerobot_eval.eval_policy, patch the policy object before the rollout loop at line 186 `action = policy.select_action(observation)`). This is doable but is real plumbing the harness does not yet have — budget for it. Reactivity claim REQUIRES a perturbation: clean LIBERO alone cannot show the reactivity horn. Concrete perturbation = displace the target object pose by a few cm at a fixed mid-episode step (or inject a camera/observation shift), held identical across all settings; positive = adaptive recovers more success than every fixed chunk because t* auto-shortens in the contact phase. Without the perturbation the experiment only tests the throughput horn and the reactivity hypothesis is untested. K=4 chunk samples per re-encode adds ~3 extra action-expert forwards (cheap; backbone KV-cache is shared), so the K-sampling cost claim holds only if the K samples reuse the prefix encode — verify this in modeling_smolvla, because predict_action_chunk currently re-runs _prepare_batch each call.
anno.smolvla_fit: Excellent fit on the signal, moderate fit on the plumbing. The user's dispersion signal IS the (K,T,A) std array (uncertainty.raw_dispersion currently collapses it to a scalar via std(axis=0).mean(); the per-timestep profile std(axis=0).mean(axis=-1) is one line away in policy_runner.py / uncertainty.py). Components that change: (1) SmolVLAPolicy._check_get_actions_condition + the queue-truncation slice in select_action (modeling_smolvla.py 343-350); (2) a new wrapper that samples K chunks at each re-encode, computes the cumulative profile, sets t*; (3) reuse conformal_active.uncertainty._conformal_quantile for the band tau. The existing dispersion machinery (uncertainty.py, query_methods.DispersionQuery) is built for OFFLINE pool-based candidate scoring via policy.forward on a DataLoader — it is NOT wired into the online rollout, so the dispersion code is reusable as a library but the online integration is net-new. Also note: this LeRobot build already ships RTC (Real-Time Chunking, rtc_config in SmolVLAConfig, RTCProcessor) as an alternative answer to the same consistency/reactivity tradeoff — that is both a strong baseline you must beat and evidence the maintainers consider this problem important.
prior_work: AutoHorizon / 'VLA Knows Its Limits' (arXiv:2602.21445, Feb 2026): THE direct predecessor. 'First test-time method that dynamically estimates the execution horizon for EACH predicted action chunk' for FLOW-BASED VLAs, evaluated on LIBERO, explicitly beats fixed-horizon oracles. Uses a per-chunk attention-mass profile with bidirectional soft-pointer turning-point detection to set the horizon. The candidate is structurally the same (per-chunk adaptive horizon from a confidence profile, flow VLA, test-time, LIBERO) with flow-head sampling-dispersion substituted for attention mass, plus a conformal band. This is the novelty threat.

AAC: 'Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLA' (arXiv:2604.04161): uses action ENTROPY as the cue to adaptively select chunk size at inference (high uncertainty -> shorter chunk). Same mechanism, scalar-uncertainty -> chunk-size; the candidate's per-timestep profile is the main differentiator from AAC specifically.

Mixture of Horizons (arXiv:2511.19433, Nov 2025): fuses multiple horizons in one policy, dynamic inference via cross-horizon consensus, 2.5x throughput. Trains horizon mixing; candidate is training-free, but MoH already covers the 'dissolve the horizon tradeoff' thesis.

Real-Time Chunking / RTC (arXiv:2506.07339) — ALREADY VENDORED in the user's lerobot (rtc_config, RTCProcessor): poses async chunking as inpainting, freezes guaranteed actions and inpaints the rest. The canonical inference-time answer to the consistency/reactivity tradeoff and a must-cite, must-beat baseline.
A2C2 / 'Leave No Observation Behind' (arXiv:2509.23224): lightweight real-time chunk-correction head every control step — another solution to the same tradeoff.
ProbeFlow (arXiv:2603.17850): training-free ADAPTIVE flow matching for VLAs — overlapping 'adaptive flow-head compute at inference' territory.
anno.so_what: The purpose is real and the contradiction is real (long chunks = throughput+coherence but blind; short chunks = reactive but expensive/jerky). A clean, training-free, dispersion-gated commit horizon with a success-per-backbone-call Pareto is a legitimately useful and falsifiable contribution, and a clean negative ('the dispersion profile does NOT localize the reactive moments, so per-step dispersion horizons do not beat the fixed frontier') is genuinely informative about whether flow-head self-disagreement carries phase information. BUT the 'so what' is badly eroded by timing: AutoHorizon already demonstrated test-time per-chunk adaptive horizons beating fixed-horizon oracles on LIBERO for flow VLAs as of Feb 2026. So the contribution is no longer 'adaptive horizons help' (settled) but the narrower 'dispersion is a better/cheaper horizon signal than attention turning-points, and conformal calibration of the band matters.' That narrower claim is publishable as a focused empirical study, not as a method paper.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: this is AutoHorizon with a different uncertainty proxy. A reviewer will say the fundamental move (per-chunk adaptive execution horizon from an intra-chunk confidence PROFILE, test-time, flow VLA, LIBERO) was already published months earlier, and the only delta is signal source (flow-head dispersion vs attention mass) plus a conformal threshold — which makes this an ablation of AutoHorizon, not a new method. To survive, the paper MUST (a) include AutoHorizon and RTC as head-to-head baselines, not just fixed chunks, and (b) show dispersion wins on a dimension AutoHorizon cannot — e.g. dispersion needs no attention introspection so it generalizes to non-attention action heads, OR dispersion localizes contact phases that attention mass misses under perturbation. A second, mechanistic objection: the K-sample dispersion profile may be DOMINATED by per-dim scale (gripper open/close has huge std vs smooth transport) and by flow-matching noise schedule, not by genuine phase information, so cumulative-mean-std may cross the band based on action-dim variance, not reactivity need — the t* could correlate with nothing useful. A third: with only 20 episodes the success-vs-backbone-calls Pareto has wide CIs; 'lies above the frontier' may be statistically indistinguishable.

title: Two-clock SmolVLA: a frozen fast expert loop that PREEMPTS via dispersion, replacing the backbone-rate single clock with a micro reactive clock + macro re-ground clock
lenses: CONTRADICTION lens: resolve a real conflict in the literature — design a fundamental change to SmolVLA that dissolves a genuine tradeoff rather than trading one horn for the other.
primitive: P1 (three-clock multi-rate, here micro-execution + meso-expert-reroll + macro-backbone) and P5 (dispersion-driven macro interrupt: the heavy loop is recruited only when the cheap loop signals affordance-mismatch).
fundamental_method_change: INFERENCE-LOOP + KV-CACHE policy: factor sample_actions so the prefix KV-cache (built in the use_cache/fill_kv_cache=True call) PERSISTS across multiple chunk emissions; add a meso re-roll path that calls denoise_step against the cached prefix without rebuilding it. The backbone re-encode (embed_prefix) becomes event-driven on a dispersion threshold instead of firing every chunk. Changes SmolVLAPolicy._get_action_chunk / select_action and VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions caching lifetime.
summary: The contradiction: heavy backbone (SmolVLM2, 16 layers) gives semantics/generalization but its per-chunk re-encode is the latency wall, forcing a single slow clock; the field's dual-system fixes (GR00T, Helix, FiS-VLA) add a fast loop but run it at a FIXED cadence and the fast loop can NEVER preempt the slow one — reactivity remains hostage to the slow clock's schedule. The dissolving move: split SmolVLA's one clock into TWO with an interrupt. MESO clock = the existing flow expert re-sampling the chunk while reusing the CACHED prefix KV (denoise_step already reuses past_key_values — the expert can re-roll a chunk WITHOUT re-running the backbone). MACRO clock = full backbone embed_prefix re-encode, fired only when dispersion on cached-prefix re-rolls stays high across the meso loop (a learned signal that the stale visual prefix no longer supports a confident action — i.e. intention/scene change). This is a genuine fundamental change: today every chunk pays a full backbone pass; here most chunks are served by cheap expert-only re-rolls against cached visual KV, and the expensive backbone fires only on a dispersion-detected scene change.
hypothesis: Re-rolling the flow expert against a cached (stale) visual prefix preserves clean-LIBERO success for several control steps before dispersion rises, so backbone re-encodes can be cut by >=40% with <3pp success loss; and dispersion-on-stale-prefix is a usable trigger for WHEN the cached prefix has gone stale (rises sharply after a scene change / object displacement).
mve_libero: Patch SmolVLA inference: after one full sample_actions (backbone + 10 flow steps, KV cached), serve the next M chunk emissions by re-running ONLY the 10 denoise_step passes against the retained past_key_values (no embed_prefix). Each emission, compute dispersion across K=4 expert re-rolls on the cached prefix; if dispersion > tau, force a real backbone re-encode. Eval on libero_spatial + libero_object (20 eps each). Compare success and backbone-call count vs vanilla (backbone every chunk). Ablate: fixed M re-rolls (no trigger) vs dispersion-triggered. No training. ~2 GPU-h.
expected_signal: Dispersion-triggered backbone recruitment cuts backbone calls substantially at near-flat success on clean LIBERO; on a displaced-object variant the trigger fires fast (dispersion spike within 1-2 cached re-rolls of the displacement) and recovers more success than fixed-cadence re-rolling. Negative result (cached-prefix re-rolls collapse success immediately) cleanly bounds how stale a SmolVLA visual prefix may be — a useful systems datapoint.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: This genuinely changes a core inference method, not a bolt-on. Verified against the actual code: VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:812) builds past_key_values once via a backbone pass with fill_kv_cache=True (lines 836-843), then runs num_steps denoise_step calls (line 883) that reuse that cache with fill_kv_cache=False (line 910). The proposal restructures the cache LIFETIME so the prefix KV persists across multiple chunk emissions and embed_prefix (the backbone re-encode) becomes event-driven on a dispersion threshold instead of firing every chunk. That is a change to the inference-loop + KV-cache policy and the select_action / _check_get_actions_condition control flow (lines 325-353). It is inference restructuring, NOT an added module. HOWEVER, be honest that the fundamentalness is modest in scope: it is a caching/scheduling change around an unchanged network and unchanged weights, in the same family as published token-caching and action-reuse methods, not a new architecture or training objective.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_spatial + libero_object (the repo's configured pair, conformal_active/config.py:18), 20 episodes each. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA via the repo's lerobot-eval subprocess path (evaluate.py reads aggregated.pc_success). Two metrics, both required: (1) success rate (pc_success) and (2) backbone-call count per episode (instrument embed_prefix). Positive = backbone calls cut >=40% at <=3pp success loss vs vanilla AND the dispersion-triggered variant beats a fixed-M-rerolls (no-trigger) ablation. CRITICAL caveat the candidate UNDERSTATES: vanilla SmolVLA already does NOT re-encode the backbone every control step — it executes n_action_steps=50 of a chunk_size=50 chunk open-loop (config defaults), so the backbone fires only once per ~50 steps already; the headroom to cut backbone calls is therefore far smaller than implied, and 'backbone every chunk' is a strawman baseline. The reactivity claim NEEDS a perturbation: name it concretely as a mid-episode object displacement / distractor injection (LIBERO object randomization or an OffScreenRenderEnv pose reset mid-rollout). Positive on perturbation = dispersion spikes within 1-2 cached re-rolls of the displacement AND triggered re-encode recovers more success than fixed-cadence. Feasibility note: the repo's existing dispersion path is OFFLINE (uncertainty.py computes dispersion on logged frames by calling policy.reset()+predict_action_chunk K times, each REBUILDING the cache); a closed-loop, cache-persisting rollout harness does not yet exist and must be written, so 2 GPU-h is optimistic for the full claim.
anno.smolvla_fit: Excellent substrate fit. Exact components that change: (a) VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions — split into embed_prefix(+fill_kv_cache) and a reusable denoise-only path accepting a persisted past_key_values; (b) SmolVLAPolicy.select_action / _get_action_chunk / _check_get_actions_condition — add a meso re-roll branch and a dispersion gate; (c) config use_cache=True is already on (configuration_smolvla.py:66), so the cache machinery exists. The user's dispersion signal (raw_dispersion in uncertainty.py:31, mean per-(timestep,dim) std across K chunks) is directly reusable as the trigger, with one important twist the candidate gets right: the novel signal is dispersion across K expert re-rolls on a CACHED/STALE prefix (cheap, one backbone pass, varying only flow noise), whereas the existing harness computes dispersion across K FULL passes (expensive, fresh prefix each time). So the existing code helps conceptually but the cheap cached-prefix re-roll variant must be newly implemented.
prior_work: FlashVLA / 'Think Twice, Act Once' (arXiv 2505.21200): training-free token-aware action REUSE that skips redundant heavy computation in 'stable' action steps and recomputes on change — functionally the candidate's reuse-then-recruit gate at action granularity.
VLA-Cache (arXiv 2502.02175): adaptive visual-token KV caching — reuse KV of static tokens across frames, recompute changed ones; closest 'reuse cached visual KV to skip backbone work' precedent.
KV-Efficient VLA (arXiv 2509.21354): RNN-gated chunked KV cache to speed the VLM backbone — overlapping KV-reuse-for-speed thesis.

AdaHorizon / uncertainty-triggered replanning and Pre-VLA (arXiv 2605.22446): within-chunk variance / uncertainty triggers test-time replan without retraining — the candidate's dispersion-gated recruitment instantiated with SmolVLA's flow self-disagreement.
EvoScene-VLA (2605.21862) and DeepVision-VLA: directly target the 'scene changes within a chunk / stale visual context' problem the candidate claims as its motivation.
Latent Bridge (2605.02739): feature-delta prediction to avoid re-running the slow dual-system component every step.
anno.so_what: The clean question is genuinely useful and underexplored as a CALIBRATED SmolVLA systems datapoint: how stale can a SmolVLA visual prefix get before its flow expert can no longer produce a confident action, and is cheap cached-prefix self-disagreement a faithful staleness detector? A clean negative (re-rolls collapse success immediately) tightly bounds open-loop visual staleness for flow-matching VLAs — a real, citable result. A positive contributes a dispersion-gated event-driven backbone scheduler. BUT the 'so what' is weakened by the crowded literature: the compute-saving framing is already owned by FlashVLA/VLA-Cache and the uncertainty-replan framing by AdaHorizon/Pre-VLA. The defensible novel wedge is narrow: SmolVLA's flow-head self-disagreement (the user's existing dispersion metric) as the SPECIFIC staleness trigger, evaluated as a staleness probe rather than a speed paper.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: the compute-saving premise is largely illusory on stock SmolVLA. Vanilla already runs open-loop for n_action_steps=50 (= chunk_size=50), so the backbone fires roughly once per 50 control steps, not every step. The '>=40% backbone-call reduction' is measured against a strawman 'backbone every chunk' baseline; against the real open-loop baseline the method ADDS backbone calls when dispersion spikes mid-chunk — its actual contribution is closed-loop re-grounding for reactivity, which COSTS compute, contradicting the headline efficiency claim. Second: re-rolling the flow expert against a frozen prefix only varies sampling noise; on a confident state the K re-rolls agree regardless of whether the scene changed, so cached-prefix dispersion may be BLIND to scene change precisely when the backbone is stale ('confident on a stale belief' is a known self-consistency failure mode). The reactivity thesis rests on dispersion-on-stale-prefix actually rising after a perturbation, which is unverified and plausibly false. Third: no training means the flow head was never optimized to be re-rolled against stale KV, so degradation could be immediate and uninformative.
anno.effort_note: Effort is 'weeks', not the claimed ~2 GPU-h, because the deliverable requires NEW code absent from the repo: (1) refactor sample_actions to persist past_key_values across emissions and expose a denoise-only re-roll; (2) a closed-loop rollout harness that runs SmolVLA step-by-step with cache persistence (current eval goes through the stock lerobot-eval subprocess; current dispersion path is offline-only and rebuilds the cache every sample); (3) embed_prefix call-counting instrumentation; (4) a mid-episode perturbation injector for the reactivity arm. Scope cut to fit budget: for a first 2-GPU-h pilot, DROP the reactivity/perturbation arm and the speed claim; instead run a pure STALENESS PROBE — for fixed M in {1,2,4,8} serve M emissions from one cached prefix (expert-only re-rolls) and plot success vs M on libero_spatial (20 eps), logging cached-prefix dispersion per step. That single curve answers 'how stale is too stale' and 'does dispersion track staleness' cheaply and de-risks the whole idea before building the gated scheduler.

title: Dispersion-warped flow integration: dissolve the compute-vs-precision tradeoff by spending num_steps non-uniformly across the chunk timesteps instead of uniformly
lenses: CONTRADICTION lens: resolve a real conflict in the literature — design a fundamental change to SmolVLA that dissolves a genuine tradeoff rather than trading one horn for the other.
