Budget: a short LoRA retrain on a fixed buffer fits ~2h/seed on one A6000; 3 seeds x 2 conditions is the honest minimum and pushes past the 2h-per-pilot single-run budget into a ~12h sweep.
anno.smolvla_fit: Changes are localized to LeRobot SmolVLA: (1) VLAFlowMatching.forward (modeling_smolvla.py:774-810) which produces the per-(B,step,dim) MSE tensor, and (2) SmolVLAPolicy.forward (modeling_smolvla.py:358-413) reduction logic — must add a per-step-weighted reduction that preserves the chunk-step axis (current 'none' collapses it). The user's existing dispersion signal partially helps but does NOT drop in: policy_runner.py computes a SCALAR per-episode dispersion (stacked.std(axis=0).mean() over K=8 chunks), whereas this objective needs a PER-STEP dispersion vector (std over K chunks kept along the chunk axis, NOT averaged) computed on the current training batch every M steps. That is a modest change to the dispersion computation (drop the final .mean over the time axis), but it adds K extra forward passes per re-estimation and must be threaded into the CLI loss path, not the active-selection loop where dispersion currently lives. Note LeRobot ALREADY has a SampleWeighter/RA-BC mechanism (sample_weighting.py) for per-SAMPLE weighting wired into update_policy and the CLI — this idea is best framed/implemented as a per-STEP extension of that existing hook, which both eases implementation and weakens the 'nobody weights the chunk loss' novelty claim.
prior_work: FreqPolicy (arXiv:2506.08822): adaptive Focal-Loss-style weighting that emphasizes high-DISCREPANCY components within flow-matching action chunks over the sequence — the closest competitor; differs only in using a frequency-domain discrepancy signal rather than the policy's own inference-time action dispersion.

Real-Time Execution of Action Chunking Flow Policies / Real-Time Chunking (arXiv:2506.07339): explicitly weights later-in-chunk actions as MORE uncertain via exponential decay — directly anticipates the 'late chunk steps deserve different treatment' hypothesis, just with a fixed positional schedule instead of a learned dispersion-driven one.

SD3 / logit-normal / Min-SNR flow-matching loss weighting (Esser et al. SD3; diffusers PR #8528): the established result that non-uniform weighting of the flow-matching loss helps — but along the NOISE-LEVEL time axis t, not the action-sequence-position axis. This is a conceptual hazard: in VLAFlowMatching the target u_t = noise - actions is constant across chunk steps, and per-batch random t already randomizes the noise level, so the dominant known loss-weighting lever is t, which this idea does not touch.

RA-BC / SampleWeighter already in the user's LeRobot tree (utils/sample_weighting.py, rewards/sarm/rabc.py): per-SAMPLE loss weighting hook already wired into update_policy and CLI. In-codebase prior art that makes the per-sample version non-novel and frames this as a per-step delta.

Self-Guidance and Adaptive Chunking for generative BC (arXiv:2510.12392): uses policy self-disagreement to modulate chunking/execution, overlapping the 'use the policy's own disagreement' motif (though at inference, not in the training objective).
anno.so_what: If positive: shows that fine-tuning capacity should be allocated by the policy's own self-disagreement within a chunk, giving a cheap, drop-in objective tweak that improves long-horizon VLA success at equal compute — a clean, generalizable training story. If negative (quite likely): it is still a publishable null that the chunk-step axis is the WRONG axis to reweight (the noise-level t dominates, per SD3), and that documented train-seed variance swamps small objective tweaks — which directly reinforces the user's existing 'Unreliable by Default' thesis. So the result matters either way. The fusion-thesis fit is real but thin: P3 (adaptive density) + P2 (bottom-up uncertainty shaping top-down optimization) map onto 'spend gradient where the policy disagrees with itself,' which is a legitimate, if loose, instantiation of the multi-scopic primitive.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The single strongest objection: the regression target in VLAFlowMatching is u_t = noise - actions, which is IDENTICAL across all chunk steps for a given sample (it does not depend on step index); per-step error magnitude reflects how hard the NETWORK finds each step under a per-batch-random noise level t, and the SD3/Min-SNR literature already establishes that the meaningful loss-weighting axis is t, not sequence position. So upweighting high-dispersion late steps may simply amplify gradient on the noisiest, least-learnable targets (chasing irreducible aleatoric multimodality / demo inconsistency at chunk tails), HURTING calibration and success — the opposite of the hypothesis. Compounding this: the user's OWN E1 result is that LoRA retrain pc_success has large train-seed std, and the expected effect (>=2pp) sits inside that noise band, so a single-seed pilot cannot distinguish signal from variance — the honest experiment is a multi-seed paired sweep that breaks the 2h-per-pilot budget. Together these make a clean positive result both mechanistically doubtful and statistically hard to claim.

title: Dispersion-Gated Adaptive Flow-Step Budget: spend denoise compute where the action manifold is sharp
lenses: SCALING-REGIME lens: COMPUTE ALLOCATION — accuracy/success vs FLOPs/latency under adaptive attention or multi-rate inference. The deliverable is a Pareto curve (success-rate vs mean per-step FLOPs/latency), not a single operating point. Grounded in the real SmolVLA substrate at /srv/data/users/anhar/codes/phosphobot/sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py: per-chunk cost = ONE heavy prefix VLM forward (num_vlm_layers=16, KV-cached) + num_steps=10 cheap expert denoise calls reusing that cache; chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 sets replan (heavy-forward) frequency; raw_dispersion() over K sampled chunks is the ready uncertainty signal (conformal_active/uncertainty.py). All knobs are config-settable per call; clean LIBERO success is the natural y-axis, mean FLOPs/latency the x-axis.
primitive: P3 (attention = adaptive compute allocation): integration density is spent where the flow field is ambiguous (high self-disagreement) and sparsified where it is sharp, with the dispersion signal acting as the GNG strength-feedback analog controlling solver granularity.
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the inference-loop integration schedule in SmolVLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:~810, the `for step in range(num_steps)` Euler loop). num_steps becomes a per-call random variable gated by an in-the-loop dispersion estimate rather than the constant config.num_steps. This is the action-expert's denoising solver, a fundamental inference component, not a bolt-on wrapper.
summary: Replace SmolVLA's FIXED num_steps=10 flow-integration loop with a dispersion-conditioned EARLY-EXIT denoiser. After a cheap probe (2 steps + 1 extra noise seed), measure the flow-head self-disagreement (raw_dispersion across the 2 partial trajectories). If dispersion is below a conformally-calibrated threshold, STOP integrating (the action manifold is sharp / unimodal -> a coarse Euler solve already converged); if high, continue to the full 10 steps. This realizes P3 (attention=adaptive compute) on the ONE axis SmolVLA exposes most cheaply, since each denoise step reuses the KV-cache and the heavy prefix forward is already paid. The deliverable is a success-vs-mean-num_steps Pareto curve.
hypothesis: On LIBERO Spatial/Object, most timesteps have a near-unimodal action posterior where 2-4 Euler steps already match the 10-step action within action-noise; gating num_steps on flow dispersion will hold clean success within 1-2pp of the 10-step baseline at ~40-60% of mean denoise FLOPs, producing a strictly better success-vs-compute Pareto frontier than any fixed num_steps in {2,4,6,8,10}.
mve_libero: No retraining. (1) Sweep FIXED num_steps in {2,4,6,8,10} on LIBERO Spatial (20 eps) to draw the baseline Pareto curve. (2) Add an adaptive variant: in sample_actions, run 2 steps, fork a second noise seed for 2 steps, compute raw_dispersion between the two x_t trajectories, threshold via the existing ConformalActionUncertainty (calibrate on 20 held-out rollout frames), and either exit or finish to 10. (3) Plot success vs mean-steps for fixed vs adaptive on the same axes. Reuse evaluate_checkpoint() and uncertainty.py as-is.
expected_signal: Adaptive point lies ABOVE-LEFT of the fixed-num_steps curve (same/within-1pp success at lower mean steps), and the per-frame exit-step histogram correlates with task phase (more steps near contact/grasp). Negative-but-useful result: if early-exit costs >3pp success, it bounds how multimodal SmolVLA's flow field actually is on LIBERO.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: It does edit a core inference component, not a wrapper: the proposal replaces the constant-num_steps Euler integration schedule inside SmolVLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:844-881, `num_steps = self.config.num_steps; dt = -1/num_steps; for step in range(num_steps): ... x_t += dt*v_t`) with a per-call data-dependent step count gated by an in-loop flow-disagreement estimate. That is the action expert's ODE solver — a genuine inference-time method change, not a bolt-on module. CAVEAT: the *mechanism* (use flow-field variance/disagreement to decide how many integration steps to take, down to 1 step when the field is near-deterministic) is exactly AdaFlow (NeurIPS 2024). So it changes a fundamental VLA method, but with a previously-published algorithm transplanted onto a new backbone. Mark as fundamental-but-not-novel rather than fundamental-and-novel.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: LIBERO-Spatial + LIBERO-Object (the proposal's choice; add Goal/Long only if the Pareto story holds). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA (lerobot/smolvla_base) at the shipped config.num_steps=10. Protocol: (1) Sweep FIXED num_steps in {1,2,4,6,8,10} over a fixed task/seed set (>=20 eps/task, ideally 50 for a stable success estimate) to draw the success-vs-mean-steps baseline frontier. (2) Adaptive variant: in sample_actions, after a cheap probe (e.g. 2 steps with two noise seeds), compute the per-element std of the two partial x_t trajectories, threshold via the existing ConformalActionUncertainty calibrated on held-out rollout frames, then either stop or continue to 10. (3) Overlay adaptive operating point(s) on the fixed curve. POSITIVE = the adaptive point lies strictly above-left of the fixed-step interpolation (success within ~1-2pp of 10-step at materially fewer mean steps, AND beating the equal-mean-step fixed setting). Reuse evaluate_checkpoint() and uncertainty.py. NOTE: no reactivity/perturbation claim is made here, so no perturbation test is needed — but that also means the multi-scopic 'attention' framing is purely a compute-allocation story, not the paper's P5 interrupt/reactivity primitive. Verifiable in budget IF eval is fast; see effort note re: the real cost.
anno.smolvla_fit: Edits exactly SmolVLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:812-881) and reads from configuration_smolvla.py (num_steps=10, chunk_size=50, num_vlm_layers=16). The existing dispersion signal helps only PARTIALLY and indirectly: conformal_active/uncertainty.py:raw_dispersion() and ConformalActionUncertainty operate on K *fully-sampled* chunks (across-chunk std), and policy_runner.py:133-143 samples K chunks via repeated policy.reset()+predict_action_chunk — i.e. K full 10-step solves. The proposed in-loop gate needs a DIFFERENT, finer signal: std between two *partial* x_t trajectories at an early step inside one solve. That is new code in the loop, not a reuse of the existing per-frame dispersion. The conformal calibration class is reusable as a thresholding utility, but the score it currently consumes is not the score the gate produces, so 'reuse uncertainty.py as-is' overstates the fit. Also note RTC path (self._rtc_enabled()) interacts with the loop — gating must be guarded to not break real-time-chunking.
prior_work: AdaFlow: Imitation Learning with Variance-Adaptive Flow-Based Policies (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2402.04292) — THE near-duplicate: uses the variance of the learned flow/ODE field to adaptively choose number of integration steps (1 step when the state is near-deterministic/unimodal, more when multimodal), specifically for robot imitation-learning decision making. The candidate is essentially AdaFlow's mechanism retargeted onto SmolVLA's action expert with a conformal threshold instead of AdaFlow's variance estimator.

AdaDiff: Accelerating Diffusion Models through Step-Wise Adaptive Computation (ECCV 2024, arXiv:2309.17074) — per-sample early-exit of the denoising process via a timestep-aware uncertainty estimation module; same 'uncertainty gates how much denoise compute to spend' idea in image diffusion.

Optimal Stepsize for Diffusion Sampling (arXiv:2503.21774) and A-FloPS (arXiv:2509.00036) — adaptive/optimized step schedules for flow/diffusion ODE solvers; show the few-step-solver acceleration space is crowded and well-studied.

Mean-Flow based One-Step Vision-Language-Action (arXiv:2603.01469) — VLAs are already being pushed to ONE-step action generation via distillation, which threatens the whole premise: if a distilled 1-step VLA matches 10-step success, an adaptive 2-10 step gate buys little.
DPM-Solver (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2206.00927) — high-order solver reaching ~10 steps with convergence guarantees; baseline-strength comparator the proposal does not include.
anno.so_what: Weak-to-moderate. The positive result ('SmolVLA's LIBERO action posterior is mostly near-unimodal so 2-4 Euler steps suffice') is a mildly interesting characterization, and the negative-but-useful framing (early-exit cost bounds how multimodal the flow field really is) is a genuine contribution. BUT the compute saved is on the CHEAP axis: per the proposal's own lens, each chunk = ONE heavy KV-cached prefix VLM forward (16 layers) + 10 cheap denoise calls reusing that cache. Cutting denoise steps from 10 to ~4 trims only the cheap tail, so wall-clock/FLOPs savings are modest unless the action expert's per-step cost is non-trivial relative to the prefix — which must be MEASURED, not assumed. The replan frequency (chunk_size=n_action_steps=50, one heavy forward per 50 executed steps) dominates cost, and this idea leaves that untouched. So the headline Pareto axis the proposal optimizes is largely the wrong one for SmolVLA's actual latency.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection (two-pronged): (1) NOVELTY — AdaFlow already did variance-adaptive flow-step counts for imitation-learning robot policies; swapping the variance estimator for a conformal threshold and the policy for SmolVLA is an application/transfer, not a new method, so a reviewer asks 'what does this teach us that AdaFlow didn't, beyond it-also-works-on-a-VLA?'. (2) WRONG-COST-AXIS — the probe itself burns 2 extra denoise steps + a second noise seed (effectively a partial second solve), so the break-even is high: if a typical clean LIBERO frame needs ~4 steps, you pay ~2 (probe) + up to ~2 more, and on hard frames you pay probe + full 10 = MORE than the 10-step baseline. Combined with the cheap-tail point above, the realistic mean-FLOPs win may be small and could even be negative on harder suites (Goal/Long). A distilled few-step VLA (Mean-Flow VLA) would also dominate the same Pareto curve without any runtime gating.
anno.effort_note: Implementation is days (small, surgical edit to one method + a fixed-step sweep harness; uncertainty.py thresholding partly reusable). The binding constraint is the 2-hour/pilot, single-GPU budget vs. the experimental matrix: a fixed sweep over 6 step-counts x >=20 eps x multiple tasks x (ideally) several seeds, PLUS the adaptive variant, is many LIBERO rollouts. A credible single-pilot must cut to ONE suite (Spatial), ~10 eps/task for the pilot, and report it as a feasibility probe, not the final Pareto. Mandatory de-risk before any rollout: (a) MEASURE the per-denoise-step vs prefix-forward FLOPs/latency split offline to confirm there is any meaningful compute to save; (b) confirm the early partial-x_t disagreement signal actually predicts 10-step-vs-k-step action divergence (offline, no env). If (a) shows denoise is <10-15% of chunk cost, kill or repivot to gating the heavy replan (chunk-execution interrupt, the P5 axis) instead — that would be the genuinely novel direction.

title: Dispersion-Triggered Replan: turning the fixed open-loop horizon into a compute-allocation knob
lenses: SCALING-REGIME lens: COMPUTE ALLOCATION — accuracy/success vs FLOPs/latency under adaptive attention or multi-rate inference. The deliverable is a Pareto curve (success-rate vs mean per-step FLOPs/latency), not a single operating point. Grounded in the real SmolVLA substrate at /srv/data/users/anhar/codes/phosphobot/sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py: per-chunk cost = ONE heavy prefix VLM forward (num_vlm_layers=16, KV-cached) + num_steps=10 cheap expert denoise calls reusing that cache; chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 sets replan (heavy-forward) frequency; raw_dispersion() over K sampled chunks is the ready uncertainty signal (conformal_active/uncertainty.py). All knobs are config-settable per call; clean LIBERO success is the natural y-axis, mean FLOPs/latency the x-axis.
primitive: P5 (Affordance-Effectivity-Fit interrupt) fused with P1 (variable meso clock): the action expert's chunk-commit horizon becomes an adaptive clock whose rate is set by bottom-up self-disagreement, so heavy-backbone compute is allocated only to information-rich moments.
fundamental_method_change: Rewrites _check_get_actions_condition and the queue-refill policy in SmolVLAPolicy.select_action (modeling_smolvla.py:~325-355). The replan trigger changes from 'queue exhausted' (time-based) to 'queue exhausted OR dispersion>tau' (content-based), AND allows EARLY abort of the remaining open-loop chunk. This is the canonical VLA inference loop's commit policy, a fundamental method, not an added module.
summary: SmolVLA's select_action drains a 50-step queue and only fires the HEAVY prefix VLM forward when the queue empties (_check_get_actions_condition: len==0). The heavy backbone forward dominates per-chunk FLOPs. Replace the binary 'replan when empty' rule with a dispersion-driven variable horizon: at each executed step, cheaply re-probe flow dispersion on the CURRENT observation (2 denoise steps, 2 seeds); coast on the open-loop queue while dispersion stays below the conformal threshold, but PREEMPT and re-fire the heavy prefix forward early when dispersion spikes. The y-axis is clean success, the x-axis is mean heavy-forwards-per-episode (the real latency driver). This is P5 (AEF interrupt) reframed as a compute-allocation Pareto rather than a reactivity claim.
hypothesis: A dispersion-triggered variable horizon will trace a success-vs-heavy-forward-count Pareto that dominates fixed-horizon n_action_steps in {10,25,50}: at matched mean heavy-forwards it yields higher LIBERO success (re-grounding exactly at hard sub-steps like grasp/insert), and at matched success it uses fewer heavy forwards than the always-replan (n_action_steps=1) extreme.
mve_libero: No retraining. (1) Baseline curve: sweep n_action_steps in {10,25,50} on LIBERO Spatial/Object (20 eps each), recording mean heavy-prefix-forwards/episode and success. (2) Adaptive variant: subclass select_action to recompute a cheap 2-step/2-seed dispersion each executed step, conformally calibrate tau on 1 seed of rollouts, refill the chunk early when exceeded. (3) Overlay adaptive vs fixed on success-vs-cost axes.
expected_signal: Adaptive sits above-left of the fixed-horizon curve. Diagnostic: dispersion-triggered replans cluster at task phase boundaries. If LIBERO (quasi-static) shows no gain at matched cost, that is itself the publishable finding that content-triggered replanning needs dynamic perturbations to pay off, motivating the injected-disturbance variant.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-true, leaning genuine. The proposal rewrites `_check_get_actions_condition` and the queue-refill commit policy in `SmolVLAPolicy.select_action` (modeling_smolvla.py:343-353), changing the chunk-commit trigger from time-based (queue empty, len==0) to content-based (queue empty OR dispersion>tau) with early abort of the open-loop tail. That IS the canonical VLA inference commit policy, not a sidecar module that leaves the forward pass untouched — so it clears the "not a bolt-on" bar more honestly than most ideas. HOWEVER, a strict reviewer will note it does NOT touch architecture, weights, tokenization, or the training objective: it is purely an inference-time control-flow change with zero learned parameters (tau is a conformal threshold, not trained). It is "fundamental method of the inference loop" but firmly in the lightest tier of fundamental — the same category the prior-art papers themselves occupy and explicitly advertise as "no training, no architecture change." So defensible as fundamental-of-inference, but do not oversell it as touching the model.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable and well-scoped. Suite: LIBERO-Spatial + LIBERO-Object (the harness already runs these), 20 eps/task-set, vanilla SmolVLA (lerobot/smolvla_base, no retrain) as the baseline. Axes: y = clean success rate; x = mean heavy-prefix-forwards/episode (the true latency driver, since each sample_actions = 1 prefix forward + 10 cheap denoise). Baseline curve = sweep n_action_steps in {10,25,50} (and the n_action_steps=1 always-replan extreme as the upper-compute anchor). Adaptive variant overlaid; POSITIVE = adaptive lies strictly above-left of the fixed-horizon curve at matched mean-heavy-forwards on at least one suite with non-overlapping seed bands. CRITICAL CAVEAT the candidate itself half-concedes: LIBERO is quasi-static, so a reactivity/interrupt claim has no perturbation to react to — you must NAME and inject one (e.g., randomized object-pose resets mid-episode, a scripted distractor nudge, or camera/observation latency injection) or the "interrupt" framing is untestable and you can only claim the compute-allocation framing. Without a perturbation, the honest null result ("content-triggered replanning gives no gain over fixed horizon on static LIBERO at matched cost") is publishable only as a negative-result note, not as validation of P5.
anno.smolvla_fit: Excellent substrate fit on plumbing, with one cost flaw. Changes localize to a select_action subclass overriding _check_get_actions_condition (modeling_smolvla.py:352) and the refill in select_action (line 343-348). The existing dispersion signal (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion + ConformalActionUncertainty for tau calibration) is directly reusable — this is the idea's strongest asset. FLAW I verified in the code: the candidate claims a "cheap 2-step/2-seed dispersion re-probe each executed step." It is NOT cheap. policy_runner.py:133-143 computes dispersion by calling predict_action_chunk K times, and EACH call re-runs the full heavy prefix VLM forward (sample_actions line 836, fill_kv_cache=True) because the KV-cache is keyed to the prefix (image+lang+state), which changes every step. So a 2-seed probe = 2 heavy prefix forwards per executed step. That cost must be charged on the SAME x-axis as the replans it avoids; otherwise the Pareto is rigged. Mitigations exist (share one prefix forward across seeds by varying only the flow noise — feasible since denoise reuses past_key_values; or cut probe num_steps to 2), but the candidate's current cost accounting is wrong and the headline "compute knob" claim is fragile until probe cost is honestly booked.
prior_work: Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLA (arXiv:2604.04161): uses action ENTROPY at inference to shrink/grow chunk size, no training, no arch change, evaluated on VLA incl. pi0-style flow-matching — this is the SAME thesis (uncertainty-driven adaptive horizon) with a near-identical 'no-retrain inference-only' selling point. The single closest competitor.

Mixture of Horizons in Action Chunking (arXiv:2511.19433): cross-horizon consensus -> self-truncating executable chunk, defers uncertain tail to replanning, reports adaptive-horizon dynamic inference on LIBERO with explicit success-vs-throughput (2.5x) tradeoff and 99% LIBERO mixed success. Directly occupies the success-vs-compute Pareto + phase-boundary-clustering story the candidate proposes.

PI-VLA / AURD (mdpi Symmetry 2026): Active Uncertainty-Resolving Decider monitors action-consensus discrepancy + state-prediction error, dynamically adjusts execution horizon via closed-loop replanning, explicitly 'breaks open-loop execution and triggers interactive replanning when signals exceed thresholds' — this is P5 (AEF interrupt) already implemented for VLA manipulation.

FASTER: Rethinking Real-Time Flow VLAs (arXiv:2603.19199) and Real-Time Robot Execution with Masked Action Chunking (arXiv:2601.20130): adaptive/early-commit chunk execution for flow VLAs on the latency axis.
ConformalDAgger / Chua et al. 2025 (arXiv:2410.08852): the conformal-threshold-on-dispersion machinery the candidate reuses is itself prior art (already cited in the repo's uncertainty.py).
anno.so_what: Modest and now largely pre-empted. IF positive, the contribution is a clean Pareto characterization on the specific SmolVLA flow-matching substrate using the self-disagreement (dispersion) signal rather than entropy — a narrow, incremental delta over AAC (2604.04161) and MoH (2511.19433). IF the result is null on static LIBERO at matched cost, the negative finding ("content-triggered replanning needs dynamic perturbations to pay off") is the more interesting and more defensible deliverable — but it only matters if you actually run the perturbation arm, otherwise it is an unsurprising restatement that quasi-static benchmarks don't reward reactivity. Either way the 'why it matters' rides on the dispersion-vs-entropy distinction and the perturbation study, not on the adaptive-horizon idea itself, which is now a 2025-2026 crowded lane.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The single strongest objection: this is a re-derivation of already-published 2025-2026 work (Adaptive Action Chunking 2604.04161; Mixture of Horizons 2511.19433; PI-VLA AURD) on a different signal (dispersion vs entropy/consensus) and a different backbone — a substitution-level delta, not a new idea. Compounding it: the central 'compute knob' claim is built on a cost-accounting error — each per-step dispersion re-probe re-runs the heavy prefix VLM forward (verified at modeling_smolvla.py:836 + policy_runner.py:140), so the probe spends exactly the resource the method claims to save; charge it honestly and the Pareto may collapse to break-even. Third: on quasi-static LIBERO there is no disturbance for an 'interrupt' to fire on, so the P5/reactivity framing is untestable without an injected perturbation the candidate has not committed to. A reviewer can reject on novelty alone (closest prior art predates this and shares the no-retrain/Pareto framing) before even reaching the cost flaw.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Genuinely changes a core inference/representation method, NOT a bolt-on. That alters which layers fill the KV-cache and therefore the representation the flow action-expert conditions on. CAVEAT that downgrades it from 'clean' to 'entangled': the change is NOT confined to the prefix. The expert layer at layer_idx cross-attends to past_key_values[layer_idx] filled by the prefix forward at the SAME index (forward_cross_attn_layer, smolvlm_with_expert.py:339-350), and expert depth is hard-tied to VLM depth (lm_expert_config.num_hidden_layers = self.num_vlm_layers, line 110; get_model_layers multiple_of = num_vlm_layers // num_expert_layers, line 404). Running the prefix at 8 of 16 layers leaves layers 8-15 KV-cache unfilled, so the expert's upper layers KeyError. So a 'fundamental change' here necessarily co-modifies the action-head computation (truncate expert in lockstep, or project the shallow hidden state up), which is more invasive than the proposal's framing implies. It is fundamental, but it touches the action expert too.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: LIBERO-Spatial first (20 eps/op-point), then Object/Goal for breadth. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA at fixed num_vlm_layers in {16 (default), 12, 8} — three static depths, each giving (success, mean prefix-FLOPs). Treatment = per-replan depth gate: at each heavy prefix call, decide full vs shallow depth from flow-head dispersion (raw_dispersion over K sampled chunks, conformal_active/uncertainty.py:31) against a calibrated tau. Y-axis = clean LIBERO success; X-axis = mean executed VLM-layer-FLOPs per replan (replan freq set by chunk_size=n_action_steps=50). POSITIVE = the adaptive point sits strictly above-left of the static-depth interpolation curve (e.g. within 1-2pp of full-depth success at >=25% fewer mean backbone FLOPs). NOTE the metric must be HONEST about the gate's own cost: computing dispersion needs K extra full-depth forward passes per gating decision (policy_runner.py:133-143 confirms ~K extra forwards/frame), which must be amortized INTO the x-axis or the savings are illusory. Reactivity claim (the 'macro full-depth on intention change' story) needs an explicit perturbation: inject a mid-episode distractor/object-shift or a language-goal swap and verify full depth is recruited at the change (layer-FLOP histogram spikes at the perturbation frame). Without a perturbation the 'two-rate / intention-change' framing is untested decoration.
anno.smolvla_fit: Concrete components touched: (1) SmolVLAPolicy.sample_actions / select_action prefix call (modeling_smolvla.py:830-843) gains a depth argument; (2) SmolVLMWithExpertModel.forward num_layers loop (smolvlm_with_expert.py:435-437) becomes a runtime-variable upper bound; (3) UNAVOIDABLY the expert path get_model_layers/forward_cross_attn_layer must be made consistent with the truncated KV-cache (the proposal's 'zero-shot reuse first-k layers' is architecturally false as written — upper-layer KV is simply absent). User's dispersion signal HELPS as the gate input and is already implemented (raw_dispersion + policy_runner sampling), so no new uncertainty machinery is needed; but it does NOT come free (K extra forwards). CLOSEST prior work; largely pre-empts the core deliverable (adaptive layer skipping + LIBERO Pareto). Differentiation is narrow: dispersion-gated vs importance-learned, plus the explicit micro/meso/macro multi-rate framing.

anno.so_what: If positive: a success-vs-backbone-FLOP Pareto showing a signal the model already emits (flow-head disagreement) can route backbone depth, beating any fixed depth — useful for the async/edge SmolVLA story. If negative (half-depth collapses zero-shot, the LIKELY outcome given the expert-VLM KV coupling), it bounds SmolVLA's depth-robustness ceiling and quantifies how much the action expert depends on full-depth prefix KV — a publishable negative for the 'unreliable by default' line. Either way the result matters. BUT the so-what is materially weakened by DeeR-VLA and especially DySL-VLA already establishing 'adaptive VLA depth pays off on manipulation benchmarks'; the contribution narrows to 'dispersion is a competitive zero-train gate signal on SmolVLA' — a method-comparison, not a new capability.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The central feasibility premise ('no retraining needed; shallow depth reuses the first-k pretrained layers' hidden state as a coarse prefix') is FALSE for this architecture. The action expert cross-attends per-layer to the prefix KV-cache at matching indices; a half-depth prefix leaves upper-layer KV unfilled and the expert's upper layers have nothing to attend to (KeyError, or a different model if patched to skip). So zero-shot half-depth is not 'graceful degradation' — it is a different forward graph requiring at minimum a lockstep expert truncation, which (i) changes the action head, undermining the clean 'backbone-only' story, and (ii) almost certainly needs the LoRA the proposal lists as optional, making it the MAIN path. Second: the dispersion gate costs K extra full-depth forwards per decision, which can erase the depth savings unless lagged — turning the headline Pareto win into a wash. Third: DySL-VLA already published the LIBERO adaptive-layer-skip Pareto, so a positive result risks reading as incremental.
anno.effort_note: NOT a 2-hour pilot as scoped, and NOT 'training optional'. Realistic minimum: (1) implement lockstep depth truncation of BOTH prefix and expert with a consistent KV-cache (the cross-attn coupling makes this the hard 1-2 day engineering step, not a config flag); (2) verify forward runs at depth 8/12 without KeyError; (3) zero-shot eval on LIBERO-Spatial 20 eps x 3 depths (~1-2 GPU-h). Adaptive run + perturbation test adds ~2 GPU-h. Honest estimate: 1-2 engineering days + ~6-10 GPU-h, matching the proposal's own 'weeks' tag, NOT the 2-hour budget. Cheapest derisking first step: after fixing the KV coupling, just measure static success at num_vlm_layers={8,12,16} zero-shot — if 8/12 collapse, the savings ceiling is bounded before any gating work.

title: Joint Compute Controller: a single dispersion signal allocates across three axes (steps x depth x horizon)
lenses: SCALING-REGIME lens: COMPUTE ALLOCATION — accuracy/success vs FLOPs/latency under adaptive attention or multi-rate inference. The deliverable is a Pareto curve (success-rate vs mean per-step FLOPs/latency), not a single operating point. Grounded in the real SmolVLA substrate at /srv/data/users/anhar/codes/phosphobot/sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py: per-chunk cost = ONE heavy prefix VLM forward (num_vlm_layers=16, KV-cached) + num_steps=10 cheap expert denoise calls reusing that cache; chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 sets replan (heavy-forward) frequency; raw_dispersion() over K sampled chunks is the ready uncertainty signal (conformal_active/uncertainty.py). All knobs are config-settable per call; clean LIBERO success is the natural y-axis, mean FLOPs/latency the x-axis.
primitive: P2 (bottom-up adaptability <-> top-down optimality reconciled at the meso level) + P3 (adaptive compute) + P1 (the meso clock owns the allocation). Dispersion is the single reconciliation variable that converts perceptual surprise into a coordinated compute budget.
fundamental_method_change: Inserts a meso controller between observation and SmolVLAFlowMatching.sample_actions / select_action that overrides config.num_steps, the executed VLM depth, and the queue-refill horizon together each step. It restructures the entire inference loop's compute schedule (three fundamental knobs at once) under one decision variable, the multi-scopic compute controller that no VLA currently has.
summary: The three cheap SmolVLA knobs (num_steps denoise budget, num_vlm_layers backbone depth, n_action_steps replan horizon) are studied in isolation everywhere in the literature. Build ONE meso-level controller that reads the calibrated flow dispersion and jointly sets all three per situation: low dispersion -> few steps + shallow depth + long horizon (cheap coast); high dispersion -> more steps + full depth + short horizon (expensive deliberation). This operationalizes P2 (bottom-up reactivity meets top-down intention reconciled at the meso clock) as a unified compute-allocation policy, and directly tests the locomotion paper's ~70%-compute-reduction claim in manipulation. Deliverable: a single success-vs-total-FLOPs Pareto frontier that dominates each one-axis sweep.
hypothesis: Jointly allocating the three knobs from one dispersion signal yields a success-vs-total-FLOPs frontier that strictly dominates the best single-axis adaptive policy (ideas 1-3) and every static config, achieving >=50% mean FLOP reduction at <=2pp clean-success loss on LIBERO Spatial/Object, because the three knobs cut different cost components (denoise vs backbone vs replan) that compound multiplicatively.
mve_libero: Stage on top of ideas 1-3 outputs (reuse their per-knob curves as the comparison frontier). (1) Define 2-3 discrete compute tiers (cheap/medium/expensive) each a (steps,depth,horizon) tuple. (2) A conformal dispersion gate picks the tier per step (tau's calibrated on 1 rollout seed via existing uncertainty.py). (3) Evaluate on LIBERO Spatial+Object (20 eps), plot the joint adaptive points against the union of single-axis curves and static tiers. All inference-time; ~2 GPU-h if depth runs zero-shot.
expected_signal: Joint adaptive frontier wraps above-left of all single-axis curves and static points (Pareto domination). Tier-selection trace shows expensive tier fires only at contact/grasp/insert phases (~20-30% of steps), reproducing the paper's 'compute where information-rich' story. If domination fails, the per-axis interaction analysis is still a publishable negative.
contribution_type: unified multi-axis compute controller + Pareto characterization

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-true, with one caveat. If implemented honestly it does restructure the inference-time compute SCHEDULE of SmolVLA (it overrides num_steps inside sample_actions, governs queue-refill horizon in select_action, and would vary backbone depth per step), so it is more than a passive bolt-on observer module: the meso controller sits in the decision path and changes what compute actually runs. That qualifies as changing the inference method, not training or architecture. HOWEVER, two of the three axes are weak as "fundamental" changes: (1) num_steps is already a single config read at modeling_smolvla.py:844, so varying it is a trivial config override, not a method change; (2) horizon adaptation is just executing fewer queued actions before replanning (select_action queue at modeling_smolvla.py:343-350) — also config-level. The only axis that would force genuine architectural surgery is DEPTH, and that is exactly the axis the proposal cannot do per-call (see smolvla_fit). So the "fundamental" status rests almost entirely on the joint-controller framing rather than on any single deep change. Honest verdict: it changes the inference loop's compute schedule, but the depth axis (the one that would make it architecturally novel) is not actually feasible inference-time on stock SmolVLA, so the realized change is closer to "schedule a couple of config knobs from one signal" than the proposal implies.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: LIBERO-Spatial + LIBERO-Object (proposal's choice), 20 eps/suite is too few for a Pareto claim — use >=50 eps/suite/config with 3 seeds or the frontier is noise. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA at the stock static config (num_steps=10, full depth=16, horizon=50), PLUS the single-axis adaptive curves (the actual comparison the thesis lives or dies on). Metric: success-rate (y) vs mean per-step FLOPs or wall-clock latency (x); the deliverable is a Pareto curve, not a point. POSITIVE = the joint adaptive frontier strictly Pareto-dominates BOTH (a) every static (steps,depth,horizon) tier AND (b) the union of single-axis adaptive curves, with the headline target >=50% mean FLOP cut at <=2pp success loss. REACTIVITY claim needs a perturbation: the proposal's "expensive tier fires at contact/grasp/insert" story is untested without one. Add a perturbation arm: at a random mid-episode step inject a state/visual shock (e.g., a small object-pose nudge or a held-out distractor, or simply delay/swap the observation) and verify the controller switches to the short-horizon+more-steps tier within 1-2 control steps AND recovers success better than the static-cheap config. Without that perturbation the "compute where information-rich" claim is just a post-hoc correlation between dispersion and contact phases, which any uncertainty signal would show. FLOPs must be MEASURED (thop/fvcore or analytic per-component count: 1 prefix VLM forward of D layers + num_steps expert denoise calls), not assumed multiplicative.
anno.smolvla_fit: Components touched, verified against the actual code at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/. (1) num_steps axis: trivially fits — read once at modeling_smolvla.py:844 inside SmolVLAFlowMatching.sample_actions; override per call. Works. (2) horizon axis: fits via the ACTION queue in select_action (lines 343-350) and config.n_action_steps; you can shorten executed horizon to replan sooner, but CANNOT extend beyond chunk_size=50 (baked into att_masks at line 767), so only the "expensive=short horizon" direction is free. Works with that asymmetry. (3) DEPTH axis: DOES NOT FIT per-call. num_vlm_layers is consumed ONCE at construction in smolvlm_with_expert.py:100-103 — it physically slices and DISCARDS text_model.layers[:num_vlm_layers] and ties the expert depth (lm_expert_config.num_hidden_layers = self.num_vlm_layers). forward() loops range(self.num_vlm_layers), a fixed instance attribute, with NO early-exit head and NO per-call depth argument. So per-step depth variation requires either (a) loading multiple model instances at different depths (memory blowup, defeats the compute-saving point), (b) monkeypatching the loop bound AND accepting that a depth-16-trained model truncated to depth-8 produces UNCALIBRATED outputs (the proposal's own "if depth runs zero-shot" hedge — it will likely tank success), or (c) actually adding early-exit + fine-tuning (weeks, no longer inference-only). The dispersion signal DOES help and is fully wired: policy_runner.py:133-142 already samples K chunks via predict_action_chunk with fresh noise and feeds raw_dispersion + the conformal threshold (uncertainty.py). So the controller's INPUT is free; the depth OUTPUT is the broken leg.
prior_work: AC2-VLA (arXiv:2601.19634, 2026): a UNIFIED ROUTER allocating computation across spatial, depth, and temporal dimensions based on robot manipulation state; 1.79x speedup, FLOPs to 29.4% of dense (~70% cut), closed-loop. This is the candidate's exact thesis (one controller, multiple compute axes, manipulation-state-driven, ~70% reduction reproducing the locomotion-paper claim). The candidate's axes (steps/depth/horizon) overlap heavily with AC2-VLA's (depth/spatial/temporal); swapping 'denoise steps' for 'spatial tokens' does not change the structural contribution. STRONGEST overlap — likely a prior-art kill.

SCALE (arXiv:2602.04208, 2026): single-pass adaptive inference that JOINTLY modulates action decoding and visual attention based on the model's OWN PREDICTIVE UNCERTAINTY. This is precisely the candidate's 'one uncertainty signal drives multiple knobs jointly' framing, already published.

Adaptive Action Chunking at inference time (arXiv:2604.04161, 2026): uses action ENTROPY (an uncertainty cue) to set chunk size / replan horizon dynamically, +4% on LIBERO-Long. This is the candidate's single-axis 'horizon' baseline (its ideas 1-3) already done with an uncertainty signal — so even the per-axis baselines the candidate plans to 'stage on top of' are published.

Act, Think or Abstain (arXiv:2603.05147, 2026): complexity-aware adaptive routing of VLA execution (act/think/abstain) by state complexity — same meso-level reactive-vs-deliberate compute reconciliation.

RTC / Leave No Observation Behind (arXiv:2509.23224): real-time correction over VLA action chunks — overlaps the reactive-replan-horizon angle; note SmolVLA already ships an rtc_processor in sample_actions.
anno.so_what: If it worked and were novel, the so-what would be real: a single Pareto frontier dominating per-axis sweeps is a clean, citable deliverable, and porting the locomotion paper's P2/P3 (bottom-up reactivity meets top-down optimality, compute where information-rich) into VLA inference is a legitimately interesting framing. A negative result (axes don't compound, frontier doesn't dominate) is also publishable as a characterization. BUT the so-what is badly undercut by AC2-VLA and SCALE: 'unified multi-axis compute router for VLA driven by manipulation state/uncertainty, ~70% FLOPs' is now the EXISTING headline, not a gap. The remaining defensible contribution is narrow: flow-DISPERSION (not entropy/attention) as the single reconciliation variable, the specific steps x horizon pairing on SmolVLA/LIBERO, and a rigorous per-axis interaction/compounding analysis. That is a workshop-grade increment, not a fundamental-method paper, unless it reframes around something AC2-VLA did NOT do (e.g., conformal CALIBRATION of the tier gate with a coverage guarantee, which is the user's actual asset).
anno.adversarial_weakness: Two-part kill. (1) NOVELTY: AC2-VLA already published the identical structural claim — one unified router, multiple compute axes (incl. depth + temporal), manipulation-state-driven, ~70% FLOP reduction in VLA manipulation. The candidate's only swap is 'denoise-steps + replan-horizon' for 'spatial tokens', and SCALE already published 'one uncertainty signal jointly modulates decoding + attention'. A reviewer will say: this is AC2-VLA's router with a different knob set and a dispersion signal — incremental. (2) FEASIBILITY of the load-bearing axis: the proposal's headline 'three knobs cut DIFFERENT cost components that compound MULTIPLICATIVELY' depends on depth being a real, free axis. It is not — num_vlm_layers is a destructive construction-time slice with no early-exit, so the depth axis is either uncalibrated (truncate zero-shot -> success collapse) or not inference-only (needs fine-tuning -> blows the 2h budget). Strip depth and you have a TWO-axis controller (steps x horizon) — and the compounding is weak there too: both num_steps and replan-horizon ultimately gate the SAME heavy prefix-VLM forward (the expert denoise calls reuse the cached prefix and are cheap; the prefix forward dominates per-chunk cost). Replanning less often (long horizon) already amortizes the prefix; cutting num_steps only trims the cheap expert calls. So the dominant FLOP term (prefix VLM) is mostly controlled by horizon alone, and the multiplicative-compounding hypothesis likely fails — the joint frontier may NOT dominate the horizon-only curve by a meaningful margin. The 'expensive tier fires at contact/grasp' story is also unfalsifiable without the perturbation arm.
anno.effort_note: see above

title: Compute-Optimal Sample-K: the dispersion estimator IS the compute it pays for
lenses: SCALING-REGIME lens: COMPUTE ALLOCATION — accuracy/success vs FLOPs/latency under adaptive attention or multi-rate inference. The deliverable is a Pareto curve (success-rate vs mean per-step FLOPs/latency), not a single operating point. Grounded in the real SmolVLA substrate at /srv/data/users/anhar/codes/phosphobot/sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py: per-chunk cost = ONE heavy prefix VLM forward (num_vlm_layers=16, KV-cached) + num_steps=10 cheap expert denoise calls reusing that cache; chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 sets replan (heavy-forward) frequency; raw_dispersion() over K sampled chunks is the ready uncertainty signal (conformal_active/uncertainty.py). All knobs are config-settable per call; clean LIBERO success is the natural y-axis, mean FLOPs/latency the x-axis.
primitive: P3 (attention = adaptive compute) applied reflexively to the measurement itself: spend sampling density only until the gating decision is resolved. This is the strength-feedback loop closed on the estimator's own cost.
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the fixed-K dispersion computation in conformal_active/policy_runner.py (the `for _ in range(n_action_samples)` loop) and uncertainty.py raw_dispersion with a sequential/early-stopping estimator that shares the prefix KV-cache across samples (each extra sample is one denoise solve, not a full forward). This changes the uncertainty-quantification primitive feeding the whole adaptive-inference stack, not a peripheral add-on.
summary: Every dispersion-gated scheme above must SAMPLE K action chunks (K extra denoise solves) to estimate self-disagreement, but the harness fixes K=8 (config n_action_samples). Under the scaling lens this is itself a compute-allocation question with a twist: the measurement consumes the budget it is trying to save. Make K adaptive and SEQUENTIAL: draw samples one at a time, stop as soon as the running dispersion estimate's confidence interval is on the right side of the conformal threshold (a sequential-test / racing strategy). This changes the uncertainty estimator from a fixed-K ensemble into a budget-aware sequential probe, and yields the meta-Pareto: decision-accuracy (does it gate correctly vs K=8 ground truth) vs mean-K. Critical because it determines whether ANY dispersion-gated controller (ideas 1-4) is net-positive on FLOPs.
hypothesis: Because most timesteps are confidently low- or high-dispersion, a sequential racing estimator will reach the same gate decision as fixed-K=8 in a mean of 2-3 samples (>60% sample reduction) with <5% decision-flip rate, making dispersion-gated inference (ideas 1-4) net FLOP-positive even after accounting for measurement cost, on LIBERO Spatial/Object.
mve_libero: Pure offline + 1 short rollout set, very cheap. (1) Collect ~500 frames of K=8 action-chunk samples on LIBERO Spatial via existing policy_runner.episode_signals(compute_dispersion=True). (2) Treat K=8 dispersion as ground-truth gate; simulate sequential stopping rules (fixed budget vs Hoeffding/SPRT-style) and measure decision-flip rate vs mean-K offline. (3) Validate the best rule in one live rollout (20 eps) measuring true wall-clock/FLOP delta. Plot decision-accuracy vs mean-K.
expected_signal: A knee in the decision-accuracy-vs-mean-K curve at low K (2-3), proving the gate is cheap to compute; and a positive net-FLOP accounting when folded into idea 2/4. Negative-but-load-bearing result: if mean-K must be >=6 for reliable gating, it shows dispersion-gated control is NOT compute-favorable for SmolVLA, a result that reframes the entire adaptive-inference premise.
contribution_type: estimator redesign + meta-Pareto (measurement-cost accounting), mostly offline

anno.fundamental_change_justification: This is mostly an estimator/measurement redesign, not a change to a core VLA method (architecture, action representation, training objective, or the policy's own forward pass). The SmolVLA forward, flow-matching head, tokenizer, and action chunk are all left intact. What changes is the WRAPPER loop that calls sample_actions K times (policy_runner.py lines 138-141 / config n_action_samples) — replacing a fixed-K for-loop with a sequential stop. That is the definition of a bolt-on to the uncertainty pipeline. The candidate's strongest claim to fundamentality is the KV-cache-sharing refactor ("each extra sample = one denoise solve, not a full forward"), and I VERIFIED this is architecturally enabled: sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:830-843) does ONE prefix VLM forward with fill_kv_cache=True, then num_steps=10 denoise_step calls that take past_key_values as an argument (line 856,907). So K samples sharing one prefix cache is a genuine inference-path change to SmolVLA's sampling routine. BUT (a) the current code does NOT do this — it calls policy.reset()+predict_action_chunk() K times = K full prefix forwards; (b) that cache-sharing optimization is independent of and separable from the sequential-K idea; (c) even with it, you are reorganizing inference plumbing, not the policy method. Honest verdict: FALSE as the headline "fundamental method change," but it is a legitimate, useful inference-efficiency contribution that is more than a trivial concat. The candidate over-claims fundamentality; flag it as estimator-plus-inference-plumbing, not architecture.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Offline-dominant and genuinely cheap (the candidate's main strength). Concrete: (1) Suite = LIBERO Spatial (+ Object as a second distribution). Metric A (offline, primary) = decision-flip rate: run the existing episode_signals(compute_dispersion=True) with n_action_samples=8 but persist the FULL (K,T,A) per-frame chunk arrays (the harness today only keeps the mean at policy_runner.py:143, so a small change is needed to dump raw samples). Then offline-simulate sequential stopping rules (fixed-budget, Hoeffding/empirical-Bernstein CI, beta-binomial/SPRT-style) and plot decision-accuracy vs mean-K. title: Does the 50-step open-loop chunk straddle the moment a LIBERO rollout goes wrong? A within-chunk failure-onset autopsy that turns the chunk boundary into a dispersion-gated commit gate
lenses: DIAGNOSTIC lens: a question nobody asked whose ANSWER MATTERS EITHER WAY, framed as a fundamental method change to a named SmolVLA component, verifiable on LIBERO+SmolVLA in <=2 GPU-hr per pilot. Grounded in the real substrate: lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot (so select_action / sample_actions / the rollout loop are patchable); SmolVLA chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50 (FULLY open-loop 50-step chunk, backbone re-prefill only when the ACTION queue empties via _check_get_actions_condition), num_steps=10 flow integration steps; the harness already samples K action chunks and computes per-frame flow-head dispersion (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion, policy_runner.py predict_action_chunk loop); eval via lerobot-eval on libero_spatial/object/goal/10.
primitive: P5 (Affordance-Effectivity-Fit interrupt: a fast pathway that preempts the ongoing motor plan) + P1 (meso clock made event-driven rather than fixed-rate)
fundamental_method_change: Replaces SmolVLA's inference-loop commit condition: PolicyClass._check_get_actions_condition / the n_action_steps queue-drain rule in select_action (modeling_smolvla.py) -- from 'queue empty' (fixed 50-step open-loop) to 'queue empty OR per-step dispersion > calibrated tau'. This is a structural change to how many steps of a chunk are committed, not a bolt-on monitor.
summary: SmolVLA executes a FULL 50-step chunk open-loop (n_action_steps=chunk_size=50) and only re-prefills the backbone when the queue empties. The unasked diagnostic question: WHEN within a chunk do LIBERO failures actually become irreversible -- early (so the policy is already committed before it could ever react) or late (so a mid-chunk replan would have caught it)? Instrument every rollout step with the harness's K-sample flow-head dispersion, log the step index at which the eventual-failure trajectory first diverges from the eventual-success manifold (via a privileged success/failure label per episode), and measure the lag between a dispersion spike and the point-of-no-return. The mechanism that the diagnostic motivates: replace the fixed queue-empty commit condition (_check_get_actions_condition) with a dispersion-gated commit -- the queue is allowed to drain to 50 only while dispersion stays below a conformally-calibrated threshold; on a spike it commits a SHORT prefix and re-prefills early.
hypothesis: On LIBERO failure episodes, flow-head dispersion rises >=1 calibrated threshold-unit several control steps BEFORE the trajectory becomes unrecoverable; therefore a dispersion-gated early commit/re-prefill recovers a measurable fraction of those failures (or, if the diagnostic shows spikes occur AFTER the point-of-no-return, it proves reactivity cannot help SmolVLA on LIBERO -- a publishable negative).
mve_libero: Eval-only pilot (no retrain): patch select_action in the editable lerobot source to (a) log per-step dispersion (reuse raw_dispersion over K=4 chunks) and a privileged per-episode success label from lerobot-eval, then (b) add the dispersion-gated commit. Run libero_spatial + libero_goal with stock smolvla_base, ~40 episodes each, baseline (fixed 50) vs gated. Compute: failure-onset step histogram, spike-to-point-of-no-return lag, and Delta success. Fits in <=2 GPU-hr (eval-only, K=4).
expected_signal: A failure-onset histogram with a clear mode, a signed spike-lead (steps the dispersion spike precedes the divergence), and a success delta (gated minus fixed). EITHER outcome publishes: positive lead => reactivity is recoverable and the gate helps; non-positive lead => SmolVLA on LIBERO fails before it can know, killing the 'add a reactive loop' agenda for this regime.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: The gated-commit half genuinely alters a core inference method: it replaces `_check_get_actions_condition` (verified at modeling_smolvla.py:352-353, currently `return len(self._queues[ACTION]) == 0`) and the queue-drain rule in `select_action` (lines 324-350) so the open-loop horizon becomes data-dependent (drain to 50 only while dispersion < tau, else commit a short prefix and re-prefill). That is a structural change to how many steps of a chunk are committed and when the backbone re-prefills — not a passive monitor bolted alongside. CAVEAT: the FIRST half of the proposal (instrument every step, log failure-onset histogram, measure spike-to-point-of-no-return lag) is purely diagnostic and changes nothing — it is a measurement harness, not a method change. So the candidate is two stapled things: a non-method-changing autopsy plus a method-changing gate. Only the gate satisfies the mandate; the writeup should not let the diagnostic borrow the gate's credit. Also note: a naive 'gate' that just shortens the open-loop horizon and re-prefills with FRESH noise is close to a one-line config change (lower n_action_steps adaptively); to be a real, defensible method change it must couple to SmolVLA's own RTC inpainting path (re-prefill conditioned on the executed prefix), otherwise reviewers will call it a thresholded early-stop heuristic.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_spatial + libero_goal (the harness already wraps lerobot-eval with --env.type=libero, evaluate.py confirmed). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA smolvla_base with the stock fixed 50-step open-loop commit (n_action_steps=50, rtc disabled). Treatment = dispersion-gated commit. Primary metric = pc_success delta (aggregated.pc_success from eval_info.json, already parsed). Secondary = mean control steps to first re-prefill, and the failure-onset histogram. This is the SAME family of intervention (partial-chunk execution + early prefix-conditioned re-prefill). The candidate's gate is differentiable only as 'event-driven RTC trigger via dispersion' rather than fixed-horizon RTC — a meaningfully smaller delta than the writeup implies, and the baseline MUST include RTC-on, not just fixed-50.

Sentinel / STAC — Agia et al., 'Unpacking Failure Modes of Generative Policies: Runtime Monitoring of Consistency and Progress', CoRL 2024 (arXiv:2410.04640). Already monitors TEMPORAL CONSISTENCY of action-chunk distributions (self-disagreement) to flag erratic failures. The candidate's dispersion signal is essentially STAC's statistical temporal action consistency; novelty is only in using it to GATE commits rather than to raise an alarm.

'Can We Detect Failures Without Failure Data? Uncertainty-Aware Runtime Failure Detection for Imitation Learning Policies' (arXiv:2503.08558) — directly uses policy uncertainty for runtime failure detection on manipulation; overlaps the autopsy half.

'Failure Prediction at Runtime for Generative Robot Policies' (arXiv:2510.09459) — trajectory-to-outcome failure predictor with detection-time metric; this IS the failure-onset-timing question the autopsy poses, already studied.

Open-Loop Planning, Closed-Loop Verification: Speculative Verification for VLA (arXiv:2604.02965) — a verifier monitors during chunk execution and triggers early replanning when trajectory becomes inconsistent; nearly identical mechanism to the dispersion-gated early re-prefill.

anno.so_what: The diagnostic question (does dispersion spike BEFORE or AFTER the point of no return) is genuinely interesting and IS publishable either way IF measured cleanly — a non-positive lead would be a useful negative result killing the 'add a reactive loop to SmolVLA' agenda for LIBERO. That negative-result framing is the candidate's strongest asset and is well matched to the user's existing 'Unreliable by Default' reliability paper. BUT the affirmative mechanism (the gate) lands in a crowded field where RTC, Sentinel, speculative verification, and adaptive-horizon chunking already occupy the space, so a positive gate result is low-novelty unless the dispersion-vs-RTC-vs-fixed comparison itself is the contribution.

Compounding this: (a) on UNPERTURBED LIBERO an early-commit gate tests 'shorter horizon helps', which has nothing to do with reactivity/AEF — without a named perturbation (latency throttle or visual perturbation) the P5-interrupt framing is unsupported; (b) the baseline as written (fixed-50) is a strawman because the codebase already has RTC, the legitimate strong baseline; (c) the user's own data shows +-9pp seed variance, so any single-seed Delta-success is noise; (d) K-sample online dispersion at every step quietly breaks the '<=2 GPU-hr eval-only' budget. Net: it can become a clean negative-result paper, but the affirmative gate as a 'fundamental contribution' is squeezed between RTC and Sentinel.
anno.effort_note: Days. Patch is hours; the cost is online per-step dispersion plumbing, the point-of-no-return proxy, a perturbation arm, multi-seed runs vs ~9pp variance, and an RTC-on baseline. Scope-cut: ship the autopsy as the negative/diagnostic headline, gate as one confirmatory pilot.

title: Is flow-head dispersion just hidden ground-truth-error in disguise? A calibration autopsy that re-purposes the flow-integration count num_steps as a dispersion sensor instead of a fixed compute budget
lenses: DIAGNOSTIC lens: a question nobody asked whose ANSWER MATTERS EITHER WAY, framed as a fundamental method change to a named SmolVLA component, verifiable on LIBERO+SmolVLA in <=2 GPU-hr per pilot. Grounded in the real substrate: lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot (so select_action / sample_actions / the rollout loop are patchable); SmolVLA chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50 (FULLY open-loop 50-step chunk, backbone re-prefill only when the ACTION queue empties via _check_get_actions_condition), num_steps=10 flow integration steps; the harness already samples K action chunks and computes per-frame flow-head dispersion (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion, policy_runner.py predict_action_chunk loop); eval via lerobot-eval on libero_spatial/object/goal/10.
primitive: P3 (attention = adaptive compute allocation: spend integration density where the signal is information-rich) + diagnostic on P5's trigger validity
fundamental_method_change: Changes SmolVLA's flow-matching action-expert sampler (Model.sample_actions in modeling_smolvla.py): the fixed num_steps Euler integration loop (dt=-1/num_steps, 10 steps) becomes a per-frame adaptive integrator whose step count is set by measured dispersion calibration. This rewrites the action-expert inference, not a wrapper.
summary: Everyone (AAC, AutoHorizon, DiG-Flow, this harness) ASSUMES flow-head self-disagreement is a usable uncertainty signal, but nobody on SmolVLA has asked the prior diagnostic: is K-sample dispersion actually CALIBRATED to instantaneous action error on LIBERO, or is it dominated by the multimodality of the flow prior (so it spikes at benign forks, not at mistakes)? And critically, dispersion depends on num_steps (10 integration steps) -- few steps = under-integrated noise inflates dispersion; many steps = the samples collapse and dispersion vanishes. The diagnostic: sweep num_steps in {2,4,10,20} and K, and measure the reliability-diagram correlation between dispersion and privileged per-step action error (||policy_action - LIBERO bddl-replay action||). The mechanism: make num_steps PER-STEP ADAPTIVE -- integrate more flow steps only where the dispersion-vs-error calibration is informative, fewer where the prior is flat -- turning a fixed integration budget into a dispersion-driven adaptive-compute schedule.
hypothesis: Dispersion's correlation with true per-step action error is non-monotonic in num_steps and peaks at an intermediate count; an adaptive-num_steps sampler matches fixed-10-step success at materially lower mean flow-FLOPs (toward the paper's ~70% compute-reduction claim) -- OR dispersion is uncorrelated with error at every num_steps, which invalidates dispersion-as-trigger for SmolVLA (a result that re-frames the whole 2026 dispersion-gating literature on this substrate).
mve_libero: Eval-only. In the editable sample_actions, expose num_steps as a runtime arg and log dispersion at each setting alongside a privileged per-step action error from the LIBERO demo replay. Run libero_object (~40 eps) sweeping num_steps in {2,4,10,20}; build reliability diagrams; then run the adaptive sampler vs fixed-10 for success + mean-FLOPs. <=2 GPU-hr (no training; flow steps are the only added cost and K can be 2-4).
expected_signal: (1) A calibration curve: Spearman(dispersion, true error) as a function of num_steps. (2) Adaptive-vs-fixed: success delta and mean flow-FLOPs reduction. A flat/zero calibration at all num_steps is the high-value negative (dispersion is prior-multimodality, not error).

anno.fundamental_change_justification: The mechanism half genuinely edits a core VLA inference method, not a wrapper. The target is VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions in .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py (lines 812-881): the fixed Euler loop `num_steps = self.config.num_steps; dt = -1/num_steps; for step in range(num_steps): x_t = x_t + dt*v_t` is rewritten so step count is set per-frame by a measured signal. That is the action-expert sampler itself, on the path that feeds select_action -> predict_action_chunk -> the closed-loop rollout, so a change here alters what the policy actually executes. TWO HONESTY CAVEATS: (1) the DIAGNOSTIC half (sweep num_steps in {2,4,10,20}, log dispersion vs error, build reliability diagrams) is eval-only instrumentation and is NOT a method change by itself; (2) 'expose num_steps as a runtime arg' is already trivially available via self.config.num_steps, so merely sweeping it is a config knob. The fundamental-change credit rests ENTIRELY on the adaptive per-frame integrator actually replacing the fixed loop and changing rollout behavior; if the project stops at the reliability-diagram autopsy, it collapses to a measurement study and is_fundamental_change is effectively FALSE.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_object first (~40 eps, fits 2 GPU-hr), extend to spatial/goal if time. The idea conflates TWO measurements on TWO code paths; name both. (A) CALIBRATION AUTOPSY on the teacher-forced replay path = conformal_active/policy_runner.py episode_signals (loads LIBERO demo frames via LeRobotDataset, already samples K chunks at lines 133-143): at each demo frame compute K-sample dispersion AND privileged error = ||mean_predicted_action - demo_action|| (demo action is in the batch). Sweep num_steps {2,4,10,20}, K {2,4}. Metric: Spearman(dispersion, demo-deviation) per num_steps + reliability diagram. CAVEAT TO STATE: demo-deviation is NOT closed-loop mistake, so low correlation is ambiguous. (B) ADAPTIVE-vs-FIXED on the closed-loop success path = conformal_active/evaluate.py -> lerobot-eval subprocess (NO ground-truth action there): baseline = vanilla SmolVLA fixed num_steps=10; treatment = adaptive sampler. POSITIVE = adaptive matches fixed-10 pc_success within paired noise at materially lower mean flow-NFEs (count denoise_step calls). REACTIVITY: the idea has NO perturbation so its reactivity claim is unverifiable; to test, inject a mid-episode visual perturbation (camera-obs dropout/occlusion or held-out distractor) and check dispersion/step-count rises at perturbed frames vs matched control. Without it, drop reactivity language. NEGATIVE-result POSITIVE = flat Spearman (~0) at every num_steps with tight CIs across >=2 suites.
anno.smolvla_fit: Changes exactly one component: VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (modeling_smolvla.py:812-881), specifically the num_steps Euler loop; denoise_step (883+) is the NFE unit to count. The user's existing dispersion signal helps the AUTOPSY directly (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion lines 31-47; policy_runner.py K-sample loop 133-143 are ready-made), but does NOT port to the adaptive SAMPLER: dispersion there needs K full predict_action_chunk calls (K backbone prefills), far too expensive to run per-frame inside a closed-loop rollout to drive step count. So the adaptive controller must use a cheap in-sampler proxy (per-step velocity-norm change ||v_t - v_{t-1}||, or variance across a small intra-batch noise tile reusing the cached past_key_values) -- which is closer to ProbeFlow's velocity-geometry than to the harness's K-chunk dispersion. This is a real implementation gap the proposal understates.
prior_work: ProbeFlow: Training-Free Adaptive Flow Matching for VLA Models (arXiv 2603.17850) -- STRONGEST overlap: already does training-free dynamic scheduling of flow integration steps for a flow-matching VLA based on trajectory complexity (cosine sim between initial and lookahead velocity vectors). The adaptive-num_steps mechanism is essentially this; differentiation must be SmolVLA substrate + dispersion-vs-velocity-geometry trigger + the calibration autopsy ProbeFlow omits.
AsyncVLA: Asynchronous Flow Matching for VLA (arXiv 2511.14148) -- adaptively schedules timesteps AND regenerates low-confidence action tokens; overlaps the spend-compute-where-uncertain thesis.

Diff-DAgger (arXiv 2410.14868) + Ensemble-DAgger -- already establishes the idea's central NEGATIVE hypothesis for diffusion policies: ensemble/sample disagreement misfires at multimodal forks and is not clean uncertainty. The 'dispersion is prior-multimodality not error' result is a KNOWN phenomenon being re-confirmed on SmolVLA's flow head, not new.

Confidence Calibration in VLA Models (arXiv 2507.17383) -- VLA calibration on 3 LIBERO suites with reliability diagrams/ECE (instruction-rephrasing ensembles). The reliability-diagram-on-LIBERO methodology is not novel; only the specific signal (flow-head K-sample dispersion vs num_steps) is.
DiG-Flow / BeingBeyond (arXiv 2512.01715) -- discrepancy-guided flow matching for robust VLA; treats flow-head discrepancy as a usable signal, the assumption this idea critiques.
anno.so_what: The diagnostic question (is flow-head dispersion calibrated to error or just prior multimodality?) matters for a 2026 literature that gates/triggers on this signal (DiG-Flow, AsyncVLA, the user's own conformal harness); a clean answer either way is publishable-adjacent. BUT it is weakened by prior work: the negative answer is already the known Ensemble-DAgger result, and the positive mechanism is already ProbeFlow. The defensible nugget is narrow: a quantified num_steps-dependence of the dispersion-error relationship on SmolVLA (the non-monotonicity hypothesis) -- nobody has plotted Spearman(dispersion, error) vs integration-step count for a flow-matching VLA. That one curve, if it shows a real peak/collapse, is what to keep; the rest is re-confirmation.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The error label is wrong and lives on the wrong code path. The privileged per-step error exists only in the teacher-forced replay path (policy_runner.episode_signals) where it equals deviation from the demo action -- which is NOT a mistake (a competent policy legitimately departs from the demo at multimodal forks). So a low dispersion-vs-error correlation is exactly what you'd see even if dispersion were a perfect mistake-detector, because the LABEL conflates 'mistake' with 'valid alternative.' Meanwhile success/compute (evaluate.py -> lerobot-eval) is closed-loop with NO ground-truth action, so calibration and success are measured on two different execution regimes and cannot be cross-validated. Net: the autopsy risks a flat/null correlation that is an ARTIFACT of the demo-deviation proxy, indistinguishable from the genuinely-interesting null -- gutting the 'high-value negative.' anno.effort_note: Autopsy alone is ~1 day and fits 2 GPU-hr (instrumentation already exists in policy_runner.py/uncertainty.py; just add a demo-deviation log + num_steps sweep). The adaptive sampler + paired success/NFE eval is the part that earns 'fundamental change' and is the real cost: editing sample_actions, designing a CHEAP in-sampler trigger (not K-chunk dispersion, too expensive per-frame), and running paired lerobot-eval -- realistically 3-5 days, and at ~40 eps the success-parity claim may be within eval noise. Scope cuts: (1) fix the error label (use rollout outcome or a proxy that doesn't assume the demo is the unique correct action); (2) add one perturbation condition or delete the reactivity claim; (3) commit to shipping the adaptive sampler, else downgrade to a measurement paper and stop claiming a fundamental method change.
