fundamental_method_change: Modifies the action expert's attention to the prefix in SmolVLA (denoise_step / the suffix-to-prefix attention in smolvlm_with_expert.py): introduces a dispersion-conditioned gain on language/prefix cross-attention. Changes the representation/inference coupling between backbone and action expert, not a post-hoc filter.
summary: LIBERO-Plus reports VLA policies largely IGNORE language. The unasked SmolVLA-specific diagnostic: at WHICH control steps does the language token stream actually move the action (causal token ablation: zero/shuffle the language tokens mid-rollout and measure the resulting action shift), and does that causal language-sensitivity collapse precisely when flow-head dispersion is high (the moments a top-down intent SHOULD be reasserting itself)? If language influence is near-zero exactly when the policy is uncertain, the top-down channel is dead when it is most needed. The mechanism the diagnostic motivates: a meso reconciliation gate inside the action expert -- when bottom-up dispersion is high, UP-WEIGHT the cross-attention to language/prefix tokens (re-inject top-down intent) instead of letting the action expert coast on memorized state; when dispersion is low, let the committed plan run. This makes the action expert's attention to the prefix dispersion-dependent.
hypothesis: Causal language-sensitivity is low overall AND anti-correlated with dispersion (language matters least when the policy is most uncertain); dispersion-gated up-weighting of prefix attention raises success on instruction-discriminating suites (libero_goal, libero_10) -- OR language-sensitivity is already adequate and the gate does nothing, proving the dead-language story does not transfer to SmolVLA's flow expert.
mve_libero: Pilot 1 (eval-only, diagnostic): patch the forward to support language-token ablation at chosen steps; on libero_goal (~40 eps) measure per-step action-shift under ablation and its correlation with dispersion. Pilot 2 (eval-only): add the dispersion-conditioned prefix-attention gain (a scalar multiplier, no new weights) and re-eval. Both are inference-only; <=2 GPU-hr each. (Optional follow-up LoRA only if the zero-train gate shows signal.)
expected_signal: A per-step causal-language-influence curve and its correlation with dispersion, plus success delta on libero_goal/libero_10 from the gate. Either a live-but-misallocated language channel (gate helps) or a confirmed-dead channel even under stress (gate fails) -- both inform the dual-system field.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: The mechanism does modify a core inference/representation pathway, not a post-hoc filter. The proposed gate scales the action expert's cross-attention to the prefix (specifically the language-token span) by a function of flow-head dispersion, inside forward_cross_attn_layer / eager_attention_forward (smolvlm_with_expert.py) called from denoise_step (modeling_smolvla.py). That changes the backbone<->expert conditioning coupling at every denoising step, which qualifies as an inference-method change. CAVEAT 1: the "no new weights, scalar multiplier" framing is misleading -- the prefix is [image_tokens, language_tokens, state_token] fused into ONE KV cache, with NO separate language cross-attention head. To up-weight language specifically the patch must (a) recover the language span boundaries from embed_prefix and (b) scale only that key-slice of the attention logits/values, threading the span index down into the attention call. That is real surgery across two files, not a one-line gain. CAVEAT 2: if the gate up-weights the ENTIRE prefix (image+language+state) it is trivial but then it is NOT a language re-grounding gate -- it just sharpens conditioning, and the "top-down intent re-injection" story collapses. The fundamental-change credit only holds for the language-span-specific version. The diagnostic half (Pilot 1) is eval-only and is NOT a method change.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Substrate confirmed present: lerobot 0.5.x editable at .deps/lerobot; SmolVLA expert uses eager_attention_forward (logits materialized -> editable); lang_tokens/lang_masks enter at embed_prefix (modeling_smolvla.py:637,693) so zeroing/shuffling language is a clean patch; harness already computes per-frame flow-head dispersion via predict_action_chunk K-sample loop (policy_runner.py:133-143, uncertainty.raw_dispersion). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA (lerobot/smolvla_base) success rate. PILOT 1 (diagnostic, eval-only): on libero_goal and libero_10 (instruction-discriminating suites), at each control step compute action-shift = ||a(full) - a(lang-ablated)|| where ablation = zero lang_masks or shuffle lang_tokens; correlate per-step action-shift with per-step dispersion. POSITIVE = a clear, statistically-tested correlation curve (sign matters either way). PERTURBATION for the reactivity claim is the language ablation itself (the required perturbation); a stronger version adds a mid-rollout distractor-object swap to force dispersion spikes. PILOT 2 (mechanism, eval-only, zero-train): apply dispersion-conditioned gain on language-span cross-attention; POSITIVE = success delta on libero_goal/libero_10 with 95% CI excluding 0 over >=40 eps/suite x >=3 seeds, AND no regression on libero_spatial/object (where layout, not language, drives success). Both pilots fit <=2 GPU-hr (eval-only, num_steps=10). RISK to verifiability: 40 eps x 3 seeds gives wide CIs; a few-pp gate effect may be statistically indistinguishable from noise within budget -- the diagnostic curve (Pilot 1) is the more defensible deliverable.
anno.smolvla_fit: Excellent mechanical fit. Changed components: (1) modeling_smolvla.py embed_prefix -- already separates image/lang/state spans, so language-span indices are recoverable for the gate; (2) denoise_step (line 883) -- entry point that calls the expert per flow step, where dispersion-gain must be passed in; (3) smolvlm_with_expert.py forward_cross_attn_layer (line 286) + eager_attention_forward (line 516) -- where the per-key-token language gain is applied to logits/values. The user's existing dispersion signal helps directly and is the strongest fit element: raw_dispersion (uncertainty.py:31) and the K-sample predict_action_chunk loop (policy_runner.py) already produce the exact scalar the gate consumes -- no new uncertainty machinery needed. Friction: dispersion is currently computed per-FRAME by resampling K full chunks (K extra forward passes), but the gate needs it per-DENOISE-STEP or per-control-step to drive attention; wiring dispersion into the live denoising loop (rather than the offline analysis loop) is non-trivial and adds latency (K-sampling inside the action loop), which partly undercuts SmolVLA's efficiency selling point.
prior_work: AAC -- Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLA (arXiv 2604.04161): uses action entropy/uncertainty as the cue to pick chunk size / replan frequency at inference (high uncertainty -> smaller chunks/replan, low -> commit). This is the SAME uncertainty-gated reactivity half of the candidate's mechanism; strongly overlaps the dispersion-high->reassert / dispersion-low->coast logic.

Stable Language Guidance for VLA -- Residual Semantic Steering (arXiv 2601.04052): names 'modality collapse' where visual priors overwhelm sparse language, audits on LIBERO-Plus/LIBERO-Pro, and isolates language's causal influence by subtracting the visual affordance prior -- i.e. it already does both the diagnostic premise AND a language re-injection mechanism. Closest competitor.

LangForce (ICML 2026, arXiv 2601.15197): dual-branch latent action queries decoupling vision-only vs language-conditioned action distributions to fix the 'Vision Shortcut'; evaluated on LIBERO. A trained architectural fix for the same dead-language problem.

LIBERO-PRO / LIBERO-Plus robustness audits (arXiv 2510.03827): language-deletion/paraphrase ablations show marginal success drop -> the candidate's core diagnostic finding ('VLAs ignore language') is already published; the candidate re-derives a known result.
When Vision Overrides Language (arXiv 2602.17659): evaluates and mitigates counterfactual VLA failures from vision dominating language -- overlaps the diagnostic and mitigation framing.
Seeing to Act, Prompting to Specify (arXiv 2512.11218): Bayesian factorization of vision vs language conditioning in VLA policy -- adjacent decomposition.
anno.so_what: The honest 'so what' is now weak. The diagnostic question ('does SmolVLA read language, and does language-sensitivity collapse when uncertain?') is partly already answered by LIBERO-Plus/PRO and the Stable Language Guidance audit, which show modality collapse on LIBERO. The genuinely-new sliver is narrow: tying language cross-attention gain specifically to the FLOW-HEAD DISPERSION signal of SmolVLA's flow expert (the anti-correlation hypothesis: language matters least exactly when dispersion is highest), which neither AAC (dispersion->chunking, not ->language) nor Stable Language Guidance (steering, not dispersion-gated) does directly. IF the anti-correlation holds, it is a clean, citable mechanistic story about WHEN the top-down channel dies. But the mitigation matters only if the gate moves success, and on LIBERO the layout shortcut means language-sensitive suites are few (goal, partly 10), so even a working gate yields small, contested deltas. Verdict: interesting negative/diagnostic result is plausible; positive 'gate beats baseline' contribution is crowded and likely marginal.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: the result is over-determined to be unsurprising and the field already has it. (1) The diagnostic confirms a published finding (LIBERO-Plus: VLAs ignore language) using a different probe -- reviewers will say 'we knew this.' (2) The mechanism is squeezed between two existing methods: AAC already does uncertainty-gated reactivity, Stable Language Guidance already does causal language re-injection on LIBERO -- the candidate is their intersection, hence incremental, not fundamental. (3) The dispersion anti-correlation hypothesis may be a confound: high dispersion at contact/grasp moments is driven by VISUAL/dynamics ambiguity, not by language relevance, so low language-sensitivity there may be CORRECT (language genuinely irrelevant mid-grasp) rather than a 'dead channel' -- making the up-weight gate actively HARMFUL (re-injecting irrelevant top-down intent during fine motor control). (4) Mechanically, because prefix is a single fused KV with no language head, the 'no new weights' framing breaks; a real language-span gain is two-file surgery and, if it up-weights the whole prefix instead, the language story is gone. (5) Budget: 40 eps x 3 seeds cannot statistically separate a few-pp gate effect from noise.
anno.effort_note: Pilot 1 (diagnostic, eval-only language-ablation + dispersion correlation) is genuinely cheap: ~1-2 days of patching (zero lang_masks at embed_prefix, dual forward, log dispersion already available) and <=2 GPU-hr; this is the part worth doing first because it is decisive and low-cost. Pilot 2 (dispersion-gated language-span cross-attention gain) is the 'weeks' part: requires threading language-span indices from embed_prefix through denoise_step into forward_cross_attn_layer/eager_attention_forward for BOTH cross-attn and the interleaved self-attn layers (self_attn_every_n_layers), plus wiring a live per-step dispersion estimate into the denoising loop (dispersion is currently an offline K-resample, expensive inside the action loop). Recommend: ship Pilot 1 as the contribution; gate Pilot 2 on Pilot 1 showing the anti-correlation. Drop the 'fundamental method change' positioning if only Pilot 1 ships (Pilot 1 is a diagnostic, not a method change).

title: How many of the 50 chunk steps are genuinely worth committing? A chunk-lifespan survival analysis that replaces the fixed n_action_steps with a learned-from-the-data affordance-phase horizon
lenses: DIAGNOSTIC lens: a question nobody asked whose ANSWER MATTERS EITHER WAY, framed as a fundamental method change to a named SmolVLA component, verifiable on LIBERO+SmolVLA in <=2 GPU-hr per pilot. Grounded in the real substrate: lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot (so select_action / sample_actions / the rollout loop are patchable); SmolVLA chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50 (FULLY open-loop 50-step chunk, backbone re-prefill only when the ACTION queue empties via _check_get_actions_condition), num_steps=10 flow integration steps; the harness already samples K action chunks and computes per-frame flow-head dispersion (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion, policy_runner.py predict_action_chunk loop); eval via lerobot-eval on libero_spatial/object/goal/10.
primitive: P4 (affordance-centric, embodiment-relative perception: contact vs transport phase) + P3 (allocate replan compute where the phase demands reactivity) + P6 (body-relative horizon)
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the constant n_action_steps cap in select_action / _check_get_actions_condition (modeling_smolvla.py) with a per-chunk horizon computed from an embodiment-relative phase signal (gripper state + EE speed from observation.state, plus dispersion). Changes the execution-granularity method of the inference loop.
summary: n_action_steps=50 is a single global hyperparameter applied uniformly to free-space transport, approach, and contact/insertion phases. The unasked diagnostic, framed as survival analysis: treat each emitted chunk as a subject and ask at what step its predicted action first DEVIATES beyond a tolerance from what a fresh re-prefill would have produced (a privileged 'oracle replan' computed by re-running the backbone every step on logged observations) -- i.e., the chunk's true useful lifespan. Stratify lifespans by task PHASE (proxy: gripper state transitions + end-effector speed already in observation.state). If contact phases have systematically short lifespans and transport phases long ones, a single global horizon is provably wrong. The mechanism: set the commit horizon per chunk from a cheap phase signal (gripper-state/speed + dispersion), making n_action_steps an affordance-phase-relative quantity rather than a constant.
hypothesis: Chunk useful-lifespan is strongly phase-dependent (short near gripper-state transitions/contact, long in transport); a phase-conditioned horizon matches or beats fixed-50 success while reducing total backbone re-prefills -- OR lifespan is phase-independent on LIBERO, justifying the fixed horizon and bounding how much reactivity granularity can ever buy here.
mve_libero: Diagnostic pilot (eval-only): during stock rollouts on libero_10 (the long-horizon suite, ~30 eps) log, every step, the deviation between the cached chunk action and a fresh-re-prefill action (oracle replan), plus gripper-state/EE-speed; fit lifespan-vs-phase. Mechanism pilot (eval-only): drive via predict_action_chunk + a phase-conditioned FIFO horizon; re-eval. Re-prefilling every step is the cost; cap logged steps to keep <=2 GPU-hr (subsample episodes).
expected_signal: A survival curve of chunk-action-validity stratified by phase, a count of avoidable vs necessary re-prefills, and success/compute deltas for the phase-conditioned horizon vs fixed-50. Either horizon-should-be-adaptive (positive) or fixed-is-fine (negative) -- both pin down the reactivity ceiling on LIBERO.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: The proposed change edits the inference-loop gate that decides when to re-prefill. In the actual source, _check_get_actions_condition is literally `return len(self._queues[ACTION]) == 0`, and the cap is the one-line slice `actions.transpose(0,1)[: self.config.n_action_steps]` in select_action (modeling_smolvla.py L343-353). Making n_action_steps per-chunk replaces a constant with a phase/dispersion-conditioned scalar in that same gate. This changes execution GRANULARITY (a receding-horizon control policy choice) but does NOT touch the trained weights, the flow-matching action expert, sample_actions, the visual tokenizer, or the training objective. The model's forward pass is byte-for-byte identical; only the wrapper deciding how many cached steps to consume changes. By the user's own mandate this is an inference-control add-on / receding-horizon scheduler, not a fundamental method change to VLA architecture/representation/training. It should be flagged as such. The candidate's framing ('changes the execution-granularity method of the inference loop') is honest but is the weakest reading of 'fundamental': it is bolt-on at the deployment layer. The genuinely novel half is the DIAGNOSTIC (survival analysis), which is an instrument, not a method change at all.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_10 (long-horizon, has clear transport vs contact/insertion phases; libero_spatial/object are too short to show phase-dependent lifespan). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA with fixed n_action_steps=50 via stock lerobot-eval (evaluate.py already wraps this). DIAGNOSTIC pilot (offline, fits existing harness): for ~20-30 logged episodes, at each logged frame compute the cached-chunk action vs a fresh re-prefill (predict_action_chunk) action; record L2 deviation, and stratify by phase using gripper-state transitions + EE-speed from observation.state (already extracted as `feature` in policy_runner.EpisodeSignals). Output = a survival curve P(deviation<=tau at step k) per phase. POSITIVE = contact-phase median lifespan is materially shorter than transport-phase (e.g., >2x gap, non-overlapping CIs); NEGATIVE = phase-independent lifespan (justifies fixed-50, bounds reactivity ceiling). MECHANISM pilot needs patching _check_get_actions_condition inside lerobot-eval to refill the queue at a phase/dispersion-conditioned horizon; metric = pc_success delta and avg re-prefill count vs fixed-50. CRITICAL GAP the candidate understates: any 'reactivity' / interrupt claim (P5) is UNTESTABLE on stock LIBERO because nothing perturbs the scene mid-rollout. To claim reactivity you MUST add a named perturbation -- e.g., teleport the target object or add a sensor-occlusion/visual-disturbance at a random step -- and show a short horizon recovers where fixed-50 commits to a stale chunk. Without that perturbation, the mechanism can only show compute (fewer re-prefills) and smoothness, NOT reactivity, so the survival study collapses to a self-consistency-vs-compute tradeoff.
anno.smolvla_fit: Components touched for the mechanism: modeling_smolvla.py select_action / _check_get_actions_condition / the `[: n_action_steps]` slice (L343-353); configuration_smolvla.py confirms chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50, num_steps=10. Diagnostic reuses conformal_active/policy_runner.py episode_signals (predict_action_chunk loop already present) + uncertainty.raw_dispersion. KEY MISMATCH: that dispersion/re-prefill machinery runs OFFLINE over a logged LeRobotDataset via DataLoader (policy_runner.py L100-150), NOT in a closed-loop env rollout. So the 'oracle replan' is computed on the open-loop policy's own logged observations -> it is a SELF-CONSISTENCY signal, not a true counterfactual lifespan. The diagnostic is cheap and fits; the mechanism needs new closed-loop wiring inside lerobot-eval. The existing dispersion signal genuinely helps as the cheap per-frame phase/uncertainty cue.
prior_work: Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLA (arXiv 2604.04161): uses action ENTROPY as the cue to dynamically select chunk size at inference, 'no extra training or architectural changes,' reports 'phase-aware switching' -- this is essentially the candidate's mechanism with entropy instead of dispersion. Strong overlap.

Mixture of Horizons in Action Chunking (arXiv 2511.19433): executes 'the longest action prefix whose disagreement remains below a data-dependent threshold,' tail deferred to replanning -- nearly identical adaptive-horizon-from-disagreement idea.

When to Trust Imagination: Adaptive Action Execution for World Action Models (arXiv 2605.06222): effective chunk size made emergent from future-reality consistency, triggers replan in difficult phases.
Bidirectional Decoding (arXiv 2408.17355): guided test-time sampling over action chunks to balance consistency vs reactivity.

Leave No Observation Behind (arXiv 2509.23224) and Chunk-Boundary Artifact (arXiv 2603.11642): analyze chunk validity / boundary degradation, the closest to the diagnostic half but without a per-phase survival curve vs oracle re-prefill.
anno.so_what: The mechanism's 'so what' is largely pre-empted: adaptive-horizon-from-uncertainty for VLA is published (2604.04161, 2511.19433, 2605.06222), so a phase/dispersion-conditioned horizon that 'matches fixed-50 with fewer re-prefills' would be a confirmatory re-derivation on SmolVLA, not a new contribution. The DIAGNOSTIC half retains a genuine 'so what': a phase-stratified survival curve of chunk-action validity on LIBERO+SmolVLA quantifies HOW MUCH of the fixed-50 horizon is wasted and WHERE, and -- critically -- the NEGATIVE result (lifespan is phase-independent on LIBERO) would bound the reactivity ceiling and explain why fixed-50 is already near-optimal at 87.3% avg, which matters for everyone tuning these knobs. That negative-result value is the strongest reason to run it.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: the 'oracle replan' is not an oracle. Defined as re-prefill on the logged open-loop trajectory, it measures self-consistency (chunk vs fresh prediction on the same observations the open-loop policy itself generated), not ground-truth usefulness -- a chunk action that 'deviates' from a fresh re-prefill may still succeed, and a low-deviation chunk may still fail. So the survival curve answers 'how stable is the flow head across re-samples along its own path,' which is close to just integrating the dispersion signal over the horizon -- a quantity the harness already computes. The phase stratification can therefore be confounded: contact phases have higher dispersion intrinsically, so 'short lifespan in contact' may be tautological with 'high dispersion in contact' rather than evidence the horizon should adapt. Combined with (a) the mechanism being already published and (b) reactivity being untestable without an injected perturbation, the defensible deliverable shrinks to 'dispersion-over-horizon is phase-correlated on LIBERO' -- a modest measurement, not a method.
anno.effort_note: Diagnostic pilot is genuinely <=2 GPU-hr and fits the existing offline harness (reuse policy_runner.episode_signals + raw_dispersion; tag phase from observation.state gripper/EE-speed; subsample libero_10 to ~20 eps). Days. The mechanism pilot is the scope sink: it needs NEW closed-loop wiring to inject a phase-conditioned horizon into select_action inside lerobot-eval (the gate exists at modeling_smolvla.py L343-353 but is not parameterized), plus a perturbation harness (object teleport / occlusion) that does not exist today and is REQUIRED for any reactivity claim. Recommend cutting to: ship the phase-stratified survival/dispersion diagnostic as the core deliverable (honest negative-result candidate); downgrade the horizon mechanism to a confirmatory follow-up citing 2604.04161/2511.19433; attempt the mechanism only if a perturbation is added.

title: Is the disagreement that matters WITHIN a chunk (across flow samples) or BETWEEN consecutive chunks (across re-prefills)? A two-axis disagreement diagnostic that re-defines SmolVLA's replan trigger
lenses: DIAGNOSTIC lens: a question nobody asked whose ANSWER MATTERS EITHER WAY, framed as a fundamental method change to a named SmolVLA component, verifiable on LIBERO+SmolVLA in <=2 GPU-hr per pilot. Grounded in the real substrate: lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot (so select_action / sample_actions / the rollout loop are patchable); SmolVLA chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50 (FULLY open-loop 50-step chunk, backbone re-prefill only when the ACTION queue empties via _check_get_actions_condition), num_steps=10 flow integration steps; the harness already samples K action chunks and computes per-frame flow-head dispersion (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion, policy_runner.py predict_action_chunk loop); eval via lerobot-eval on libero_spatial/object/goal/10.
primitive: P5 (reactive interrupt) + P2 (the meso level reconciles the committed top-down chunk against the fresh bottom-up re-prediction) -- with the diagnostic deciding which disagreement IS the affordance-mismatch signal
fundamental_method_change: Adds a second inference-loop trigger and changes which signal governs re-prefill timing in select_action: from queue-empty (time) to a disagreement axis selected by the diagnostic (intra-chunk dispersion vs inter-chunk overlap inconsistency). Computing inter-chunk disagreement requires running predict_action_chunk on a short overlap each step -- a structural change to the loop's gating, not a monitor that only logs.
summary: The harness measures only ONE kind of self-disagreement: across K flow samples of the SAME chunk (intra-chunk dispersion). There is a second, never-compared axis on this substrate: the disagreement between the overlapping suffix of the CURRENT executing chunk and the prefix of the NEXT re-prefilled chunk (inter-chunk / temporal-consistency disagreement, a Sentinel-style quantity). The unasked diagnostic: which axis better predicts the next-chunk failure on LIBERO -- the policy's epistemic spread (intra) or its temporal inconsistency (inter)? Run a head-to-head predictive-power comparison (AUROC for predicting episode failure, and lead time before the point-of-no-return). The mechanism: replace SmolVLA's purely time-based re-prefill trigger with whichever axis wins -- specifically a trigger that re-prefills EARLY when inter-chunk disagreement on the executed overlap exceeds a calibrated bound (the chunk and its successor contradict each other => the world changed under the open-loop plan).
hypothesis: Inter-chunk overlap disagreement is a stronger and earlier predictor of LIBERO failure than intra-chunk K-sample dispersion (because LIBERO is quasi-static, so flow-sample spread is mostly benign prior multimodality, whereas suffix/prefix contradiction reflects genuine plan invalidation) -- OR intra-chunk dispersion wins, validating the cheaper signal the harness already computes. Either ranking is a reusable result for every flow-matching VLA.
mve_libero: Eval-only. Patch select_action to additionally compute, each step, a cheap fresh predict_action_chunk and the L2 between its leading actions and the cached chunk's corresponding suffix (inter-chunk), while also logging intra-chunk K-sample dispersion. On libero_spatial + libero_object (~40 eps each), compute AUROC(signal -> episode failure) and spike-lead for both axes; then run the winning-axis early-replan trigger vs fixed baseline. The extra per-step chunk prediction is the cost; subsample steps to hold <=2 GPU-hr.
expected_signal: Two AUROC numbers + two lead-time distributions (intra vs inter), and a success delta from the winning trigger. A clean verdict on which self-disagreement axis is the real failure predictor for SmolVLA on LIBERO -- directly actionable for the async replan condition.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-TRUE, with a caveat. The diagnostic half (compute two signals, compare AUROC) is pure monitoring and is NOT a method change. The mechanism half — replacing the queue-empty/time trigger in SmolVLA.select_action / _check_get_actions_condition with a disagreement-gated early re-prefill — IS a genuine change to the inference-loop control structure (which signal governs when the backbone re-runs and the chunk is discarded). That qualifies as changing a core inference method, not a bolt-on logging module. HOWEVER, it is the weaker kind of fundamental change: it alters the gate, not the policy's representation, training objective, or token routing. It does not touch the multi-rate clock structure (P1) the reference paper actually contributes — it only adds one extra event-driven trigger on top of the existing single clock. A reviewer can fairly call it adaptive chunk-horizon / replan-trigger tuning, a known sub-genre, rather than a new architecture.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Eval-only, fits the 2-GPU-hr/pilot budget. Suite: libero_spatial + libero_object (~40 eps each via lerobot-eval --env.type=libero, the path conformal_active/evaluate.py already drives). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA (lerobot/smolvla_base) with the stock open-loop trigger. Phase 1 (diagnostic): patch the deps copy of SmolVLA.select_action to, on a subsampled set of steps, (a) draw K flow samples of the held chunk = intra-chunk dispersion (reuse raw_dispersion from uncertainty.py), and (b) run one extra predict_action_chunk and L2 the overlap of its prefix vs the cached chunk's suffix = inter-chunk disagreement. Log both per step plus terminal success. Metric: AUROC(signal -> episode failure) and spike-lead (#steps before the point-of-no-return) for each axis. Positive = one axis has materially higher AUROC (e.g. >0.65 and >0.05 gap) with non-overlapping bootstrap CIs. Phase 2 (mechanism): early-replan trigger on the winning axis vs fixed baseline; positive = +success delta beyond seed noise (need >=3 seeds; LIBERO single-run noise is large). CRITICAL GAP: reactivity claims need a PERTURBATION. LIBERO default is quasi-static, so an inter-chunk advantage may never fire. Name a concrete perturbation: mid-episode object pose jitter, a forced visual occlusion, or injected camera/inference latency (the deps already model inference_delay in RTC). Without an induced disturbance the inter-chunk axis has nothing to detect and the diagnostic likely returns intra-wins-or-tie, a valid but deflationary result.
anno.smolvla_fit: Concrete and accurate on the substrate. Changes live in the editable deps copy at sim/libero_active/.deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py: select_action (lines ~324-350) and _check_get_actions_condition (line ~352). chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 confirms fully open-loop, so an early trigger is a real behavioral change. The existing dispersion code helps ONLY partially: raw_dispersion (uncertainty.py:31) is reusable as the intra-axis kernel, but the harness currently computes it OFFLINE on teacher-forced dataset batches (policy_runner.py:133-143 via a DataLoader), NOT live in the rollout queue. The idea's claim that the harness already computes per-frame dispersion in the rollout loop / select_action is INACCURATE — that wiring does not exist and must be built. The inter-chunk axis is entirely new code. Cost is real: K intra samples + 1 inter chunk per monitored step = (K+1) extra flow integrations (num_steps=10 each) on top of normal inference; must subsample steps hard to stay under budget.
prior_work: Kim et al. 2025, Real-Time Chunking (Physical Intelligence) — ALREADY IN-TREE at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/rtc/ and wired into SmolVLA (rtc_config). RTC treats overlapping-chunk reconciliation as inpainting with prefix attention; it is the canonical inter-chunk-consistency mechanism. The idea's inter-chunk axis is RTC's premise reframed as a trigger.

Liu et al. 2024/2025, Bidirectional Decoding (BID, arXiv:2408.17355, ICLR 2025) — backward coherence = closeness of the new chunk to the previously selected sequence = exactly the inter-chunk consistency signal, and forward contrast couples within/across chunks. Directly pre-empts the intra-vs-inter framing.

Romer et al. 2025, FIPER: Failure Prediction at Runtime for Generative Robot Policies (arXiv:2510.09459, NeurIPS 2025) — runtime failure alarm from OOD + a novel action-chunk ENTROPY (an intra-chunk spread signal); AUROC-style runtime prediction is its core contribution.

Agia et al. 2024, Unpacking Failure Modes of Generative Policies: Runtime Monitoring of Consistency and Progress (arXiv:2410.04640) — monitors temporal consistency of action-chunk distributions to detect failures; very close to the inter-chunk-disagreement-predicts-failure hypothesis.

PI-VLA AURD and SV-VLA Speculative Verification (2026) — both already implement deviation/consensus-discrepancy-triggered closed-loop replanning of the chunk, i.e. the exact mechanism Phase 2 proposes.

How VLAs Fail Differently (arXiv:2605.28726) and SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for VLA — black-box action-monitoring failure signatures and AUROC comparisons across signals, the diagnostic genre this idea sits in.
anno.so_what: Real but shrinking. The honest contribution is a head-to-head AUROC ranking of intra-chunk flow dispersion vs inter-chunk overlap inconsistency as failure predictors for a FLOW-MATCHING VLA on LIBERO, on the user's exact substrate. If clean, it tells every flow-matching-VLA practitioner which cheap self-signal to gate replanning on, and the answer is reusable either way (the matters-whether-positive-or-negative criterion is met). But the so-what is undercut because (a) the winning mechanism in either case already exists in-tree (RTC for inter, the harness dispersion for intra), so the novel deliverable collapses to which knob to turn, and (b) FIPER/BID/Agia have already studied chunk-entropy and temporal-consistency failure signals, so the question is not actually unasked — it has been answered piecemeal for other policies/benchmarks.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The single strongest objection: on quasi-static LIBERO with a fully open-loop 50-step chunk, the inter-chunk axis has almost nothing to detect — the world does not change under the plan — so the most likely outcome is intra ties or wins and inter contributes nothing, which merely re-derives that the harness's existing dispersion is the signal to use, i.e. a null result dressed as a diagnostic. To make inter meaningful you must inject a perturbation, at which point you are no longer testing vanilla SmolVLA on stock LIBERO but a hand-designed disturbance regime, and the result becomes inter detects the disturbance I injected, which is nearly tautological and not clearly generalizable. Second blow: BID's backward coherence + forward contrast and the in-tree RTC already operationalize the inter-chunk-consistency-vs-reactivity tradeoff, so even the framing is not novel — a reviewer will ask what this adds over BID beyond computing an AUROC on SmolVLA/LIBERO. Third: LIBERO per-config success variance across seeds is large; a Phase-2 success delta from early replanning will be hard to separate from noise in a 2-GPU-hr budget.
anno.effort_note: Phase 1 (diagnostic, eval-only) is days: patch select_action in the deps copy, reuse raw_dispersion, add the inter-chunk L2, log + AUROC. Realistically tight, not 2 hr — the (K+1) extra flow integrations per monitored step and the need for >=3 seeds across two suites push wall-clock up; subsample steps aggressively and possibly drop to one suite for the pilot. Phase 2 (the actual method change: gated early replan + success comparison vs baseline, multi-seed) is the part that risks blowing the budget and getting swamped by LIBERO seed noise. Scope cut: do Phase 1 diagnostic only as the pilot, on libero_spatial with ONE injected, clearly-named perturbation so the inter axis is testable, and treat the trigger as a stretch goal. The reactivity-needs-a-perturbation requirement is the load-bearing scope decision; without it the pilot is a foregone null.

title: Dispersion-Gated AEF Chunk Interrupt: replace the queue-empty refill condition in select_action with a flow-disagreement preemption gate
lenses: ARCHITECTURE-FUSION lens (domain): direct structural graft of multi-scopic locomotion primitives (P1 three-clock, P3 attention=adaptive-compute, P5 AEF interrupt, P2 bottom-up<->top-down meso) onto named SmolVLA components (flow-matching action expert, fixed-num_steps integration loop, uniform SigLIP prefix tokenizer, select_action queue loop). Grounded in lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py and the existing dispersion harness (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion).
primitive: P5 (Affordance-Effectivity-Fit interrupt) + P1 micro clock: a fast reactive pathway that preempts the in-flight chunk, fired by the flow head's self-disagreement (epistemic affordance-mismatch proxy).
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the inference-loop control method: SmolVLA's _check_get_actions_condition (queue-empty refill) becomes a dispersion-thresholded interrupt. This changes the chunk-execution policy itself, not a module bolted alongside it. The action expert, tokenizer, and weights are untouched; the FUNDAMENTAL change is to WHEN/WHY a new chunk is computed (the inference temporal-control method).
summary: SmolVLA's select_action (modeling_smolvla.py L325-353) refills its action queue ONLY when the queue is empty (_check_get_actions_condition returns len==0). This is the canonical fixed open-loop chunk: 50 steps committed blindly. Graft P5 (AEF interrupt) by replacing that condition with a fast micro-clock gate. At every drained step, cheaply re-sample K=4 candidate action chunks from the flow head on the CURRENT observation (reusing the harness's raw_dispersion from uncertainty.py), maintain an EWMA of per-step dispersion, and PREEMPT the remaining open-loop chunk -- forcing an immediate re-decode -- when dispersion crosses a conformally-calibrated threshold (reuse ConformalActionUncertainty + IQTTracker already in-repo). This makes the replan trigger content/affordance-driven instead of queue-exhaustion-driven. The interrupt is a learned/calibrated fast pathway that overrides deliberation -- exactly the locomotion paper's reactivity-preempts-planning primitive.
hypothesis: On LIBERO with a mid-rollout perturbation injected at a fixed step (teleport/displace the target object in the LIBERO env, RobustVLA-style), a dispersion-gated interrupt recovers more episodes than the fixed queue-empty refill, because it re-looks within a few control steps of the disturbance instead of finishing a now-stale 50-step chunk. On clean LIBERO it should match baseline success at the cost of extra re-decodes only where dispersion spikes.
mve_libero: Subclass SmolVLAPolicy, override _check_get_actions_condition / select_action to also re-sample K=4 chunks and trigger refill on dispersion>tau (tau calibrated from 20 clean-rollout dispersion scores via existing ConformalActionUncertainty). Add a small env wrapper that displaces the target object once at step t in LIBERO-Spatial. Run lerobot-eval (evaluate.py path) on 20 episodes x {baseline, interrupt} x {clean, perturbed} on libero_spatial single suite. Metric: post-perturbation success delta + mean re-decodes/episode. ~4 eval configs x 20 eps fits in <=2 GPU-h.
expected_signal: Perturbed-condition success: interrupt > baseline by a measurable margin (target >=8pp); clean-condition success within noise of baseline; re-decode count concentrated right after the injected perturbation (visible as a dispersion spike). Negative result (no recovery gain) is itself publishable: it shows flow-dispersion is too slow/uncalibrated to serve as a reactive trigger on this substrate.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-but-defensible TRUE. The proposal replaces SmolVLA's inference-loop control method: `_check_get_actions_condition` (modeling_smolvla.py L352, literally `len(self._queues[ACTION]) == 0`) and the `select_action` refill logic (L325-353) become a content-driven dispersion-thresholded interrupt. This changes WHEN/WHY a new chunk is decoded — the chunk-execution temporal-control policy — not the weights, tokenizer, or action expert. That is a genuine change to the inference method (one of the four allowed fundamental targets), so it clears the bar that a pure bolt-on side-module would fail. HOWEVER the honest caveat: it is the SOFTEST of the three fundamental-change options in the user's brief. The forward pass, flow integration, and representation are all untouched; what changes is a single scalar gate condition in the execution loop. A skeptical reviewer can fairly call it "an inference-time control heuristic wrapped around an unmodified policy" rather than an architectural change. It is fundamental-to-inference, not fundamental-to-architecture. Flag accordingly: it is NOT a bolt-on module (it overrides core control flow), but it is the least ambitious reading of the mandate.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable, with one essential fix to the proposed protocol. Suite: LIBERO-Spatial single suite (the in-repo evaluate.py wraps lerobot-eval and parses aggregated.pc_success). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLAPolicy with the stock queue-empty refill (n_action_steps=50, num_steps=10, both confirmed in configuration_smolvla.py). Treatment = subclassed policy whose refill condition also fires when EWMA dispersion (raw_dispersion from conformal_active/uncertainty.py, K=4 chunks) exceeds a conformally-calibrated tau (ConformalActionUncertainty + IQTTracker, both in-repo and unit-tested). CRITICAL: a reactivity claim is UNTESTABLE on clean LIBERO, because vanilla SmolVLA already re-decodes every 50 steps and clean episodes give the interrupt nothing stale to recover from — you would only measure extra compute for no benefit. You MUST inject a mid-rollout perturbation: displace/teleport the target object once at a fixed step t (e.g. t=20, before the chunk would naturally refill) via a thin LIBERO env wrapper. Do NOT hand-roll this — LIBERO-plus / LIBERO-PRO (github.com/sylvestf/LIBERO-plus) and the RobustVLA perturbation suite already provide object-displacement perturbations; reuse one for credibility and to preempt "your perturbation is a strawman." Metrics: (1) PRIMARY: post-perturbation success delta (interrupt vs baseline) on the perturbed condition; positive = >=8pp absolute gain with non-overlapping bootstrap CIs over >=20 episodes x >=3 seeds (20 eps single-seed is too noisy for an 8pp claim — pc_success std at n=20 is ~10pp); (2) clean-condition success within noise of baseline (no regression); (3) mean re-decodes/episode and their step-distribution (the dispersion spike should cluster right after t). Compute: 4 configs x 20 eps is feasible in the 2h budget ONLY if the gate is sub-sampled (see weakness); naive per-step K=4 re-sampling will blow the budget.
anno.smolvla_fit: Strong mechanical fit, all claims verified against source. Changes: subclass SmolVLAPolicy, override `_check_get_actions_condition`/`select_action` (modeling_smolvla.py L325-353). The user's existing dispersion signal helps directly and non-trivially: policy_runner.py already samples K chunks via repeated `policy.predict_action_chunk(batch)` with `policy.reset()` between calls and computes per-(step,dim) std — exactly the gate's score function, so the sampling plumbing exists. ConformalActionUncertainty/IQTTracker give a calibrated tau for free. IMPORTANT cost finding the proposal understates: each dispersion sample is a FULL backbone forward + num_steps=10 denoise iterations, and the in-repo path calls `policy.reset()` so there is NO KV-cache reuse across the K samples. A per-drained-step K=4 gate therefore costs ~4 full decodes per check step versus the baseline's ~1 decode per 50 steps — the word "cheaply re-sample" in the summary is wrong; it is expensive. Also unmentioned: LeRobot's SmolVLA already ships an RTC (Real-Time Chunking) path (rtc_config, RTCProcessor, modeling_smolvla.py L257-271, L860) that handles asynchronous chunk switching via inpainting — `select_action` even asserts RTC is disabled. The dispersion gate and RTC are different mechanisms (when-to-replan vs how-to-stitch), but a reviewer will ask why the comparison ignores the repo's own built-in chunk-management feature.
prior_work: Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for VLAs (arXiv:2604.04161) — near-identical thesis: if model uncertainty is high, shrink the executed chunk / replan; if confident, extend. Evaluated on LIBERO-Spatial. This is the closest competitor and largely subsumes the clean-LIBERO half of the idea.

Mixture of Horizons in Action Chunking (arXiv:2511.19433) and the attention-guided execution-horizon line — interprets the model's own confidence (action self-attention) to autonomously decide how far to execute before replanning; same 'replan when internally uncertain' primitive without a perturbation.

When to Trust Imagination / Active Uncertainty-Resolving Decider (arXiv:2605.06222) — explicitly monitors action-consensus disagreement and state-prediction error as the signal to trigger closed-loop replanning; this is the dispersion-as-replan-trigger idea by another name.

Open-Loop Planning, Closed-Loop Verification: Speculative Verification for VLA (arXiv:2604.02965) — executes the longest action prefix whose cross-horizon disagreement stays below a threshold, defers the tail to replanning; mechanically the same gate.

Real-Time Chunking / RTC (pi.website; HF lerobot/rtc docs; arXiv:2509.23224 'Leave No Observation Behind') — the in-repo baseline for reactive asynchronous chunk switching; the dispersion gate must be differentiated from and ideally compared against it.

RobustVLA (arXiv:2511.01331), LIBERO-plus (github.com/sylvestf/LIBERO-plus), LIBERO-PRO (arXiv:2510.03827), Affordance Field Intervention 'escaping memory traps' (arXiv:2512.07472) — ready-made LIBERO perturbation/robustness harnesses; reuse for the perturbation rather than hand-rolling.
anno.so_what: Modest and conditional. The honest contribution is NOT 'we invented uncertainty-triggered replanning' (multiple 2025-2026 papers own that) but a narrow, falsifiable measurement on a specific substrate: does SmolVLA's flow-head self-disagreement (the user's existing dispersion signal) work as a REACTIVE interrupt trigger fast enough to recover from a mid-rollout perturbation, when the policy itself was never trained for reactivity? That has value mainly as a NEGATIVE result: if a calibrated dispersion gate fails to recover (because flow dispersion is too noisy, lags the disturbance, or fires everywhere/nowhere), that tells the field the popular 'disagreement = replan signal' recipe does not transfer to flow-matching VLAs out of the box — useful and publishable as a cautionary finding. A positive result is interesting but heavily pre-empted by the adaptive-chunking literature, so the framing should be 'reactive recovery under perturbation' (which most prior work does NOT test — they test clean-LIBERO horizon adaptation), not 'better chunk scheduling.' The perturbation-recovery angle is the only genuinely differentiable wedge.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The strongest objection is a fork. (1) NOVELTY: 'replan when the action distribution disagrees with itself / when uncertain' is the explicit mechanism of at least four 2025-2026 VLA papers (Adaptive Action Chunking 2604.04161, Mixture of Horizons, Speculative Verification 2604.02965, When to Trust Imagination 2605.06222), several already on LIBERO-Spatial. Reframing it as P5/AEF locomotion borrowing does not change that the gate is the same. The only defensible novelty is the perturbation-recovery evaluation, NOT the method. (2) FEASIBILITY/COST: the proposal calls the K=4 per-step re-sampling 'cheap,' but verified source shows each sample is a full backbone forward + 10 denoise steps with NO KV-cache reuse (policy.reset() between samples). A per-drained-step gate is ~4x more compute than baseline PER STEP, i.e. ~200x per chunk window — it will not fit 4 configs x 20 eps in 2h without sub-sampling the gate (check every N steps, or reuse the prefix KV-cache across the K noises, which the current harness does not do). (3) CONFOUND: a positive perturbed-recovery result could come purely from re-looking-sooner (ANY fixed shorter horizon, e.g. n_action_steps=10, would also recover), so the experiment MUST include a fixed-short-horizon ablation as a second baseline; without it, the dispersion gate's contribution is unidentifiable and a reviewer will reject. (4) TRIGGER VALIDITY: SmolVLA was not trained for reactivity; flow dispersion may not spike at the perturbation at all (it measures sampling-noise self-disagreement, not OOD-detection), so the gate could be a no-op — the very risk the proposal admits, but it is the modal outcome, not the tail.

title: Three-Clock SmolVLA: split the single forward-per-chunk into micro (queue drain) / meso (dispersion-gated chunk re-decode) / macro (prefix re-encode only on intention change)
lenses: ARCHITECTURE-FUSION lens (domain): direct structural graft of multi-scopic locomotion primitives (P1 three-clock, P3 attention=adaptive-compute, P5 AEF interrupt, P2 bottom-up<->top-down meso) onto named SmolVLA components (flow-matching action expert, fixed-num_steps integration loop, uniform SigLIP prefix tokenizer, select_action queue loop). Grounded in lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py and the existing dispersion harness (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion).
primitive: P1 (three independently-clocked loops, micro/meso/macro) with the macro loop gated on intention change -- directly attacks the 'no three-rate VLA exists' gap.
fundamental_method_change: Restructures the inference forward method: the monolithic embed_prefix->denoise loop in sample_actions is decomposed so that prefix re-encoding (macro) and suffix denoising (meso) run on SEPARATE clocks against a persisted past_key_values, rather than always together. This is a method-level change to how/when each half of the network fires -- not an added module.
summary: SmolVLA today does ONE thing per chunk: embed_prefix encodes vision+language+state into past_key_values (sample_actions L830-843), then 10 flow steps emit a 50-step chunk, executed open-loop. That conflates perception re-encoding and action re-decoding into a single clock. Graft P1 (three-clock) by structurally separating them on SmolVLA's OWN cache: (micro) the queue drains at control rate; (meso) re-run only denoise_step over the CACHED prefix KV to refresh the chunk at an intermediate rate without re-encoding images -- cheap, because past_key_values is reused; (macro) re-run the expensive embed_prefix + VLM KV-fill ONLY when a macro trigger fires (sustained high dispersion or a detected subtask/intention change). The meso loop reuses the existing KV cache; the macro loop is the only one paying SigLIP+VLM cost. Each loop has its own rate, matching the locomotion paper's micro/meso/macro decomposition, realized on SmolVLA's actual prefix/suffix cache split.
hypothesis: Refreshing the action chunk via meso-rate denoise_step over a stale-but-cached prefix preserves most clean-LIBERO success while cutting backbone (SigLIP+VLM) forward passes substantially, because in quasi-static LIBERO the visual prefix changes slowly; firing the macro re-encode only on dispersion spikes recovers the cases where the stale prefix is actually wrong. So: large compute reduction at near-iso success, validating the paper's ~70%-compute-reduction claim in manipulation.
mve_libero: Subclass SmolVLAPolicy: persist past_key_values across select_action calls; add a meso path that calls only model.denoise_step (reusing cached KV, fresh noise) every M control steps, and a macro path that calls full embed_prefix+KV-fill only when EWMA dispersion>tau OR every Mmax steps as a safety floor. Instrument prefix-encode counts. Eval on libero_spatial 20 eps x {baseline, 3-clock} measuring success + #prefix-encodes (FLOP proxy). One clean suite, 2 configs, <=2 GPU-h.
expected_signal: 3-clock config: success within ~2-3pp of baseline while prefix-encode count drops >=40-60%; a FLOP-vs-success Pareto point dominating fixed-rate. If success collapses, that quantifies how stale the cached prefix becomes -- a clean negative characterizing the meso/macro rate tradeoff on LIBERO.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Genuinely a method-level change to VLA INFERENCE, not a bolt-on. The proposal restructures the monolithic forward in sample_actions (verified at modeling_smolvla.py L812-881): today embed_prefix + vlm_with_expert.forward(fill_kv_cache=True) (L830-843) and the num_steps denoise loop (L848-876) always fire together per chunk. The candidate persists the returned past_key_values (a plain layer-keyed dict, confirmed in smolvlm_with_expert.py L262-276) ACROSS select_action calls and decouples WHEN the prefix half (macro) vs the suffix-denoise half (meso, denoise_step L883-916 with fill_kv_cache=False) execute, each on its own clock. That is a change to how/when each half of the network fires against a persisted cache — architecture/inference-level. CAVEAT that keeps this from being a slam-dunk "fundamental": LeRobot already ships the same decoupling as a first-class feature (async inference: RobotClient drains a local queue while the server computes the next chunk; actions_per_chunk / chunk_size_threshold). The novel delta over stock async is only the dispersion-GATED macro trigger and the intermediate meso re-decode-over-stale-prefix, so the fundamental-ness rests on the gating policy, which is closer to an inference-control change than a new architecture.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable, but the MVE as written has a measurement flaw that must be fixed first. Suite: libero_spatial, 20 episodes, seed-matched. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLAPolicy. Treatment = ThreeClockSmolVLAPolicy subclass. Metric: aggregated.pc_success (closed-loop, written by lerobot-eval; the harness already shells out to it via evaluate.py L66-99) PLUS a backbone-forward (prefix-encode) counter instrumented inside sample_actions. Positive result = treatment within ~2-3pp of baseline success while prefix-encode count drops materially AND that drop is real headroom (see flaw). THE FLAW: SmolVLA defaults are chunk_size=50, n_action_steps=50, num_steps=10 (configuration_smolvla.py L29-30,63). With n_action_steps=50 the baseline ALREADY does only ONE prefix-encode per 50 control steps — the queue drains 50 actions before _get_action_chunk re-fires (select_action L343-350). So under stock config there is almost NO compute to save; the meso loop adds work. To create headroom the experiment MUST first reduce n_action_steps (e.g. 5-10) so the baseline re-encodes often, THEN show the meso re-decode recovers most of that at lower backbone cost. This config change must be reported as part of the claim, else the "40-60% prefix-encode reduction" is measured against a strawman. REACTIVITY claim needs a named perturbation: the closed-loop LIBERO rollout itself is the perturbation for the dispersion-gated macro trigger (does firing re-encode on dispersion spikes recover success the pure-meso config loses?); for a stronger test, inject a mid-episode visual/object-pose disturbance and check macro fires. Injection point for the subclass: lerobot-eval loads via --policy.path, so you need a registered custom policy type or a monkeypatch import shim — verify the subclass is actually loaded, not silently falling back to stock SmolVLA.
anno.smolvla_fit: Excellent mechanical fit. Exact components touched: (1) modeling_smolvla.py sample_actions L812-881 — split into a macro path (embed_prefix + fill_kv_cache=True, L830-843) and a meso path (denoise_step over persisted past_key_values, L883-916); (2) select_action L325-350 / _check_get_actions_condition L352-353 — add meso/macro clock counters and the gating logic; (3) past_key_values must be stored as instance state across calls (confirmed persistable: layer-keyed dict, smolvlm_with_expert.py L262-276; use_cache defaults True L66). The user's dispersion signal helps DIRECTLY as the macro gate: raw_dispersion (uncertainty.py L31-44, std across K sampled chunks) is exactly the "stale prefix is wrong" detector. BUT a cost subtlety the candidate glosses: computing dispersion requires K denoise passes per evaluation point (policy_runner.py L133-143 currently calls predict_action_chunk K times, each a FULL sample_actions incl. prefix). For the meso loop to be cheap, dispersion must be recomputed using K denoise_step passes over the CACHED prefix (fresh noise, no re-encode) — a change to how dispersion is computed online. That is implementable (the cached prefix is right there) but is extra plumbing the MVE understates.
prior_work: TIDAL: Temporally Interleaved Diffusion and Action Loop for High-Frequency VLA Control (arXiv 2601.14945) — NEAREST PRIOR ART. Splits VLA inference into a low-frequency macro-intent loop (semantic reasoning) and a high-frequency micro-control loop, caching semantic embeddings and interleaving flow-matching integration steps. This is the candidate's two-clock core almost exactly, on a flow VLA.

AC^2-VLA: Action-Context-Aware Adaptive Computation in VLA (arXiv 2601.19634) — a learned router predicts high cache-reuse probability and BYPASSES the expensive multimodal backbone by querying a 'cognition cache'. This is the candidate's dispersion-GATED macro trigger, but with a learned router instead of a dispersion threshold.

DuoCore-FS / Asynchronous Fast-Slow VLA for Whole-Body Manipulation (arXiv 2512.20188) — explicit slow VLM (1-3 Hz) writing bridge embeddings to a buffer + fast action pathway (30 Hz); cross-timescale training to fix the train-inference mismatch. The fast/slow two-clock decomposition with a shared buffer.
FASTER: Rethinking Real-Time Flow VLAs (arXiv 2603.19199) — asynchronous pipeline minimizing time-to-first-action and raising inference frequency for flow/chunking policies.

Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time (arXiv 2604.04161) and AURD/within-chunk-variance replanning — uncertainty/entropy/variance triggers shorter chunks and more frequent replanning; 'when within-chunk variance is high, switch/replan'. This is the candidate's dispersion-gated reactivity, already framed as variance-triggered replanning.

VLA-Cache (arXiv 2502.02175) / AC^2 cache-reuse line / OxyGen (2603.14371) — re-encode only salient/active tokens, reuse cached KV for static tokens; the broad 'reuse the VLM KV cache, recompute selectively' family.

LeRobot async inference (huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/async) — STOCK SmolVLA ALREADY decouples chunk prediction (slow backbone) from execution (queue drain) via RobotClient + chunk_size_threshold. The candidate's micro/macro split largely already exists in the user's own stack.
anno.so_what: Real but crowded. The clean question — "on quasi-static LIBERO, how stale can the cached prefix get before success collapses, and does a cheap dispersion gate recover it?" — is a legitimate, publishable characterization IF framed as an empirical staleness/rate-tradeoff study with the dispersion signal as the gate. A negative result (success collapses fast => LIBERO is less quasi-static than assumed, or the flow head can't correct a stale prefix) is genuinely informative. BUT the headline 'large compute reduction at iso-success, validating the locomotion paper's ~70% claim' is at high risk of being (a) already shown by TIDAL/DuoCore-FS/AC^2-VLA, and (b) trivially true or trivially false depending on n_action_steps. The 'so what' survives only if the contribution is reframed as: dispersion-gated (vs learned-router / fixed-rate / entropy-chunk) macro triggering, head-to-head, using a signal the user already has — i.e. a gating-policy comparison, not 'we invented multi-rate VLA inference'.
anno.adversarial_weakness: The strongest objection is a pincer. (1) NOVELTY: the two-clock cache-reuse core is prior art (TIDAL is nearly identical; AC^2-VLA does the gated-bypass; DuoCore-FS/FASTER do fast-slow), and the 'three-clock micro/meso/macro' framing is mostly relabeling — micro (queue drain) and macro (prefix re-encode) are EXACTLY stock LeRobot async; only the meso re-decode-over-stale-prefix is arguably new, and TIDAL already interleaves flow steps against cached embeddings. (2) MEASUREMENT: with SmolVLA's default n_action_steps=50, the baseline already encodes once per 50 steps, so the advertised 40-60% prefix-encode reduction is measured against a config nobody runs; forcing small n_action_steps to manufacture headroom is reviewer-bait. Worse, on quasi-static LIBERO the cheap meso path may match the baseline simply because re-encoding the near-identical image was never necessary — making the result a property of LIBERO being easy, not of the method. The locomotion paper's 70% claim came from a domain with continuous terrain change; LIBERO's static tabletop may show EITHER trivial savings (prefix never needed refreshing) or trivial collapse, neither of which transfers the locomotion insight.
