title: Dispersion-Adaptive Flow Budget: replace the fixed num_steps=10 integration loop with a per-frame compute-density controller
lenses: ARCHITECTURE-FUSION lens (domain): direct structural graft of multi-scopic locomotion primitives (P1 three-clock, P3 attention=adaptive-compute, P5 AEF interrupt, P2 bottom-up<->top-down meso) onto named SmolVLA components (flow-matching action expert, fixed-num_steps integration loop, uniform SigLIP prefix tokenizer, select_action queue loop). Grounded in lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py and the existing dispersion harness (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion).
primitive: P3 (attention = adaptive compute allocation): the flow-step budget IS the compute-density knob, driven by flow-head dispersion as the strength-feedback signal.
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the flow-integration method: the fixed-num_steps Euler loop becomes a dispersion-conditioned adaptive-step integrator (variable dt schedule per frame). This changes the action-generation algorithm itself, not a wrapper. dt = -1/num_steps becomes a per-frame variable; the loop's termination is uncertainty-driven.
summary: The flow-matching integration loop in sample_actions (L844-876) hard-codes num_steps=10 Euler steps for EVERY observation, regardless of difficulty -- uniform compute in time. Graft P3 (attention = adaptive compute) by making the integration budget a function of the flow head's own self-disagreement: spend MANY denoise_step iterations where dispersion across an initial K-sample probe is high (information-rich / ambiguous affordance), and FEW where it is low (confident). Concretely: take an early cheap dispersion estimate at coarse num_steps, then continue integrating to a fine budget only on high-dispersion frames. This is a strict 'representational/compute density where the scene is uncertain' instantiation on SmolVLA's exact denoising knob, targeting the paper's ~70%-compute-reduction story while keeping the network and weights frozen (training-free, inference-only -- fits the SmolVLA-specific TTA gap).
hypothesis: Most LIBERO frames are easy (low dispersion) and converge with far fewer than 10 flow steps; allocating the saved steps to the few high-dispersion frames yields equal or better success at lower average integration cost. Distinguishes P3 from the temporal-only adaptive-chunking literature (AAC/AutoHorizon set chunk LENGTH; this sets per-frame INTEGRATION DEPTH -- an unclaimed axis with the flow-dispersion signal).
mve_libero: Subclass and override sample_actions: probe dispersion with a coarse pass (e.g. 4 steps, K=4 noises), then if dispersion<tau accept the coarse chunk, else integrate to 10 steps. Calibrate tau from clean rollouts. Eval libero_spatial 20 eps x {fixed-10 baseline, adaptive} logging mean flow-steps/frame + success. Fully training-free; 2 configs, <=2 GPU-h.
expected_signal: Adaptive config: mean flow-steps/frame drops (target ~5-6 vs 10) with success within noise of the fixed-10 baseline; a per-frame histogram showing high-step frames cluster at contact/decision moments. If accuracy drops at fewer steps everywhere, that bounds SmolVLA's flow-step sensitivity -- a useful negative on whether 10 steps is already minimal.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: It genuinely changes a core VLA inference method, not a bolt-on. The target is SmolVLA's action-generation algorithm itself: the fixed Euler loop in VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (verified at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py L844-876, `num_steps = self.config.num_steps` (=10), `dt = -1.0/num_steps`, `for step in range(num_steps): ... x_t = x_t + dt*v_t`). Replacing this with a per-frame, uncertainty-driven variable-step/early-termination integrator alters the ODE solver that produces every action chunk. That is the inference algorithm, satisfying mandate #2. CAVEAT: the specific variant in mve_libero (probe at coarse 4 steps, accept-coarse if dispersion<tau else continue to 10) is a two-tier early-exit gate, closer to an adaptive solver than a wrapper, but a weak instantiation of "compute density" -- it is binary (4 or 10), not a continuous per-frame schedule. The fundamental-change claim holds for the integrator override; it would be stronger as a true variable-dt schedule rather than a 2-bucket gate.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Verifiable but with a harness wrinkle. Closed-loop LIBERO success in this repo runs through `lerobot-eval` as a subprocess (conformal_active/evaluate.py builds `lerobot-eval --policy.path=... --env.type=libero --env.task=libero_spatial --eval.n_episodes=20`), which drives the standard select_action/predict_action_chunk -> sample_actions path. So the override must be patched directly into the editable .deps/lerobot sample_actions (feasible: it is an editable install) or monkeypatched before eval; a flag alone will not do it. Concrete protocol: Suite = libero_spatial, 20 eps. Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA fixed num_steps=10 (shipped default). Metric pair = aggregated.pc_success from eval_info.json AND mean network-function-evaluations per frame (denoise_step calls, INCLUDING probe passes). POSITIVE = success within +/-1 std of fixed-10 while mean NFE/frame drops materially (idea targets ~5-6). Log a per-frame step histogram to test the "high-step frames cluster at contact/decision moments" claim. CRITICAL on framing: the proposal invokes P3 (compute where uncertain) but the title drifts toward P5 (reactive interrupt). There is NO perturbation in the MVE. Any reactivity/AEF-interrupt claim must add a named perturbation (mid-episode object displacement, camera occlusion, or a force nudge in the LIBERO sim) and show the budget spikes at the perturbed frames vs fixed-10. Without a perturbation the only defensible claim is compute efficiency. Budget: 2-3 configs x 20 eps libero_spatial is well under 2 GPU-h on the A6000.
anno.smolvla_fit: Tight component fit. Changes exactly VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions (integration loop L844-876) in modeling_smolvla.py; config knob num_steps (default 10, configuration_smolvla.py L63). The existing dispersion signal PARTIALLY helps but is more obstacle than asset. raw_dispersion (conformal_active/uncertainty.py) measures self-disagreement across K *full* predict_action_chunk samples -- each a complete prefix-encode + 10-step integrate (policy_runner.py L133-143 loops K times with policy.reset()). Wrong granularity and wrong cost: it is dispersion of *finished* chunks, not of a *coarse-budget* chunk, and costs K full forwards. The MVE needs a NEW cheap signal: dispersion across K noises at the *coarse* step count (4 steps), reusing the cached prefix KV (sample_actions builds past_key_values once). Implementable from the same code, but not the existing harness signal as-is. Cost accounting matters: K coarse probe passes are not free; K=4 at 4 steps is ~16 NFE before any refinement, which can eat the savings vs a flat 10. The honest knob may be K=2 probe or a velocity-norm proxy rather than full dispersion.
prior_work: ProbeFlow: Training-Free Adaptive Flow Matching for VLA Models (arXiv 2603.17850) -- NEAR-IDENTICAL DIRECT COMPETITOR. Training-free, dynamically schedules flow-matching integration steps on a VLA flow head, evaluated on LIBERO (and MetaWorld 14.8x speedup N=50->2.6), explicitly allocates a denser schedule to navigate semantic bottlenecks. Uses cosine similarity between initial and lookahead velocity vectors as the difficulty probe instead of action dispersion. Covers ~90% of the candidate pitch (training-free + per-frame adaptive flow steps + VLA + LIBERO + bottleneck density). The candidate's only surviving differentiator is the probe signal (flow-head sample dispersion vs velocity-cosine geometry) -- a thin, possibly negative, delta.

AdaFlow: Imitation Learning with Variance-Adaptive Flow-Based Policies (arXiv 2402.04292) -- established variance-adaptive ODE step-size for flow policies: a learned per-state variance scalar sets solver step size; low variance -> near one-step. Covers the 'adaptive integration depth driven by uncertainty' axis the candidate calls unclaimed. NOT VLA/training-free, which is the candidate's wedge against it.

D3P: Dynamic Denoising Diffusion Policy via RL (arXiv 2508.06804) -- a state-aware adaptor allocates per-action denoising steps (3 easy, 6-8 grasp/align), jointly trained with RL. Directly demonstrates the 'more steps at contact/decision moments' histogram claim listed as the candidate's expected signal. Differentiator: D3P trains the adaptor; candidate is training-free.

Entropy-Adaptive Diffusion Policy Optimization (ICCV 2025) and token-level early-stopping for diffusion LMs (arXiv 2602.11133) -- both formalize hyperparameter-free dynamic early-stopping of the denoising process via alignment/convergence signals, overlapping the 'stop early when confident' mechanism.
anno.so_what: Moderate-but-shrinking. The honest contribution is NOT the mechanism (adaptive flow steps is now crowded: ProbeFlow, AdaFlow, D3P) but two narrower things: (1) a clean empirical bound on SmolVLA-specific flow-step sensitivity -- does LIBERO success actually need 10 Euler steps, or is the shipped default already wasteful/already minimal? A useful, citable measurement for SmolVLA users regardless of sign. (2) Whether the dispersion signal the user already built is a better or worse per-frame difficulty probe than ProbeFlow's velocity-cosine geometry. If dispersion wins, a real (if incremental) result; if it loses, an honest negative that justifies the velocity-geometry choice. The grand multi-scopic 70%-compute / attention=adaptive-compute (P3) framing is mostly post-hoc narrative on what is mechanically the existing adaptive-flow-steps literature; reviewers will see through it.
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: ProbeFlow already published the exact thesis (training-free, per-frame adaptive flow-integration steps, VLA flow head, LIBERO, bottleneck-dense scheduling). The candidate's delta collapses to "use sample-dispersion instead of velocity-cosine as the probe," and that delta likely LOSES on its own efficiency metric: dispersion needs K full coarse forward passes (the existing harness pays K x predict_action_chunk per frame), whereas ProbeFlow's velocity-cosine reuses vectors already computed inside the single ongoing integration at near-zero marginal cost. So the candidate's probe is strictly more expensive than the incumbent's probe while chasing the same savings -- the compute-reduction headline may not materialize once probe cost is counted honestly. Second-order: a binary 4-or-10 gate (the MVE) is not "compute density," it is two buckets; the continuous P3 version is harder and closer to AdaFlow. The idea risks being "ProbeFlow with a worse probe."
anno.effort_note: Implementation is genuinely days and fits the 2-GPU-h pilot: override sample_actions in the editable .deps/lerobot (coarse-probe + early-exit), expose num_steps/tau, run configs on libero_spatial through evaluate.py/lerobot-eval, log NFE/frame. The expensive part is DEFENSIBILITY, not compute. Mandatory scope cuts before running: (1) Read ProbeFlow (arXiv 2603.17850) fully and reframe as "is dispersion a better difficulty probe than velocity-geometry for SmolVLA," with ProbeFlow's velocity-cosine schedule as a REQUIRED baseline alongside fixed-10 -- three arms, not two. (2) Count probe FLOPs honestly in the efficiency metric (NFE including probe) or the result misleads. (3) Either drop the reactivity/AEF framing (keep pure P3 efficiency) OR add a named LIBERO perturbation to back it. (4) Prefer a continuous variable-dt schedule over the 4-or-10 binary gate to escape "two buckets." Without these cuts it is a near-duplicate; with them it is a small honest probe-comparison contribution.

title: Affordance-Density Token Routing in embed_prefix: replace uniform SigLIP patch tokens with a dispersion-saliency-pruned prefix
lenses: ARCHITECTURE-FUSION lens (domain): direct structural graft of multi-scopic locomotion primitives (P1 three-clock, P3 attention=adaptive-compute, P5 AEF interrupt, P2 bottom-up<->top-down meso) onto named SmolVLA components (flow-matching action expert, fixed-num_steps integration loop, uniform SigLIP prefix tokenizer, select_action queue loop). Grounded in lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py and the existing dispersion harness (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion).
primitive: P3 (dynamic-density attention) fused with P4 (affordance-centric, action-relevant perception): density flows to what the scene affords the policy's actions.
fundamental_method_change: Replaces the tokenizer/perception front-end method: embed_prefix's fixed full-patch image embedding becomes a saliency-routed variable-density token set entering the VLM KV cache. This changes the representation SmolVLA reasons over -- a fundamental perception-method change, not a downstream filter on outputs.
summary: embed_prefix (L637-729) feeds ALL SigLIP image patches into the VLM KV cache at uniform density -- the documented LIBERO failure mode (position-memorized uniform patches collapse under object displacement). Graft P3+P4 (attention-density + affordance-centric perception) by routing token density: derive a per-patch action-relevance saliency from how much each image patch influences the flow head's action output (a cheap occlusion/attention-gradient probe correlated with action-chunk dispersion), then keep dense tokens on high-saliency (action-affording) regions and merge/drop background tokens BEFORE the VLM KV-fill. This replaces SmolVLA's uniform tokenization with a body/affordance-relative density map -- the visual-tokenization branch of the fundamental-change mandate. Unlike VLA-Pruner (attention magnitude) or ROI-Foveated (gripper geometry), the retention criterion here is derived from the policy's own action-disagreement, tying perception density to affordance-effectivity fit.
hypothesis: Concentrating token density on action-relevant regions and sparsifying background (a) reduces VLM prefix cost and (b) is more robust to object displacement than uniform patches, because the kept tokens encode affordance rather than absolute layout. So on LIBERO-PRO-style object-repositioning, the routed prefix narrows the displacement collapse gap at lower token count.
mve_libero: Training-free start: subclass, in embed_prefix compute per-patch saliency via a single-pass gradient-of-action-norm w.r.t. patch embeddings (or a cheap drop-one probe on a patch grid), keep top-p patches, mean-merge the rest, then proceed to KV-fill. Eval libero_spatial 20 eps clean + a displaced-object variant x {uniform baseline, routed} logging success + #kept tokens. 4 configs, <=2 GPU-h. (If gradient probe too slow, approximate saliency from SigLIP attention rollout.)
expected_signal: Routed prefix: clean success within ~3pp of baseline at notably fewer tokens; on the displaced-object variant, smaller success drop than uniform (target: recover part of the displacement gap). Negative result -- routing hurts or doesn't help robustness -- still answers whether SmolVLA's fragility is tokenization-density-driven or weight-driven.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: Borderline-true, with a heavy caveat. It does alter the perception front-end: embed_prefix (L637-729 of modeling_smolvla.py) currently concatenates the full fixed set of SigLIP/connector image embeddings into the VLM KV-fill at uniform density; routing to a variable-density token set changes the representation the VLM and the flow-matching action expert attend over. That is a representation/inference-method change, not a filter on action outputs, so it clears the bar more legitimately than an output-side add-on. HOWEVER, the proposed training-free MVE (subclass embed_prefix, compute per-patch saliency, keep top-p, mean-merge the rest, proceed to KV-fill) is operationally a token-pruning module spliced into one method - the exact 'plug-and-play' shape that the prior-art pruning papers self-describe. So it is a fundamental-change in kind but a bolt-on in implementation; it should be flagged as such. It only becomes unambiguously fundamental if the routing is learned/differentiable and trained jointly, which the MVE is not.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Clean-success half is verifiable cheaply; the robustness claim is NOT cheaply verifiable on the current harness. Concrete clean sketch: suite = libero_spatial (and optionally libero_object). Metric = pc_success from lerobot-eval's eval_info.json (the harness already parses overall/aggregated.pc_success in conformal_active/evaluate.py), plus mean #kept image tokens logged from the subclassed embed_prefix. Baseline = vanilla lerobot/smolvla_base (uniform 64-token prefix). Positive = routed prefix stays within ~3pp of baseline pc_success at a meaningfully lower kept-token count. The reactivity/displacement claim requires a perturbation that does NOT exist here: eval is fully delegated to the lerobot-eval CLI with no per-step env hook, so a 'displaced-object variant' must be newly built (override LIBERO init states / object qpos, LIBERO-PRO style) - that is its own engineering task, not a 2-GPU-h drop-in. Without that perturbation, the headline robustness hypothesis is unfalsifiable. CRITICAL substrate problem: SmolVLA already compresses each frame to 64 tokens via PixelShuffle, so the token-budget headroom (and thus the efficiency win that motivates pruning) is far smaller than on OpenVLA-class models with 256+ tokens; the 'notably fewer tokens' positive criterion is weak here.
anno.smolvla_fit: Touch points are correctly identified: SmolVLAFlowMatching.embed_prefix in .deps/lerobot/.../smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py (L637-729) builds the prefix; embed_image in smolvlm_with_expert.py (L191) returns the connector-resampled image_hidden_states whose tokens would be routed. A subclass override is feasible. BUT the claimed tie to the user's dispersion signal does NOT hold: conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion and policy_runner.py compute a per-FRAME scalar (std across K full action chunks, K calls to predict_action_chunk) - there is no per-PATCH attribution. To get per-patch saliency you need a different mechanism: gradient-of-action-norm w.r.t. patch embeddings (an extra backward pass per frame, awkward under the flow-matching sampler and torch.compile at L611, and not what dispersion measures) or SigLIP attention rollout (which is precisely VLA-Pruner's mechanism). So the dispersion harness gives no leverage on the saliency map; the 'affordance-effectivity-fit via the policy's own disagreement' framing is aspirational, not implemented by the existing signal.
prior_work: VLA-Pruner: Temporal-Aware Dual-Level Visual Token Pruning (arXiv:2511.16449, Nov 2025) - the closest work: dual-objective retention using ACTION-DECODE attention for execution-relevant token importance + temporal smoothing, evaluated on LIBERO with token-budget sweeps; this is essentially the candidate's claimed novelty ('retention from the policy's own action signal') already published, plug-and-play and training-free.
SpecPrune-VLA (arXiv:2509.05614, Sep 2025) - action-aware self-speculative visual token pruning for VLA acceleration.
Action-aware Dynamic Pruning for Efficient VLA Manipulation (arXiv:2509.22093, Sep 2025) - action-conditioned dynamic token pruning.

The Better You Learn, The Smarter You Prune: Differentiable Token Pruning for VLAs (arXiv:2509.12594, Sep 2025) - the LEARNED-routing version, which is the only way this idea would be genuinely fundamental rather than a filter.
SemanticVLA (arXiv:2511.10518) and VLA-IAP (arXiv:2603.22991) and DTP (arXiv:2601.16065) - semantic/interaction-aligned and distracting-token pruning for VLA, all 2025-2026.
anno.so_what: The intended payoff (cheaper + displacement-robust perception by spending token density on action-affording regions) is a legitimate question, and a negative result ('SmolVLA's documented uniform-patch fragility is weight-driven, not tokenization-density-driven') would be informative. BUT the so-what is badly undercut on this exact substrate: SmolVLA is already aggressively token-compressed (64/frame via PixelShuffle + half-depth VLM), so the efficiency lever is small and the most-cited motivation (large prefill cost) barely applies. The robustness angle is the only part that could matter, and it is precisely the part the harness cannot test today. So the contribution risks being 'a known pruning technique re-derived on a model that least needs pruning.'
anno.adversarial_weakness: Strongest objection: the central novelty claim is already published. VLA-Pruner (Nov 2025) defines token retention via action-decode attention - the same 'tie perception density to action relevance' thesis - tested on LIBERO with budget sweeps. The candidate's only escape (saliency derived from the action-CHUNK DISPERSION signal) is not actually realizable from the existing harness, which produces a per-frame scalar, not a per-patch map; the practical fallback the proposal itself names ('approximate saliency from SigLIP attention rollout') collapses the method onto exactly the prior art. Compounding this: on SmolVLA's 64-token prefix there is little to prune, so even a clean win is marginal and the headline robustness test needs infrastructure (object-displacement env hook) that doesn't exist. Net: novelty is largely pre-empted and the cheap-MVE story does not match the differentiator.

title: Meso Bottom-Up<->Top-Down Handshake: feed a dispersion summary back into embed_suffix so reactivity revises the action prior mid-denoise
lenses: ARCHITECTURE-FUSION lens (domain): direct structural graft of multi-scopic locomotion primitives (P1 three-clock, P3 attention=adaptive-compute, P5 AEF interrupt, P2 bottom-up<->top-down meso) onto named SmolVLA components (flow-matching action expert, fixed-num_steps integration loop, uniform SigLIP prefix tokenizer, select_action queue loop). Grounded in lerobot 0.5.2 editable source at .deps/lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/modeling_smolvla.py and the existing dispersion harness (conformal_active/uncertainty.py raw_dispersion).
primitive: P2 (bottom-up<->top-down reconciled at the meso level): dispersion as the meso reconciliation variable fused into the action-expert conditioning.
fundamental_method_change: Changes the conditioning method of the action expert: embed_suffix gains a bottom-up conditioning input, making the suffix denoiser's input a function of the policy's own reactive state -- a fundamental change to the action-expert's input contract and (if fine-tuned) its training objective. The cross-attention bridge stops being purely one-directional.
summary: SmolVLA's data path is strictly top-down: prefix (language intent + vision) conditions the suffix action expert one-directionally via cross-attention; nothing flows bottom-up. embed_suffix (L731-772) builds the action+timestep tokens with no channel for the policy's own reactive/uncertainty state. Graft P2 (bottom-up adaptability meets top-down optimality at the meso level) by adding a bottom-up channel at the suffix: compute a compact running dispersion/affordance-mismatch summary from the previous chunk and inject it as an additional conditioning token (concatenated into the action_time_emb fusion) so that, when bottom-up reactivity is high, the action prior is biased toward fresh-observation correction, and when low it trusts the top-down committed plan. The meso (action-expert) level becomes the explicit reconciliation point of perception-up and intention-down, instead of a pass-through.
hypothesis: Letting the action expert see its own recent self-disagreement lets it modulate between sticky (commit top-down plan) and reactive (re-ground on fresh obs) behavior, improving recovery after a disturbance without a separate interrupt module -- because the reconciliation is internal to the meso loop. Tests whether a tiny bottom-up channel beats purely top-down conditioning on perturbed LIBERO.
mve_libero: Cheapest verifiable form: add one scalar->embedding bottom-up token (prev-chunk dispersion) into embed_suffix's fusion, LoRA-fine-tune only the action_time_mlp + the new projection on the existing LIBERO buffer (reuse the repo's LoRA train.py path, steps_per_round-scale), then eval libero_spatial 20 eps clean + perturbed vs the base policy. Training is the small LoRA already used in-repo; fits <=2 GPU-h if restricted to one suite and a short LoRA run.
expected_signal: Bottom-up-conditioned LoRA: >= base on clean libero_spatial and better post-perturbation recovery; ablating the bottom-up token to zero should erase the perturbation gain (clean isolation of the channel's effect). A null result cleanly shows top-down conditioning already saturates what the action expert can use.

anno.fundamental_change_justification: It genuinely changes a core VLA method, not a bolt-on. The action expert's input contract is altered: embed_suffix (modeling_smolvla.py:731-772) currently fuses only action_emb + sinusoidal time_emb via action_time_mlp_in/out. Adding a learned projection of a bottom-up reactive scalar into action_time_emb makes the flow-matching denoiser's velocity field a function of the policy's own recent self-disagreement. Because denoise_step (L883-916) calls embed_suffix at every one of the num_steps=10 integration steps, the bottom-up signal modulates the entire integration trajectory, and if fine-tuned it changes the training objective (the v_t regression target is now conditioned on a new input). The cross-attention prefix->suffix bridge stops being strictly one-directional. That is a representation+conditioning change to the action expert, which qualifies. CAVEAT: the magnitude is small (one extra token / one extra projection), so it sits near the boundary between fundamental and add-on; an adversarial reviewer could argue it is a thin conditioning add-on rather than an architectural rethink.
anno.libero_verification_sketch: Suite: libero_spatial (cheapest, the harness already targets it; evaluate.py shells to lerobot-eval --env.type=libero, parsing aggregated.pc_success). Baseline = vanilla SmolVLA LoRA fine-tuned on the SAME fixed buffer with the bottom-up token forced to zero (the natural ablation IS the baseline). Metric = pc_success over 20 episodes, plus a separate post-perturbation recovery rate. CRITICAL GAP the proposal underspecifies: the reactivity claim REQUIRES a perturbation, but there is NO perturbation infrastructure in this repo (grep for perturb/disturbance/apply_force returns nothing; eval is a black-box lerobot-eval call). A clean perturbation must be ADDED before this is verifiable, e.g. (a) at chunk boundaries, apply a one-shot object-pose or robot-state jitter via the LIBERO sim's set/reset-state hook, or (b) use the existing LIBERO-Plus object-layout/lighting perturbation suites as the perturbed condition. Positive result = bottom-up >= zero-token baseline on clean libero_spatial AND strictly better post-perturbation recovery, with the gain erased when the token is zeroed (clean isolation). Without a perturbation harness, the headline claim cannot be tested and only the clean-suite no-regression check is runnable in the 2h budget.
anno.smolvla_fit: Changes exactly: embed_suffix (modeling_smolvla.py:731) gains a new input + a new nn.Linear projecting the bottom-up scalar into expert_hidden_size, added into action_time_emb before/after action_time_mlp; and the inference loop sample_actions/denoise_step (L812-916) must thread a per-chunk dispersion value through. The user's existing dispersion signal HELPS conceptually but DOES NOT plug in cleanly: raw_dispersion (uncertainty.py:31) is computed OFFLINE at episode/demo-selection time by re-sampling K=8 chunks per frame in policy_runner.py (L133-143), NOT inside the live select_action path. To use prev-chunk dispersion online you must sample K chunks per inference call (K extra forward passes per chunk) or accept a one-chunk-stale scalar — and with chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 the signal updates only ONCE PER 50 ENV STEPS, making it a coarse meso-rate variable, not a reactive one. DEEPER PROBLEM: training (forward, L774, via lerobot-train on a static shuffled buffer) is teacher-forced on independent frames with NO previous chunk, so there is no natural training value for the bottom-up token; it must be faked (zeroed, or a recomputed proxy), creating a train/inference distribution mismatch that LoRA on the small E1 buffer is unlikely to bridge. The repo's LoRA target regex (modeling_smolvla.py:498) covers action_time_mlp_in/out but the NEW projection is a fresh module needing modules_to_save / explicit trainability, not a standard LoRA adapter.
prior_work: AsyncVLA (arXiv:2511.14148, Nov 2025): a confidence rater estimates per-action-token confidence in a flow-matching VLA and FEEDS IT BACK to selectively re-denoise low-confidence tokens with self-correction; evaluated on LIBERO/Bridge/Fractal. This is the same bottom-up-uncertainty-into-action-generation thesis with a stronger, per-token learned mechanism. Closest competitor; the candidate is a coarser cross-chunk scalar variant.

DiG-Flow: Discrepancy-Guided Flow Matching for Robust VLA (arXiv:2512.01715, Dec 2025): uses a discrepancy/disagreement signal to guide the flow-matching trajectory for robustness — directly overlaps the 'dispersion guides denoising' core.

Leave No Observation Behind / A2C2 (arXiv:2509.23224): asynchronous action-chunk correction that injects the latest observation into a predicted chunk to restore closed-loop responsiveness — competes on the 'reactive correction over open-loop chunks' claim.
Speculative Verification / Deviation-based Replanning for VLA (arXiv:2604.02965): replans only when execution deviates — the meso 'commit-vs-replan' gating idea, via a different mechanism.

SmolVLA paper (arXiv:2506.01844) + RTC processor already in this repo's modeling_smolvla.py (rtc_processor, L860-879): real-time chunking already addresses mid-chunk staleness, partially preempting the 'reactive over chunks' motivation.
anno.so_what: If positive: shows a tiny, training-cheap bottom-up channel (reusing a free uncertainty signal the policy already produces) lets the action expert self-modulate between committing to the top-down plan and re-grounding on fresh observation, improving disturbance recovery WITHOUT a separate interrupt module or a learned confidence rater. If negative: cleanly demonstrates that top-down prefix conditioning already saturates what the flow head can use, i.e. a scalar bottom-up summary adds nothing — a genuinely informative null given the live competitors. Either way the result matters. BUT the 'so what' is materially weakened by AsyncVLA/DiG-Flow already occupying this conceptual slot with richer mechanisms; the contribution narrows to 'minimal/cheap meso-rate variant' rather than 'first to feed uncertainty back into the action expert.'
anno.adversarial_weakness: The single strongest objection: there is no honest training signal for the bottom-up token. lerobot-train processes shuffled, independent, teacher-forced frames with no 'previous chunk,' so during fine-tuning the dispersion input must be zeroed or faked — meaning the model never learns to USE it; at inference you then feed a real, distributionally-novel scalar the LoRA weights have never been trained against. The likely outcome is the projection learns to ignore the token (gradient pressure toward zero) and the clean-vs-perturbed gain is noise, indistinguishable from the zero-token baseline. Compounding this: with chunk_size=n_action_steps=50 the signal is one-chunk stale and updates 50x slower than the env, so it is not actually 'reactive' in the P5 sense — it is a slow meso scalar mislabeled as reactivity. Secondary: no perturbation harness exists, so the headline claim is untestable as scoped; and computing live dispersion costs K extra forwards per chunk, straining the 2h budget once you add a perturbation eval condition.
